angleSummary: 16 active modules across 5 rooms. All module handlers are real (graduated from stubs). Partner is feature-flagged off by default but ships with hardcoded fake signals. Care Circle and Garden are design-only (zero code). WidgetKit infrastructure is written but no Swift extension target exists. Language setting has no UI caller. Key gaps: onboarding missing, language picker missing, goals progress arc is a fake, pets species hardcoded to guinea_pig for all users, pets coregulation log never written.

mergedFindings.title: Partner module broadcasts hardcoded SAMPLE_SIGNALS (mood=low, energy=high) to real Supabase partner_snapshots — bilateral sharing is a data fixture
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/modules/partner/repo.ts:42 — `const SAMPLE_SIGNALS: RawSignals = { mood: 'low', energy: 'high', cyclePhase: null, focus: 'deep' }` used at line 84 in buildMySnapshot(), which is called by pairWithCode, setConsent, goDarkToday, clearDark, publish. Supabase migration 20260602103016_partner_bilateral_sync.sql creates live partner_snapshots table. features.ts:22 defaults partner to false. The module is absent from the dump-classify.ts MODULES array so no brain dump can route to it.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any user who enables the partner flag (or any future release that flips it on) will have their partner see fabricated emotional state (always low mood, high energy, no cycle data, deep focus) regardless of what they actually logged. The consent/privacy filtering layer is real but the data flowing through it is a hardcoded fixture. This is a privacy/trust violation if either user believes the data is real.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Keep feature flag at default:false. Add a blocking code comment in repo.ts TODO(signals) making clear the flag must not be flipped until SAMPLE_SIGNALS is replaced with live reads from sleepRepo.latestSleep, cycleRepo.current, moodEvents.latestEnergyOrMood, and habits repos. The interpret() and consent-filtering layers are already correct — only the signal source needs to change.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. The fix is wiring 4 existing live repos into buildMySnapshot(). No schema change needed. The flag stays false until wiring is complete.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test: buildMySnapshot() with a known mood log returns that mood value, not the hardcoded constant. Integration test: a mood-logged user's snapshot in partner_snapshots differs from SAMPLE_SIGNALS.

mergedFindings.title: Language setting (EN/ES/TR) has no UI caller — all users are silently locked to English
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/settings/appLang.ts exports setAppLang() and getAppLang(). Exhaustive grep of apps/native/src/ for 'setAppLang' (excluding the module file itself and test files) returns zero results. useAppLang() is consumed by DumpScreen, TodayNoticings, and brain/copy.ts — so the language mechanism works when the value is set — but no UI component ever calls setAppLang(). The SettingsScreen in navigation/Router.tsx contains only account email and sign-out. Default is hardcoded to 'en'.
mergedFindings.userImpact: The app ships with EN+ES+TR promise. Spanish and Turkish speakers receive English copy with no in-app path to change it. Crisis copy (crisisCopy.ts) and brain noticings are genuinely trilingual but unreachable in the correct language. This is a promise-vs-reality gap that surfaces immediately in user testing with non-English speakers.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a 3-chip language selector (English / Español / Türkçe) to SettingsScreen calling setAppLang(). Approximately 15-20 lines, no data model changes.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Trivially low. Purely additive UI change.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that selecting the 'tr' chip persists via store and that useAppLang() re-renders downstream consumers correctly.

mergedFindings.title: Goals progress arc always renders a fake 50% fill — no progress field exists in storage
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/modules/goals/GoalsBox.tsx:491-508 — comment: 'goals don't have a progress field in storage yet, so we render an indeterminate ring (a quiet half-fill)'. Code: `const pct = goal.latestProgress ? 0.5 : null` — any goal with any progress note always shows exactly 50%. goals_registry schema (migrate.ts) has no progress column. The GoalArc SVG renders 135° fill with no relation to actual completion.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Every goal with any logged activity shows a 50% progress ring. A goal with one note and a goal with fifty notes are visually identical. The UI implies a metric that does not exist, which erodes trust. Users who log progress cannot see actual advancement.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Option A (lowest risk): remove the arc from FocusHero entirely and render editorial text only. ~10-line removal, no schema migration. Option B: add a progress_pct int column to goals storage and a log_progress router action — requires migration.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for option A. Medium for option B (requires migration + router action).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: GoalsBox snapshot test: goal with 3 progress notes does not render pct=0.5. FocusHero test: renders null arc when no progress_pct is stored.

mergedFindings.title: No onboarding flow — new users land on brain-dump input with zero context, empty modules, and Serra's personal pet names in the nav
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/main.tsx — Gate() renders SignedIn > Router with no first-run check. Router.tsx index route is DumpScreen with no new-user detection. grep for 'firstRun|onboarding|welcome' in apps/native/src/ returns 0 UI results. moduleManifest.ts:39 hardcodes hint 'tontin + pinpon' (Serra's cats' names) visible to every user in the Pets nav hint. No language picker on first launch. No consent screen.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A new beta user (friend, tester) sees a blank text area with zero explanation of what Ollie is, what to type, or how modules work. Pets nav hint literally shows a developer's personal cat names to every user — a product bug, not a personalization. Modules like Cycle, Medication, and Habits show cold-state empty messages with no setup guidance.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Immediate (1 line): change moduleManifest.ts:39 Pets hint from 'tontin + pinpon' to 'your pets'. Medium-term: add a minimal 2-screen first-run flow gated by a store flag (what is Ollie + language picker). Add consent banner (DEPLOY_TODO §7).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for the manifest fix. Medium effort for full onboarding (sprint-level).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Snapshot test confirming moduleManifest contains no personal names. First-launch flag test: store key 'settings.firstLaunchDone' missing renders onboarding screen.

mergedFindings.title: Pets species hardcoded to guinea_pig for ALL pets — cats, dogs, and birds receive wrong care cadences and clinically incorrect watcher cards
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/modules/pets/bridge.ts:47-51 — `const DEFAULT_SPECIES = 'guinea_pig'` with comment 'BUILD GAP'. No species registry exists in the pets module. No onboarding flow collects species. SPECIES_PROFILES[guinea_pig] is applied to all AI-generated care-gap watchers regardless of actual pet type.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A user with a cat or dog receives vitamin_c scurvy warnings and guinea_pig feeding cadences in their watcher cards. This is clinically wrong care advice presented with the authority of AI-generated noticings.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Surface a species selector in PetsBox add/edit flow. Until then, add a disclaimer that pet care is calibrated for guinea pigs only, or default to a neutral 'unknown' species profile that omits species-specific care advice.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — requires schema change (species column) + onboarding UI + routing the species into the care-gap detector.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that a cat-species pet does NOT receive vitamin_c care gap cards. Test that SPECIES_PROFILES is only applied when species is confirmed.

mergedFindings.title: Pets coregulation_log is never written — emotional-bond detector always runs on empty input and never fires
mergedFindings.evidence: packages/orchestrator/src/pets.ts:255-256 reads pets.coregulation_log from store. pets/bridge.ts:192-195 reads but never writes coregulation_log. modules/dump/bridge.ts does not write coregulation_log. Exhaustive grep of apps/native/src/ for `store.set('pets', 'coregulation_log'` returns zero results. The coregulation detector exists in orchestrator logic but has no live data source.
mergedFindings.userImpact: The 'emotional bond' and 'coregulation' Layer-2 watcher cards never fire for any user. This is a silent feature gap — the feature appears complete in the orchestrator layer but the app never feeds it data.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a prominent TODO at the top of pets/bridge.ts documenting the gap. The actual fix requires wiring the dump mood/pet-mention co-occurrence path into coregulation_log writes — a separate sprint.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for documenting. Medium complexity to wire.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Integration test: after a dump containing 'cuddled with [pet name] while anxious', coregulation_log has one entry in the store.

mergedFindings.title: Mood module is review-only with no direct input UI — screen is a dead end with no entry affordance
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/modules/mood/MoodBox.tsx:1-11 — comment: 'The AI router still does the writing; this is a review + cleanup surface.' HealthRoom.tsx:264 labels energy as 'READ-ONLY — mood folded in (no chevron, no drill)' and intentionally suppresses drill-through. No direct mood input widget exists on the MoodBox screen. Other modules (ChoresBox.tsx:211/477, MedicationBox.tsx:754) have a dump-bar hint at bottom; MoodBox has none.

There is no quick 'tap to log mood' affordance and no hint that mood is captured via the brain dump. The module appears broken rather than intentionally read-only.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a dump-bar hint at the bottom of MoodBox (same 5-line pattern as ChoresBox.tsx:211/477) explaining that mood is captured via the brain dump.

mergedFindings.testsToAdd: MoodBox renders a 'mood is captured via the dump' hint when no events exist today.

mergedFindings.title: Finance module is dump-input only — no manual transaction entry UI — sparse data makes Layer-2 detectors fire on noise
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/modules/finance/FinanceBox.tsx — grep for 'add.*transaction|manual.*entry|input|form|text.*field|amount.*field' returns 0 results. All finance data comes exclusively from brain dump routing. Bank integration (Plaid/TrueLayer) was explicitly removed (commit 47a6fa6). No CSV import. The doom-buying detector and cycle×spend detector in bridge.ts require data density that dump-only entry makes unrealistic.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Users who don't naturally narrate purchases will see a permanently empty finance box. Bills and subscriptions must be entered via dump. Layer-2 finance detectors may fire false noticings on sparse data, reducing trust in the AI observations.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a simple amount+merchant+date quick-add sheet inside FinanceBox.tsx calling transactions.add() directly. The dump path continues as the primary route. No schema changes required.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — requires new UI surface.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that a manual add via the quick-add sheet lands in the SQLite table and appears in FinanceBox on next render.

mergedFindings.title: JournalNoticed feed not built — dump history is invisible to the user
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/dump/index.ts:4-5 — comment: 'The Journal feed lives in JournalNoticed (task #22, not yet built).' DumpScreen renders input + TodayNoticings + PatternCards but no history list. dump_archive table is written to SQLite via modules/dump/bridge.ts but no screen reads it back for the user.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Users can dump thoughts but cannot see any history of what they wrote. The primary ADHD reassurance loop ('did the app hear me? what did I tell it last week?') is missing. TodayNoticings shows AI-derived observations but the raw/recent dump list that provides psychological closure is absent.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a collapsible 'recent' section to DumpScreen rendering the last 5-10 rows from dump_archive (already accessible via modules/dump/bridge.ts). No new API needed.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Additive UI. Data layer already exists.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: DumpScreen integration test: after 3 dumps, recent list shows 3 items.

mergedFindings.title: Partner pairing QR code is decorative and unscannable — copy explicitly promises scanning behavior
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/modules/partner/PartnerBox.tsx:594-636 — FauxQR component comment: 'Not actually scannable (no dep); the 6-digit code is the working channel for now.' aria-hidden=true. PartnerBox copy at line 268 says 'let them scan it side-by-side, or send these six digits' — directly promising scanning behavior that does not work.
mergedFindings.userImpact: User may attempt to scan the QR code with their partner's phone camera and it will fail. The copy creates an explicit false affordance. Only the 6-digit code path works; users must discover this by failing to scan.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Change the copy from 'let them scan it side-by-side, or send these six digits' to 'send them these six digits'. Optionally label the FauxQR graphic as 'illustration'. Longer-term: replace with a real QR library (e.g. qrcode.react).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — copy change only for the immediate fix.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: No automated test possible for visual scanning; manual verification. Snapshot test confirming copy does not contain 'scan it side-by-side'.

mergedFindings.title: Settings screen is a stub — only sign-out and email visible; language, notifications, biometric, and consent controls are all missing
mergedFindings.evidence: navigation/Router.tsx SettingsScreen() renders exactly 2 items: account email (read-only) and sign-out button. setAppLang() has no caller. Push token registration exists in store.ts but is not surfaced. Biometric Face ID code exists (per memory) but has no settings UI. packages/consent exists but is not wired to Settings.

mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add language picker first (3 chips, calls setAppLang) since it blocks all non-English users. Then notification permission toggle. All others can follow incrementally.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low per setting added — each is an independent addition.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that SettingsScreen renders language chips and that selecting one persists via setAppLang.

Language picker: Rounds 1 and 2 confirm zero callers. Round 3 did not independently cover this finding but did not contradict it.
Goals arc: all 3 rounds agree it is fake. No dissent.
Onboarding: Rounds 1 and 2 confirm absence. Round 3 confirmed moduleManifest personal names separately. Combined picture is consistent.

Pets species hardcoding and coregulation gap: only Round 3 found these — Round 1 and Round 2 did not inspect pets/bridge.ts. Confidence 1, but code evidence is direct (BUILD GAP comment + zero write grep). Not contradicted by other rounds.
JournalNoticed: only Round 1 found this. Rounds 2 and 3 did not contradict it — Round 1 cites an explicit 'not yet built' comment in dump/index.ts.

angleSummary: The Ollie monorepo has a consistent pattern of orphaned packages, dead notification backends, split API layers, and a mis-wired cadence-scanner notification path. The most critical issues are: (1) the cadence-scanner fires all time-based cues to a NOOP console backend — no device notification ever reaches the user from this path; (2) three parallel module-name registries diverge silently and cause silent routing drops; (3) apps/api (ollie-notifications worker) is undeployed with a placeholder KV ID yet is the hardcoded target for iOS device-token registration; (4) three packages (@ollie/sync, @ollie/auth, @ollie/research-stream) are fully orphaned but CI still builds and tests them, creating false confidence that encrypted sync and passphrase vault are live.

mergedFindings.title: Cadence-scanner fires all cues to NOOP_BACKEND — no device notification delivered from cadence loop
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: packages/notifications exports Electron/Capacitor backends; apps/native never calls installBackend() — grep returns 0 results; native uses apps/native/src/notify/systemNotify.ts (Tauri plugin) directly. Round 3: packages/notifications/src/index.ts lines 74–90 shows NOOP_BACKEND is default (console.log only); packages/orchestrator/src/cadence-scanner.ts line 461 calls notify() from @ollie/notifications with no injected hook; apps/native/src/store.ts wires scheduleNotification→systemNotify for module-level future notifications only. grep for installBackend() in apps/native/src/: 0 results.
mergedFindings.userImpact: All time-based cadence cues (chores overdue, pet feeding, medication reminder, habit timing) that fire through cadence-scanner are silently dropped on device — console only. Module-level scheduled notifications (cycle, sleep, work timers) work correctly via the separate injected scheduleNotification path.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: packages/notifications is a well-engineered budget/dedupe/category-enforcement layer. Neither cadence-scanner nor the Tauri local-notification path honors it at runtime. Constitutional rules (daily cap, mute, no-streaks) are enforced at the type level only.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Option A: inject a notify hook into cadence-scanner (add a parameter) and wire it to systemNotify in apps/native. Option B: write a packages/notifications/src/backends/tauri.ts that wraps @tauri-apps/plugin-notification and call installBackend(tauriBackend) at native boot. Option B wires the full budget/dedupe layer.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — touches cadence-scanner public API or adds a new backend adapter. Requires device test to verify cues appear.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Integration test: cadence-scanner fires a cue → verify system notification is dispatched (mock Tauri backend, assert deliver was called). Runtime verify: set a pet feeding window to fire in 5s on device and confirm a notification appears.
mergedFindings.dissent: Round 1 framed this as a P2 architectural mismatch (notification constitution not enforced). Round 3 escalated to P1 based on cadence-scanner→NOOP path being confirmed in code. Marked needs-runtime-verification because store.ts comment ('scanner calls notify() internally regardless') may indicate cues are intentionally surfaced through TodayNoticings UI instead. Runtime test needed before final severity.

mergedFindings.title: Three parallel module-name registries kept in sync by hand — already drifting, silent routing drops
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 2: packages/logic/src/dissection/types.ts defines ModuleName (14 values, missing: mood, medication, chores, crisis). apps/native/src/router/schema.ts defines Module (14 values, missing: reminders, astrology, health). workers/ai-proxy/src/index.ts has its own embedded set. dispatch.ts line ~56 comments: 'module list drifted ahead of the native Module type (separate packages, kept in sync by hand; audit #22)'.
mergedFindings.userImpact: When ai-proxy adds or renames a module, fragments silently drop in dispatch.ts with no matched handler. The dissection fallback router will mis-route because its ModuleName set is a subset. No compile-time check catches the drift.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Silent data loss on routing. The only signal is a console.error that is not surfaced in production.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Move the canonical module union into @ollie/logic/dissection/types.ts and re-export it. Import that type in both apps/native/src/router/schema.ts and the ai-proxy worker. Add a compile-time exhaustiveness check in dispatch.ts.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — type-only refactor. Does not touch runtime logic.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Type-level test: assert that the Module union in schema.ts equals the ModuleName union from @ollie/logic via TypeScript Exclude/Extract at compile time.

mergedFindings.title: apps/api (ollie-notifications) is undeployed with a placeholder KV ID but is the hardcoded iOS device-token registration endpoint
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 2: .github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml deploys only workers/{ai-proxy,cron,apns-push,sentry-tunnel} — apps/api absent. Round 3: apps/api/wrangler.toml line 60 has placeholder KV id 'REPLACE_AFTER_wrangler_kv_create_DEVICE_TOKENS'; wrangler.toml comment says 'ollie-notifications is NOT currently deployed'. packages/notifications/src/backends/capacitor.ts hardcodes apps/api /register-token as the iOS device-token registration endpoint. Round 1: native app calls workers/apns-push at workers.ts:563 for /push.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If iOS push is ever activated via the capacitor backend, device-token registration will fail silently (undeployed worker + placeholder KV). User receives no remote push notifications. Account deletion (GDPR / App Store erasure) route in apps/api/src/account-delete.ts may also be unreachable in production.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Two APNs workers with split ownership: apps/api (undeployed, capacitor references it) and workers/apns-push (deployed, native app calls it). Any CI re-deploy leaves apps/api behind. The split creates a maintenance trap.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Consolidate: move /register-token into workers/apns-push (already deployed). Resolve the placeholder KV ID via `wrangler kv:namespace create DEVICE_TOKENS`. Then either delete apps/api or formally tombstone it and add it to deploy-workers.yml. Confirm account-delete.ts has a replacement before removal.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — touches account-delete endpoint which must survive. Run `wrangler deployments list --name ollie-notifications` to confirm current deploy state before acting.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: E2E: POST /register-token → token appears in KV AND push_tokens table → send test push → confirm receipt on device. Smoke test: GET /register-token returns 405, POST with bad auth returns 401.

mergedFindings.title: @ollie/sync and @ollie/auth are fully orphaned packages — encrypted multi-device sync not wired in shipped app
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: grep '@ollie/sync' and '@ollie/auth' across all .ts/.tsx produces zero hits outside the packages' own src/tests. Native uses apps/native/src/api/supabase.ts (direct @supabase/supabase-js) and apps/native/src/storage/encrypted.ts (@ollie/crypto) — bypassing both. Round 2 and 3 confirm with independent greps: 0 results for from '@ollie/auth' or @ollie/auth in any package.json outside self. @ollie/auth has 249 lines (vault/passphrase derive). CI still builds and tests both packages.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Encrypted multi-device sync (the feature @ollie/sync implements) is silently non-functional in the shipped app. No compile error warns of this. Architecture docs say encrypted sync is the user-data transport; the app writes plaintext to SQLite with no Supabase sync wired. CI runs full test suites for dead code.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: @ollie/auth depends on @ollie/store (localStorage) and @ollie/events — a layer violation that also prevents use in CF Worker or Node.js server contexts. @ollie/sync's VITE_SERVER_APPLY flag may gate something but is unverified.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Short term: add // ORPHANED comments to packages/sync/src/index.ts and packages/auth/src/index.ts; suppress from pnpm -r test. Long term: product decision — wire @ollie/sync to native (touches storage schema) or delete both packages.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero for annotation/CI suppression. High if wiring @ollie/sync — touches storage schema.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Workspace-level smoke test: every package in packages/* is imported by at least one app or worker. Verify VITE_SERVER_APPLY=1 wires @ollie/sync anywhere in native before deciding to delete.

mergedFindings.title: @ollie/research-stream is orphaned — 372 lines, zero callers, CI still runs its tests
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1, 2, 3 all independently grep @ollie/research-stream across .ts and package.json — zero results outside the package itself. Round 2: the research/labeling pipeline it was meant to power is handled instead by /enrich-dump + /label routes in workers/ai-proxy. Round 3: package is 372 lines with deps on @ollie/api, @ollie/consent, @ollie/events, @ollie/store.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Dead package inflates install time and CI test noise. False impression that a B2B research/labeling pipeline is wired when it is not.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Orphaned package carries cross-cutting deps (@ollie/api, @ollie/store) that increase the dependency graph width unnecessarily.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add // ORPHANED comment; exclude from pnpm -r test. Product decision: wire or delete.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None until wiring decision is made.

mergedFindings.title: apps/native has a parallel 1100-line HTTP client layer (api/workers.ts) alongside packages/api/client.ts — silent contract drift
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: apps/native/src/api/workers.ts line 13 acknowledges the duplication ('The pattern mirrors packages/api/client.ts but is standalone'). packages/api is in native's deps but only serverReminderBridge.ts imports it; all other worker calls go through native-local api/workers.ts. Round 2: packages/api/src/index.ts exports createOllieAPI + routeViaHaiku; only 1 import of @ollie/api in native src. Round 3: apps/native/src/api/workers.ts is 614 lines; api/index.ts adds ~500 more. routeViaHaiku in packages/api/src/anthropic.ts (256 lines) is unused in primary native code paths.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Bug fixes and new endpoints added to packages/api/client.ts silently do not apply to the native app's main call paths. Auth headers, retry logic, and error shapes can diverge between the two layers.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Two parallel HTTP clients for the same CF workers. Any worker API contract change must be applied twice. Legacy brainDump() and routeViaHaiku exports remain in packages/api and are not called by native primary paths, keeping dead endpoints alive in ai-proxy.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Extend packages/api/client.ts to cover the endpoints in apps/native/src/api/workers.ts and remove the native-local file. Then delete brainDump() from workers.ts and routeViaHaiku from @ollie/api. Add 410 responses on /brain-dump and /v1/messages in ai-proxy with a removal date.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — touching the primary HTTP call path in native requires regression testing all modules.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: One test per public endpoint in packages/api/client.ts verifying request shape matches worker expectations.

mergedFindings.title: packages/notifications Tauri backend missing — electron + capacitor backends shipped but never installed; Tauri path bypasses budget/dedupe entirely
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: packages/notifications/src/backends/ contains electron.ts, capacitor.ts, web.ts — no tauri.ts. Native never imports any backend from @ollie/notifications/backends/*. Round 3: packages/notifications/src/backends/electron.ts is a full Electron IPC backend (apps/electron is deleted). capacitor.ts is 200+ lines and hardcodes calls to apps/api /register-token (undeployed). grep installBackend in apps/native/src/: 0 results.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Dead code shipped every build. Capacitor backend is particularly risky: calling installCapacitorBackend() would route iOS device tokens to an undeployed endpoint with a placeholder KV ID — silent failure. Electron backend references a deleted app.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: The Tauri local notification path (systemNotify.ts) completely bypasses packages/notifications budget, dedupe, suppression, and per-category mute. No-streaks and daily-cap constitutional rules are enforced at type level only, not at runtime.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Delete electron.ts (apps/electron is gone). Add a prominent warning to capacitor.ts ('NOT installed in Tauri shell'). Write packages/notifications/src/backends/tauri.ts wrapping @tauri-apps/plugin-notification, then call installBackend(tauriBackend) in apps/native main.tsx.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for comment/deletion. Medium for writing and wiring the Tauri backend (requires device test).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test: sending two notifications with the same dedupe_key via Tauri backend only fires once.

mergedFindings.title: Dual storage systems (SQLite + localStorage @ollie/store) bridged by manual SYNCS array — new SQLite modules silently invisible to orchestrator
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 2: apps/native/src/bridge/index.ts syncs 14 modules manually in SYNCS array. bridge/index.ts comment confirms it is not exhaustive by design. Any new SQLite-backed module that misses a bridge.ts entry has its data invisible to orchestrator/watcher layer — silent failure with no console.error.
mergedFindings.userImpact: New modules added with SQLite repos but missing from bridge/index.ts SYNCS will produce no watcher offers or notices. Developers have no enforcement guard to catch the omission.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Manual registry pattern in a fast-moving codebase is a recurring source of silent bugs. Already one example: partner module uses kv (localStorage) not SQLite, so it correctly has no bridge entry — but the distinction is nowhere enforced.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add an eslint-plugin-ollie rule: every modules/*/repo.ts that calls sql.execute must have a corresponding entry in bridge/index.ts SYNCS. Alternatively, extract a type-level registry.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — lint rule only.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that adding a new SQLite-backed module repo without a bridge entry fails the lint rule.

mergedFindings.title: PII scrubber duplicated: workers/ai-proxy/src/pii.ts is a hand-maintained copy of @ollie/pii-scrub regex layer
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 2: workers/ai-proxy/src/pii.ts line 1-12 comment: 'NOTE: canonical scrubber moved to @ollie/pii-scrub … Keep these two implementations in sync for the regex layer.' workers/ai-proxy/package.json already declares @ollie/pii-scrub as a dep (used in index.ts for /enrich-dump). The local pii.ts is a separate regex-only copy run as a second pass before forwarding to Anthropic.
mergedFindings.userImpact: When @ollie/pii-scrub regex layer is updated (new phone formats, URL patterns), the local copy silently diverges. PII may leak to Anthropic even though the canonical scrubber would have caught it.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Two independent regex sets for the same purpose in the same worker. Divergence is silent — no test enforces parity.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Export the regex-only layer from @ollie/pii-scrub as a sub-path (e.g. @ollie/pii-scrub/regex) and import it in ai-proxy. Delete workers/ai-proxy/src/pii.ts.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — @ollie/pii-scrub is already a declared dep of ai-proxy.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that both the @ollie/pii-scrub canonical path and the ai-proxy second-pass use identical regex patterns (or eliminate the second pass entirely).

mergedFindings.title: marketing/site is an isolated 148 MB Astro sub-workspace inside the monorepo — invisible to root CI, not deployed
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: pnpm-workspace.yaml root lists apps/*, packages/*, workers/* — no marketing/*. marketing/site has its own pnpm-workspace.yaml and pnpm-lock.yaml. CI does not cd into it. Round 3: marketing/site/node_modules is 148 MB (du confirmed); marketing/site/dist is 88 KB. vercel.json implies a Vercel deployment; memory notes confirm 'Ollie has NO public web'.
mergedFindings.userImpact: 148 MB dead weight in the monorepo. Security vulnerabilities in marketing/site go undetected by CI. vercel.json references a deployment that is not running.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Two diverging lockfile trees. Astro app maintained manually with no automation.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Delete marketing/site/node_modules/ and marketing/site/dist/ (untracked anyway). Add both to .gitignore. Decide: keep source in repo (add to workspace + CI) or move to separate repo.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero — only deleting untracked build artifacts.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: If kept: add CI step cd marketing/site && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build.

mergedFindings.title: tools/eslint-plugin-ollie is outside the pnpm workspace — its tests do not run in root CI
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: pnpm-workspace.yaml has no tools/* entry. eslint.config.mjs line 16 uses a raw file-path import ('./tools/eslint-plugin-ollie/index.cjs'). Plugin tests (node --test rules/*.test.cjs) are not run by root pnpm test — manual only. Plugin uses CommonJS (type: commonjs) while monorepo is ESM.
mergedFindings.userImpact: ESLint plugin rule regressions go undetected in CI. Rules that enforce architecture invariants (banned-phrases, module registry) can silently break.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Plugin has no external deps so workspace membership is safe. Missing from pnpm -r test.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add tools/* to pnpm-workspace.yaml. Verify pnpm -r test covers the plugin after membership change.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Verify pnpm -r test runs plugin tests after workspace membership change.

mergedFindings.title: @ollie/auth has a layer-violation dependency on @ollie/store and @ollie/events — prevents use in server/worker contexts
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: packages/auth/package.json dependencies include @ollie/crypto, @ollie/events, @ollie/store. @ollie/store wraps localStorage (browserAdapter) with a React peerDependency. An encryption vault should be a leaf node with zero UI-layer deps.
mergedFindings.userImpact: None directly (package is orphaned). But if @ollie/auth is ever wired for server-side sync, it cannot run in a CF Worker or Node.js context because it carries localStorage and React peer-dep requirements.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Layer violation: crypto primitives (bottom) depend on state-management (middle). If @ollie/sync is wired for server-side sync, it cannot pull in @ollie/auth without dragging in the browser store.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Refactor @ollie/auth to accept a storage interface (key-value callbacks) instead of importing @ollie/store. Remove @ollie/events dep — callers emit events after auth state changes. Since the package is currently orphaned, refactor risk is low now.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low now (no callers). Grows if wired.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that @ollie/auth exports compile and run in a Node.js (no-DOM) context after refactor.

mergedFindings.title: ~13 stale references to deleted apps/web and apps/desktop scattered across packages/
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: grep -rn 'apps/web|apps/desktop' /packages --include='*.ts' returns 13 hits across packages/logic/src/dissection/fallback-route.ts:38, packages/sync/src/index.ts:425, packages/events/src/registry.ts:42, packages/notifications/src/index.ts:454, packages/notifications/src/suppression.ts:15, packages/orchestrator/src/braindump-dispatch.ts lines 13/662/1026/1062/1095/1124, packages/store/src/store.ts:13. Both apps/web and apps/desktop confirmed deleted.
mergedFindings.userImpact: None at runtime. Misleads contributors and AI audit agents into treating deleted apps as reference implementations. orchestrator/braindump-dispatch.ts has 6 comments referencing hooks in the deleted app — those contracts are fiction.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Cognitive overhead. TODO comments in orchestrator that can never be resolved.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: grep-replace all apps/web and apps/desktop references in packages/ with apps/native where applicable, or delete the comments. Add a lint rule in eslint-plugin-ollie banning 'apps/web' and 'apps/desktop' from non-design directories.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — comment-only changes.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Lint rule: ban 'apps/web' and 'apps/desktop' string literals from packages/ source files.

mergedFindings.title: docs/ + root directory audit/planning sprawl — 58 .md files, 5 dated audit dirs, two competing roadmaps
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: find docs -name '*.md' returns 58 files across docs/audit/, docs/audit-2026-06-09/, docs/audit-2026-06-15/, docs/audit/2026-06-18/, root-level audits/ (20 files). Round 2: root has CODEBASE_MAP.md, DATA_SCHEMA.md, DEPLOY_TODO.md, OLLIE_BOXES_2026-05-25.md, OLLIE_COFOUNDER_PRESENTATION.html/pdf, OLLIE_FEATURE_AUDIT_2026-05-25.md, OLLIE_ROADMAP_2026-05-25.md. Round 3: docs/MASTER_ROADMAP_2026-06-15.md vs root OLLIE_ROADMAP_2026-05-25.md — two roadmaps. Three differently-named audit subdirs make canonical state unclear.

mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: N/A.

apps/api deploy state: wrangler.toml comment says 'NOT currently deployed' but this cannot be confirmed without running `wrangler deployments list --name ollie-notifications`. If it was manually deployed at some point, the KV placeholder may be live.

packages/notifications backend enforcement: Round 1 says constitutional rules are 'enforced by type definitions only, not at runtime'. Round 3 confirms NOOP path. No round found a runtime path where budget or dedupe actually fires on device — consistent, but no positive runtime confirmation.

Three parallel module-name registries diverging by hand — any ai-proxy module addition silently drops fragments with no compile-time or runtime warning

angle: Agent 3 — Frontend App Architecture (apps/native/src, React/Tauri shell, routing, state, module/room wiring). Branch: redesign/olive-neumorphic.
angleSummary: Three independent rounds inspected the same codebase section and converged on 11 distinct issues. The two highest-risk structural gaps are: (1) zero error boundary coverage — any uncaught render throw white-screens the entire app with no recovery; and (2) useModuleData silently swallowing SQLite errors, leaving users on an infinite loading dot. Both were confirmed across all three rounds. A third systemic risk — the COMPONENTS registry typed as non-nullable masking undefined at runtime — was found by Round 3 and is a P2 crash trap. Dark mode infrastructure exists but is architecturally frozen by 40 files using a static color import; this is intentional today (forceMode=light) but will require a large-scale port when unblocked. Duplicate inline style constants (SMCP_STYLE/KICKER_STYLE/TITLE_STYLE) and Tile component copies are cosmetic debt confirmed across all three rounds. Quick-win dead code (App.tsx stub) and minor UX regressions (blank Clerk loading, hardcoded greeting, pets orphan in IA) round out the picture.
implementationRuntimeMismatches: Dark mode: ThemeProvider + CSS vars are fully implemented and would work for 7 CSS Module files, but 40 inline-style files import a static `colors` alias — so dark mode works in CSS but is frozen in inline styles. forceMode='light' intentionally gates this. Not a mismatch per se, but the system appears to support dark mode while being architecturally incapable of it for most screens.

navigate(-1) in BackBar: Round 3 flags this as P3/suspected because Tauri WKWebView may behave differently from a standard browser on empty history stack. Rounds 1 and 2 noted the same pattern but did not flag it as a distinct issue. Actual behavior on device is unverified.

GrocerySyncBridge getToken stability: All three rounds note that Clerk v5 documents getToken as a stable reference, but none could verify this in the Tauri localhost proxy context at static analysis time. Needs runtime confirmation.

mergedFindings.title: No error boundary anywhere in the component tree — any unhandled render throw crashes the entire app
mergedFindings.evidence: All three rounds ran exhaustive grep: `grep -rn 'ErrorBoundary|componentDidCatch|getDerivedStateFromError' apps/native/src/` → zero results. main.tsx wraps only ClerkProvider + ThemeProvider. Layout.tsx has no error boundary. Router.tsx has no Suspense or error boundary. With 14 Box components all eagerly loaded, one null-deref or malformed SQLite row silently removes the entire React tree.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any runtime error in any Box or Room (malformed SQLite row, null-deref in HealthRoom refresh, Clerk token edge case) white-screens the full app. User sees a blank screen with no message and must force-quit and relaunch. On iOS this is indistinguishable from a crash.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: React 18 renders nothing on unhandled render error in production. Affects all 14 eagerly-loaded Box components and all 5 Room files simultaneously.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a single class ErrorBoundary wrapper around <Outlet /> in Layout.tsx that renders a calm fallback ('something went wrong — tap to retry') and calls Sentry.captureException. ~20 lines, two files (Layout.tsx + new ErrorBoundary.tsx). Module-level boundaries can follow.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low — purely additive wrapper, no data-layer changes.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Render a Box whose render() throws; assert the ErrorBoundary fallback renders and the rest of the navigation (TabBar, other routes) is still accessible.

mergedFindings.title: useModuleData silently leaves screen frozen on infinite loading dot when SQLite migration or refresh fails
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/lib/useModuleData.ts lines 81-97 (R3 path references confirmed by R1 lines 92-96 and R2): setReady(true) is called only on the success path. The catch block only calls console.error and exits — it never sets an error state or calls setReady(false). All callers (SleepBox.tsx:93, GroceryBox.tsx:351, and all Room files) render '·' dots or 'loading…' for the falsy-ready branch with no timeout or fallback. HealthRoom refresh is a Promise.all of 9 concurrent calls — one failure silently collapses the entire refresh.
mergedFindings.userImpact: User taps any Room or Box on a device with a corrupt DB, failed Tauri plugin, or first-install schema race — sees '·' dots forever. No error message, no retry button, no explanation. Polling continues silently every 6 s with no user-visible effect.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Affects every module screen. The bug is centralized in one hook, making it high-leverage to fix.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `error: string | null` to useModuleData's state and return value. In the catch block: set error to a user-readable string and still call setReady(true) (or add a separate `failed` boolean). Each caller can then render a one-line 'couldn't load — tap to retry' tile. One hook file change + callers add a two-line guard.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. The hook is centralized; the change is additive. All callers already branch on ready.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: useModuleData unit test: mock migrate() to reject → assert error is non-null. Mock refresh() to reject → assert error is non-null and ready is not stuck false. Also cover HealthRoom's Promise.all failure path.

mergedFindings.title: Blank white screen during Clerk auth loading on cold start — no loading placeholder
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/main.tsx lines 64-69: <SignedIn><Router /></SignedIn><SignedOut><SignInGate /></SignedOut>. Clerk v5 (@clerk/clerk-react ^5.61.3) suppresses BOTH SignedIn and SignedOut while isLoaded=false. grep across all src/ for 'ClerkLoading' → zero results. On cold start (especially TestFlight/slower hardware), users see a blank cream rectangle for 200–800 ms with no indication the app is loading.
mergedFindings.userImpact: First-time users see a blank screen indistinguishable from a crash during auth initialization. Critical trust issue at first use and during TestFlight evaluation.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Also masks any Clerk initialization error — no fallback path if Clerk fails to load.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Wrap Gate body with Clerk's own <ClerkLoading> to render a minimal spinner or olive-neumorphic animated logo during the auth check. One import, wraps existing JSX.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero — purely additive.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Document in the onboarding test plan; runtime-only behavior not easily unit-testable.

mergedFindings.title: COMPONENTS registry in moduleRegistry.ts typed as non-nullable — missing entry crashes all routes silently
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/moduleRegistry.ts lines 30-54. COMPONENTS is typed Record<string, ComponentType> — index access returns ComponentType (non-nullable) even when the key is absent. Line 54: Component: COMPONENTS[m.id]. If a developer adds an entry to MODULE_META in moduleManifest.ts but forgets to add it to COMPONENTS, React Router mounts <Route element={<undefined />}> → React throws 'Element type is invalid' which crashes the entire <Routes> tree. TypeScript produces no warning because Record<string, X>[string] is typed as X not X | undefined.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Adding any future module (brain v2, mood, partner) by only touching moduleManifest.ts crashes the whole app for every user on next update — all routes break, not just the new one.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Silent TypeScript gap: the type system gives false confidence. The error only surfaces at runtime in production. No error boundary currently wraps the Routes tree.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Type COMPONENTS as Record<string, ComponentType | undefined> and add a runtime guard: `Component: COMPONENTS[m.id] ?? FallbackBox`. Or add a module-load assertion: `MODULE_META.forEach(m => { if (!COMPONENTS[m.id]) throw new Error('Missing component for ' + m.id) })`. Add a test asserting MODULE_META.every(m => m.id in COMPONENTS).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — one-line type change and one-line null-guard. No runtime behavior change for existing modules.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: assert every MODULE_META entry has a matching key in COMPONENTS. This test would have caught the gap immediately.

mergedFindings.title: Box screens show stale data for up to 6 seconds after a brain dump writes to SQLite
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/lib/useModuleData.ts line 23: POLL_MS = 6000. DumpScreen.tsx emits no CustomEvent after dispatch completes. dispatch.ts fires runAllSyncs() + recomputeBrain() non-blocking but emits no module-invalidation signal. Box screens (Grocery, Chores, etc.) only refresh on the 6 s poll or window focus. PatternCards are reactive via store.subscribeKey; per-screen Glance data (choresToday, medTaken, etc.) is owned by local useState and only refreshed by polling.
mergedFindings.userImpact: User dumps 'bought milk, ran out of pasta', immediately taps the Grocery box — sees pantry state from before the dump. If the box was already open (no focus event), they wait up to 6 s. Contradicts the 'contextually aware' product promise.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: The SQLite-to-store bridge wires PatternCards reactively but leaves module-specific Glance data on a polling cadence. Two different reactivity models in the same app.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: After dispatchRouterOutput resolves, fire: window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('ollie:module-updated')). In useModuleData, add a window.addEventListener that calls refresh() on that event. One file change each, no new dependencies.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. The CustomEvent is fire-and-forget; worst case is a spurious extra SQLite read.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Mount a Box, dispatch a dump, assert the Box re-renders with new data within 100 ms without waiting for the 6 s poll interval.

mergedFindings.title: Dark mode infrastructure fully built but permanently dead — 40 files hardcode light palette via static import
mergedFindings.dissent: Rounds 1 and 2 note forceMode='light' as a known deferred item (product decision, Faz 6b). Round 3 escalates this to a structural finding: even if forceMode is removed, 40 files import `colors` from tokens.ts as a static alias (line 116: export const colors = lightPalette) and will never respond to ThemeProvider state. The CSS Module files (7 files using CSS vars) WOULD work in dark mode; the inline-style files (40) would not. Rounds 1/2 treated this as product-deferred; Round 3 identifies an architectural gap that must be addressed before dark mode can ship regardless of schedule.
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/theme/tokens.ts line 116: `export const colors = lightPalette` — static alias. grep for `import { colors } from '../theme/tokens'` across apps/native/src → 40 .tsx files. grep for `useTheme()` or `useTokens()` → zero results. main.tsx line 94: forceMode='light'. ThemeProvider injects CSS vars onto <html> which 7 CSS Module files consume correctly. The other 40 inline-style files bypass ThemeProvider entirely.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Dark mode will never ship without porting 40 files. forceMode='light' is intentionally suppressing this, but removing it without the port would expose a half-broken dark mode to users where rooms and boxes stay light even when the system is dark.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Do not remove forceMode='light' before the port. Document scope: extract a useColors() hook wrapping useTheme() and migrate 40 files mechanically. Add a lint rule banning `import { colors } from '../theme/tokens'` in .tsx files to prevent regression.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: High for the full port — 40 files, each needing conversion from static import to hook call. No data layer changes, but visual regression risk across all screens.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Snapshot tests per room/box asserting token values match the active theme mode. Lint rule: ban static `import { colors }` in component files.

mergedFindings.title: All 14 Box components eagerly imported at router boot — no code splitting
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/moduleRegistry.ts lines 11-24: 14 static top-level import statements (GroceryBox through PartnerBox). grep for 'React.lazy|lazy(|Suspense' across apps/native/src/ → zero results. GroceryBox alone is 1,480 lines; total module tree is ~10,931 lines of component code. Round 2 notes this is a catch-22 with the missing error boundary — lazy() failures are unrecoverable without an error boundary.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Every module's SQLite migration imports, repo adapters, and sub-components bundle into the initial JS chunk. Cold-start parse/eval cost is proportional to the full module tree on every launch, not just the screen opened. Measurable on low-end iPhones.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Prevents incremental loading. Also blocks adding lazy() until error boundary (P1) is in place.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: After adding the error boundary (finding #1): convert moduleRegistry.ts to React.lazy(() => import(...)) for each Box. Wrap MODULE_MANIFEST routes in <Suspense fallback={<LoadingDot />}>. No logic change — each Box is already a single default export.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low after error boundary exists. Do not add lazy() before error boundary or lazy() failures become unrecoverable.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Bundle-size regression check (vite-bundle-visualizer snapshot) confirming initial chunk drops significantly. Verify each lazy-loaded module renders after Suspense resolves.

mergedFindings.title: Tile component copy-pasted into all 5 Room files with divergent implementations
mergedFindings.evidence: grep 'function Tile' apps/native/src/rooms/*.tsx → 5 matches (HouseholdRoom.tsx:207, HealthRoom.tsx:354, GrowthRoom.tsx:245, ResponsibilitiesRoom.tsx:258, MoneyRoom.tsx:262). HealthRoom.tsx already has a diverged Tile signature with an optional 'to?' prop and a conditional Link/div branch that the other 4 lack. HouseholdRoom's Tile types 'to' as required string — silently breaks if someone tries to add a read-only tile by copying the HealthRoom pattern.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Design drift is already visible between HealthRoom (read-only tile renders plain div) and the other 4 rooms (always render a Link). Future visual changes (hover state, dark mode, accessibility) must be applied to 5 independent copies.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Extract apps/native/src/rooms/RoomTile.tsx using the HealthRoom variant (optional to prop) as canonical. Replace 5 local definitions with a single import.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — pure refactor, no behavior change. Risk: missing HealthRoom's optional-to variant and breaking the read-only energy tile; test covers this.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Render test for RoomTile with to=undefined (assert no Link rendered, no chevron) and to='/box/foo' (assert Link rendered).

mergedFindings.title: SMCP_STYLE, TITLE_STYLE, KICKER_STYLE constants redeclared in 20–37 files with already-diverged values
mergedFindings.evidence: R1: 37 const declarations across codebase (confirmed grep count: 146 matches for the style names). R2: 20 occurrences of SMCP_STYLE alone (Router.tsx, TabBar.tsx, DumpScreen.tsx, NeedsConfirmCard.tsx, TodoScreen.tsx, all 5 Room files, ChoresBox.tsx, SleepBox.tsx, GoalsBox.tsx, PetsBox.tsx, CycleBox.tsx, BodyBox.tsx, HabitsBox.tsx, AdminBox.tsx, FeedMeView.tsx, GoalCreateModal.tsx). R3: confirms divergence already present — Router.tsx KICKER_STYLE has fontSize:10 vs other files. theme/tokens.ts exports colors/radii/shadows but no typography presets.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Invisible today but any global type change (letterSpacing, fontWeight) requires touching 20-37 files. Divergence is already happening: Router.tsx KICKER_STYLE differs from HealthRoom.tsx.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a textStyles object to theme/tokens.ts (smcp, title, kicker, aside) and replace local constants with imports. Also fix the diverged Router.tsx KICKER_STYLE value at the same time. Mechanical find-and-replace.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero — values are nearly identical; alignment is the fix.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Lint rule banning module-local declarations of SMCP_STYLE/KICKER_STYLE/TITLE_STYLE (enforced via ESLint custom rule or banned-phrase scan).

mergedFindings.title: TodoScreen has its own manual polling loop instead of using useModuleData
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/todo/TodoScreen.tsx lines 200-206: manual setInterval(POLL_MS=6000) + window.addEventListener('focus', onFocus). The useModuleData hook was created specifically to eliminate this pattern (its own comment at lib/useModuleData.ts:1 references audit #35). TodoScreen was not migrated.
mergedFindings.userImpact: TodoScreen's polling behavior may drift from POLL_MS constant changes. The migration once-guard is not applied — the todo migration could run multiple times on React StrictMode double-invoke.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Migrate TodoScreen to use useModuleData({migrationKey:'todo', migrate, refresh}) and delete the manual setInterval/focus wiring.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — mechanical substitution.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: StrictMode double-invoke test asserting the todo migration runs exactly once per mount.

mergedFindings.title: Pets module orphaned from rooms IA — no discoverable path from any Room
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/Router.tsx lines 153-168: ROOMED_IDS contains 'grocery' and 'chores' but NOT 'pets'. pets is in group 'your-stuff' in moduleManifest.ts line 39. The visible filter excludes ROOMED_IDS so grocery/chores are hidden from the flat section. pets is not in ROOMED_IDS, so it falls through to the flat group section as a lone item under 'your stuff' below the 5 room cards. HouseholdRoom (/room/household) only lists chores + grocery.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Users navigating via rooms (the primary IA) have no discoverable path to the Pets module. They must navigate to /modules (secondary flat list) to find it. Likely a product decision for v1 but creates a navigation dead-end.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Either: (a) add 'pets' to ROOMED_IDS and include it in HouseholdRoom as a glance tile, or (b) add an explicit Pets room. This is a product decision before a code change.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low code risk; requires design decision.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Snapshot test for ModulesIndex asserting every module in MODULE_META is either in a room card or explicitly listed in the flat fallback — no orphans.

mergedFindings.title: navigate(-1) in BackBar causes silent navigation failure on empty history stack (deep-link entry points)
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/Layout.tsx lines 42-53: BackBar renders a back button for any path not in the hardcoded isTopLevel set. Room paths (/room/health, /room/household, etc.) are NOT in the top-level set, so they render a Back button. Handler is navigate(-1). In a BrowserRouter, navigate(-1) on an empty history stack (e.g. cold-start deep-link directly to /room/health via widget) may navigate to the WebView's previous page in Tauri's WKWebView, which could be blank or an external URL.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A user cold-launched into a Room via widget or deep link and tapping back may see a blank screen or be navigated to an unexpected destination. Not reproducible in standard browser testing — needs device verification.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Guard: `onClick={() => { if (window.history.length > 1) navigate(-1); else navigate('/modules'); }}`. One-line fix. Alternatively add '/room/*' to the isTopLevel check so rooms get no back button (they're always reachable via TabBar).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low. One-line guard.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Integration test: render BackBar at /room/health with empty history stack → assert navigate() is called with '/modules' not -1.

mergedFindings.title: Pantry push scanner fires at module load before grocery SQLite migration has run — silent failure on fresh install
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/main.tsx lines 38-47: scanPantryPushes() is called at module evaluation time, before ReactDOM.createRoot() and before any React component mounts. The grocery SQLite migration (migrateGrocery()) only runs when GroceryBox or HouseholdRoom mounts via useModuleData. On first launch, pantry.list() inside the scanner queries a table that may not exist yet. The scanner catches the SQL error silently (pushScanner.ts lines 87-89). First-boot push scan always returns 0 fired notifications.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Pantry depletion push notifications never fire on first app open after a fresh install or DB reset. Only fires after the user navigates to Grocery or Household once. Low-frequency but entirely silent failure.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Move scanPantryPushes() into the GrocerySyncBridge component (already in Router.tsx) so it runs after auth + after first mount. Or run it inside useModuleData's post-migration callback for GroceryBox.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Moving an async call from module evaluation into a React effect.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Integration test: assert scanPantryPushes fires after migration runs, not before. Existing test (returns 0 when table absent) already passes.

mergedFindings.title: BoxPlaceholder reads URL via window.location.pathname regex instead of React Router useParams
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/Router.tsx lines 374-397: readBoxIdFromPath() uses window.location.pathname.match(/\/box\/([^/]+)/). This runs at render time inside a function that is not a hook. Currently works because BrowserRouter uses pathname and app is served at root. Will silently return empty string if routing base changes or hash-routing is used.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Currently invisible in production. Will silently display a blank module name if the routing base ever changes. Also prevents SSR if ever considered.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace readBoxIdFromPath() with const { id } = useParams<{ id: string }>() inside BoxPlaceholder. Two-line change.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Render BoxPlaceholder with a mocked route and assert the id is displayed correctly.

mergedFindings.title: Room-level useModuleData migration keys are separate from Box-level keys — same migrations run twice per session
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/rooms/HouseholdRoom.tsx line 79: migrationKey: 'room-household'. apps/native/src/modules/chores/ChoresBox.tsx line 88: migrationKey: 'chores'. The migrationOnce guard in lib/useModuleData.ts is keyed by migrationKey. HouseholdRoom calls migrateChores() + migrateGrocery() under key 'room-household'; ChoresBox calls migrateChores() under key 'chores'. Both guards pass, so migrateChores() runs twice per session when user opens HouseholdRoom then navigates to /box/chores.
mergedFindings.userImpact: No data corruption (migrations are CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, idempotent at SQLite level). Mild: ~10-50 ms of redundant SQLite round-trips per Room→Box navigation.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Key the migrationOnce map by the migrate function reference (WeakMap) or share the same key between Room and Box — Room uses the canonical per-module key ('chores') rather than 'room-chores'.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — all migrations are idempotent; the fix is a naming change.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test: call migrateGrocery via two different useModuleData instances with different keys; assert the underlying SQL executes only once via mock.

mergedFindings.title: Hardcoded personal pet names ('tontin', 'pinpon') shipped in app copy and stub handlers
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/moduleManifest.ts line 39: hint: 'tontin + pinpon'. apps/native/src/modules/pets/PetsBox.tsx line 194: 'tontin'. apps/native/src/modules/stubs.ts line 18: '"logged tontin's vitamin C"'. apps/native/src/body/handler.ts line 227 + router/schema.ts line 170: 'tontin'. These are Serra's personal pet names hard-wired into visible copy, stub handlers, and routing schema.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Every beta user sees 'tontin + pinpon' as the pets module hint. Stub handler example could surface in logs or UI visible to other users, leaking personal data. Trust/polish blocker for beta.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace all 'tontin'/'pinpon' occurrences with generic copy: hint → 'your pets', stub → 'logged vitamin C for the cat', handler comments → 'pet name'. ~6 files, search-replace.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — purely copy changes, no logic impact.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: CI banned-phrase scan: block 'tontin' and 'pinpon' from appearing in src/.

mergedFindings.title: Import statement placed after constant declaration in Router.tsx — invalid static import ordering
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/Router.tsx lines 32-39: const TITLE_STYLE: React.CSSProperties = {...} declared at line 32, then import { colors, radii, shadows } from '../theme/tokens' at line 39. Static imports must lexically precede code in ES modules. TypeScript/Vite hoists this at compile time so it works today, but violates import/first lint rule.
mergedFindings.userImpact: No runtime impact today. Risk: a future stricter build mode or static analysis tool rejects the file. Developer confusion during code review.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Move the import { colors, radii, shadows } from '../theme/tokens' above line 32. One-line fix.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Enable eslint import/first rule in eslint.config.mjs to catch this class of issue automatically.

mergedFindings.title: Hardcoded 'good evening' greeting in DumpScreen regardless of time of day
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/dump/DumpScreen.tsx line 264: 'good evening' is hardcoded as a Text caption. No time-of-day check (getHours()) anywhere in DumpScreen.
