mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/server-apply-routes.ts line 69-70: since = req.searchParams.get('since') passed directly to pullGroceryPantry. server-apply.ts line 182: &updated_at=gt.${encodeURIComponent(sinceIso)}. encodeURIComponent prevents injection. A string like 'hello' reaches PostgREST which returns 400/422; pullGroceryPantry returns [] on !res.ok (line 190), giving the client a silent empty pull that looks like 'no new rows'.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A buggy client sending a non-ISO since param silently gets an empty pull and loses incremental sync — stale data displayed with no error surfaced to the user.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Silent empty-pull data loss on device. No security breach. Hard to debug since the 400 from PostgREST is swallowed.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In handleSyncGroceryPantry: `if (since && isNaN(Date.parse(since))) return json({ error: 'invalid_since' }, 400);` before calling pullGroceryPantry.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — fails fast instead of silently returning empty.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: GET /sync/grocery-pantry?since=not-a-date → 400. ?since=2026-06-01T00:00:00Z → passes. ?since omitted → returns all rows.

mergedFindings.title: /register-token (apps/api): APNs device token stored to KV without hex format validation
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/api/src/worker.ts lines 306-341: handleRegister checks only !body.token (truthy check). No hex format validation against /^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,200}$/. Token stored verbatim via env.DEVICE_TOKENS.put(key, ...). The downstream sendApns function (line 464) does validate hex format and returns { ok: false } for invalid tokens — so bad tokens silently fail at delivery. workers/apns-push worker correctly validates at line 102.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A malformed APNs token registers successfully. Cron-triggered pushes silently fail for that user. User loses notification delivery with no error surfaced.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Silent notification delivery failure. KV storage of garbage data. The Postgres mirror (mirrorTokenToPostgres, line 353) also stores the malformed token.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add after the !body.token || !body.platform check: `if (!/^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,200}$/.test(body.token)) return new Response('invalid token format', { status: 400 });`
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Near zero — legitimate iOS tokens are always 64-char hex.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: POST /register-token with token='not-hex' → 400. With token='' → 400.

mergedFindings.title: APNs push payload forwarded to Apple without size validation in apns-push worker
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/apns-push/src/index.ts lines 105-136: body.payload validated only as typeof === 'object', then JSON.stringify(body.payload) forwarded directly to api.push.apple.com. Apple APNs hard limit is 4096 bytes. An oversized payload causes Apple to return 413 (TooMuchData); the worker passes this through to the caller which may retry, wasting budget. Worker itself has no content-length guard before req.json(). Endpoint is internal (APNS_INTERNAL_SECRET required).
mergedFindings.userImpact: Internal caller sending an oversized payload causes silent notification loss without a clear error. Cron callers may retry, wasting budget.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: APNs rejects oversized payload with 413 (TooMuchData). No crash or data leak. Internal endpoint only.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: After payload validation: `if (JSON.stringify(body.payload).length > 4096) return json({ error: 'payload_too_large' }, 413);`
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — internal endpoint only.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: POST /push with payload > 4096 bytes → 413 from worker before Apple is called.

implementationRuntimeMismatches: /route/dump locale: R1 says bad locale can cause a 500 (RangeError in some V8 versions, dump lost); R2 rates it P4 and says try/catch in segmentation.ts lines 89-98 handles it gracefully; R3 confirms the try/catch exists. Resolution: the fallback is real but V8-version-dependent behaviour is unverified at runtime — treat as P3 with defensive fix still warranted.

CF KV key 512-byte limit for dumpId overflow (Finding 3): all three rounds describe the overflow but whether CF Workers platform silently truncates or throws needs runtime verification. R1 says KV.put .catch() is silent; R2 confirms caught+non-crashing; R3 agrees. The silent failure path is consistent across rounds but actual CF platform behaviour is unconfirmed without wrangler dev test.
topRisks: P1: /brain-dump proxy has zero JWT auth — any caller can exhaust ANTHROPIC_API_KEY by cycling fake x-user-id values to bypass per-user rate limit (workers/ai-proxy/src/index.ts:436-447)

P1: /label endpoint interpolates unvalidated locale directly into Anthropic user message — prompt injection for authenticated users corrupts the entire B2B analytics corpus (workers/ai-proxy/src/label.ts:147-149)

P2: /route/dump accepts dumpId of any length/type — a 500-char dumpId silently breaks idempotency via CF KV key overflow, causing duplicate AI charges on retry (workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts:208)

P2: /enrich-dump metadata string fields (device_id, locale, country, app_version) have no length caps — can pump ~63KB per field into KV and Supabase raw_dumps at 10 req/min (workers/ai-proxy/src/telemetry.ts:172-177)
P2: /ingest-event and /cook-history buffer full request body before any Content-Length pre-check — authenticated amplification vector (telemetry.ts:247, cook-history.ts:101)
quickWins: label.ts line 116: add VALID_LOCALES = new Set(['en','es','tr']) check — one line closes the P1 prompt injection path
index.ts ~442: add verifyClerkJwt() guard to /brain-dump path — copy verbatim from /route/dump pattern
dump.ts ~208: add UUID format regex on body.dumpId before idempotencyKey call — one conditional block
telemetry.ts ~172: add .length caps on device_id (≤64), locale (≤8), country (≤3), app_version (≤20) after typeof checks

angleSummary: UI/UX audit of apps/native/src on branch redesign/olive-neumorphic. Covers dump flow, room navigation, module reachability, copy quality, empty/error states, accessibility, onboarding, dark mode, and ADHD-safety fidelity. All findings code-confirmed; no runtime verification performed.

mergedFindings.title: No onboarding — new users land on a blank DumpScreen with zero orientation after sign-in
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/main.tsx: SignedIn renders <Router /> directly → Router mounts DumpScreen at /. No onboarding flag, welcome screen, firstRun check, or tutorial exists in any file. grep for 'onboarding', 'firstRun', 'first_time', 'welcome', 'ONBOARDED' across apps/native/src/ returns zero application hits (one comment in pets/bridge.ts only).
mergedFindings.userImpact: A first-time user after sign-in sees 'what's on your mind?' with no explanation of the dump-to-module pipeline, what rooms are, or why the textarea is the entire product. ADHD users especially need a scaffolded first moment; without it the minimalism reads as a broken app, not a calm assistant. Empty module states ('brain dump something to fill it') assume prior knowledge that was never taught.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a localStorage ONBOARDED_KEY check after Clerk sign-in. If absent, show a one-screen overlay (3 sentences max: 'dump anything here → we file it for you → tap Rooms to see it'). Dismiss = set flag. Does not need a wizard — an inline callout under the textarea with 2 example dumps ('try: I bought milk' / 'I slept 5 hours') suffices for v1 alpha.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Purely additive; existing users skip via stored flag.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test overlay appears on first sign-in; test it is skipped on second open via stored flag.
mergedFindings.dissent: Round 1 classified P3; Round 3 classified P1. Round 3 is correct given alpha launch risk — new users with no mental model will churn before they discover the value. Raised to P1.

mergedFindings.title: Hardcoded 'good evening' greeting — wrong on every morning and afternoon open
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/dump/DumpScreen.tsx line 264: literal string 'good evening' in JSX. No time-of-day logic exists anywhere in the file. Verified via direct read.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Every user who opens the app before 6pm sees an incorrect greeting. The home screen is the highest-frequency surface — a stale greeting signals the AI is inattentive, directly undermining trust in a product sold as a calm life assistant.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace literal with: `const getGreeting = () => { const h = new Date().getHours(); return h < 12 ? 'good morning' : h < 18 ? 'good afternoon' : 'good evening'; };` — call in render. No state, no I/O.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Negligible. Pure function.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test getGreeting() at h=6, h=13, h=20.

mergedFindings.title: HealthRoom sleepSub dead ternary — both branches return 'last night', empty state reads as contradictory
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/rooms/HealthRoom.tsx line 198: `const sleepSub = !ready ? ' ' : g.sleep ? 'last night' : 'last night';` — both ternary branches are identical. When sleep is null the tile shows value='no log' + sub='last night', which is internally contradictory.
mergedFindings.userImpact: First-time users (and any day without a sleep log) see a tile that says 'no log / last night'. The copy implies a log existed last night, contradicting the value. Adds cognitive load on the highest-value health glance surface.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Line 198: change `'last night' : 'last night'` to `'last night' : 'tap to log'`.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero. One-character change.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Snapshot derived glance strings for g.sleep=null case.

mergedFindings.title: 'cmd + enter to send' keyboard hint always visible on iPhone — inapplicable on touch devices
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/dump/BrainDumpInput.tsx line 378: hint text 'cmd + enter to send' rendered unconditionally. No platform detection, matchMedia, or CSS breakpoint guard exists in BrainDumpInput. iPhone is the primary dogfood device.
mergedFindings.userImpact: iPhone users see a macOS keyboard shortcut that does nothing and has no meaning on a touch keyboard. Occupies screen real estate in an already-cramped bottom row and erodes product polish on the most important interaction surface.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Hide via CSS: `.cmdHint { @media (hover: none) { display: none; } }` — or conditionally render null when `navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1`. Replace with 'tap send' or nothing on touch.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero. Visual-only.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Snapshot: touch UA → hint absent or shows 'tap send'; desktop UA → 'cmd + enter'.

mergedFindings.title: GoalCreateModal requires 5 mandatory free-text fields including jargon terms — blocks ADHD users mid-flow
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/modules/goals/GoalCreateModal.tsx lines 79-85, 315: canSave gated on what + why + obstacle + premortem + ulyssesContract all non-empty. Modal opens from casual dump ('I want to go to greece'). Terms 'premortem' and 'ulysses contract' are undefined in UI.
mergedFindings.userImpact: An ADHD user who offloaded a fleeting thought is immediately blocked from saving unless they write a premortem and a Ulysses contract — high activation cost. Most will abandon. Violates the 'dump and move on' product promise. Jargon terms increase cognitive load for all users.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Change canSave to require only what + why. Collapse obstacle/premortem/ulysses under an 'add more' expander. Ulysses contract is most valuable at deletion time, not creation — prompt for it then instead.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium. Ulysses-contract deletion gate and 72h low-mood delete-lock both degrade gracefully when goal.ulyssesContract is blank (GoalsBox reads it conditionally). Verify deletion flow still guards correctly with blank contract.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: GoalCreateModal: Save enabled with only what+why filled. Deletion gate: goal with no ulyssesContract skips contract step gracefully.

mergedFindings.title: prefers-reduced-motion users get a 2500ms solid full-viewport colour flood after every dump
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/dump/DumpScreen.module.css lines 46-56: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ack { opacity: 1; animation-duration: 0ms; } }`. Static opacity:1 override disables the animation but keeps the element at full opacity until ACK_FADE_MS=2500ms JS cleanup timer fires (DumpScreen.tsx line 42). A 2.5-second solid sage full-screen remains on every dump.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Reduced-motion users — who opted in specifically to avoid vestibular/sensory discomfort — get a 2.5s solid-colour viewport takeover instead of a brief animation. The ADHD-safe product promise is broken for this population.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `display: none` to the reduced-motion block, or detect `prefers-reduced-motion` via matchMedia in the ACK timer and cut ACK_FADE_MS to ~100ms. The aria-live=polite region already announces 'Okay!' so screen readers are unaffected.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. aria-live still fires; sighted reduced-motion users simply get no visual, which is the intended behaviour.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Manual QA checklist item: verify on device with prefers-reduced-motion enabled.
mergedFindings.dissent: Only Round 1 found this. Rounds 2 and 3 noted in doNotTouch that the prefers-reduced-motion block is 'correctly implemented'. This is a dissent: Round 1 correctly identifies that disabling animation is NOT equivalent to removing the full-viewport colour block for 2.5s. The CSS is logically present but behaviourally wrong for the reduced-motion use case.

mergedFindings.title: NeedsConfirmCard exposes raw snake_case action names to users ('body · log_symptom', 'work · create_task')
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/dump/DumpScreen.tsx lines 58-66 (buildRouteLabel): concatenates raw module id + raw action string from router schema (apps/native/src/router/schema.ts lines 157-229). NeedsConfirmCard.tsx line 99 renders this as routeLabel. Confirmed by direct read of DumpScreen.tsx.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Every grey-zone routing (confidence 0.60–0.79) shows a confirmation card with developer jargon. Breaks the calm editorial voice and confuses non-technical users on what should be the clearest moment of trust-building.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a FRIENDLY_LABEL lookup map in buildRouteLabel covering the ~25 action types in schema.ts (e.g. `{'body·log_symptom': 'logged a symptom for Body'}`). Fall back to current format if key is missing.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Purely cosmetic; routing and dispatch logic unchanged.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Snapshot NeedsConfirmCard with a representative routeLabel to lock in friendly copy.

mergedFindings.title: ResponsibilitiesRoom focus tile shows todo count under 'focus' label when no focus logged — internally contradictory
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/rooms/ResponsibilitiesRoom.tsx lines 117-128: when focusMinutes=0 and todoCount>0, focusVal renders as e.g. '3 today' (a todo count) but focusSub renders 'no focus logged yet'. Tile label is 'focus'. The value is not a focus metric.
mergedFindings.userImpact: ADHD user glancing at the room dashboard may read '3 today' as minutes/sessions of focus, then be confused by the sub-label. Cognitive load spike on a glance surface designed for instant clarity.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: When focusMinutes=0, set focusVal='none yet' and focusSub='no focus logged today — tap to start'. Do not fall through to todoCount.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: None. Display-only.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Snapshot derived glance strings for focusMinutes=0 / todoCount>0 case.

mergedFindings.title: Mood module unreachable by tap — ROOMED_IDS includes mood but HealthRoom has no link to /box/mood
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/Router.tsx line 160: 'mood' is in ROOMED_IDS (filtered from flat module list). apps/native/src/rooms/HealthRoom.tsx lines 12-13, 201, 264: energy tile is explicitly READ-ONLY with no chevron and no Link ('there's no mood screen' per comment at line 353). MoodBox exists and is registered (moduleRegistry.ts:33) at /box/mood but no tap path reaches it from any Room.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Users who dump mood/energy can never navigate to MoodBox to review or delete entries. Their mood history is invisible and uncontrollable. For an ADHD-safety product, 'where did my mood notes go?' is a trust-breaking question.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Either (a) add a drill tile in HealthRoom linking to /box/mood, or (b) if mood is intentionally read-only and integrated, document this as a product decision and ensure users are informed that mood is surfaced only as the energy tile.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low if additive link. Product decision needed first.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Navigation smoke test: from /room/health, can reach /box/mood.
mergedFindings.dissent: Round 2 flagged this as P2 confirmed. Round 1 did not find it. Round 3 did not flag it separately. HealthRoom.tsx comment at line 353 says 'no mood screen' suggesting this may be a deliberate product decision (mood absorbed into energy tile). Needs product verification before fixing.

mergedFindings.title: Pets module orphaned — not in ROOMED_IDS, appears as a lone 'your stuff' flat-group below the 5 room cards
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/Router.tsx lines 153-174: ROOMED_IDS does not include 'pets'. apps/native/src/navigation/moduleManifest.ts line 39: pets assigned to group 'your-stuff'. ModulesIndex renders non-roomed visible modules as flat group cards below the 5 room cards. No PetsRoom exists; HouseholdRoom.tsx does not link to /box/pets.
mergedFindings.userImpact: The Rooms page promises 'one calm screen per part of your life' then breaks the metaphor with a flat 'your stuff' overflow section containing just pets. Reads as an oversight; new users cannot tell if pets is intentionally excluded or unfinished.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add 'pets' to ROOMED_IDS in Router.tsx. Add a pets Tile + PatternCards entry to HouseholdRoom.tsx linking to /box/pets. PetsBox already exists and is registered.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Purely additive to HouseholdRoom.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: ModulesIndex render test: no flat-group sections when ROOMED_IDS includes pets.

mergedFindings.title: Migration failure leaves module screens stuck at 'loading…' indefinitely — no error message, no retry
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/lib/useModuleData.ts lines 92-97: failed migrate/refresh catches error, logs to console, leaves `ready` as false forever. All module Boxes render 'loading…' when !ready (confirmed in HabitsBox.tsx:142, SleepBox.tsx:95, etc.) with no error branch.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If SQLite migration fails (corrupted db, storage quota, permissions), the user's entire module becomes an infinite loading screen with no explanation and no path out. Silent failure on data the user trusts Ollie to safeguard.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a `failed` state to useModuleData that flips in the catch block. Each Box checks `failed` and renders an inline calm message: 'something went wrong — tap to retry' with a retry callback calling refresh().
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Additive state in hook; opt-in check per Box.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: useModuleData: when migrate throws, hook exposes failed=true. Box unit test: renders error state when failed=true.

mergedFindings.title: Notification permission prompt positioned inside BrainDumpInput — intrusive interrupt in the typing zone
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/dump/BrainDumpInput.tsx line 391: <NotifyPrimeLine /> rendered at the bottom of the BrainDumpInput Stack, inside the input affordance, below the send/mic/photo buttons. Verified by direct read.
mergedFindings.userImpact: The first dump is the user's highest-anxiety moment. A permission prompt appearing inside the typing area (rather than below it) breaks the ADHD user's train of thought and violates the 'fire and forget, silent ack' dump UX principle. Visually it reads as part of the send row.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Move <NotifyPrimeLine /> from BrainDumpInput.tsx to DumpScreen.tsx, placed after <TodayNoticings /> as a standalone block. No logic change.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Pure render relocation.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Snapshot DumpScreen: NotifyPrimeLine is outside the input component tree.

mergedFindings.title: GoalCreateModal missing keyboard focus trap — Tab key escapes modal into background DumpScreen
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/modules/goals/GoalCreateModal.tsx lines 99-101: cardRef.current.focus() moves focus into the card on mount, but no Tab/Shift-Tab keydown guard, no inert on siblings, and no focus-trap library is used. Card has role=dialog + aria-modal=true. Grep for 'trap', 'inert', 'Tab keydown' in GoalCreateModal.tsx returns no relevant hits.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Keyboard users (common on desktop Tauri build) can Tab out of the modal into the background, making background elements operable while the frozen backdrop is in place. WCAG 2.1 §2.1.2 violation. Also affects DeleteConfirmOverlay and LowMoodGateOverlay in GoalsBox.tsx lines 327-397.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add onKeyDown handler on the dialog div that intercepts Tab/Shift-Tab and cycles focus among focusable children. Or add `inert` attribute to layout root while modal is open.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Scoped to GoalCreateModal.tsx and the two overlays in GoalsBox.tsx.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: JSDOM: Tab from last focusable element wraps to first; Shift-Tab from first wraps to last.

mergedFindings.title: Dark mode force-locked to light in main.tsx — token infrastructure exists but pinned off; hardcoded rgba shadows will break when unlocked
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/main.tsx line 94: `<ThemeProvider forceMode="light">`. Dark palette defined in apps/native/src/theme/tokens.ts line 83 (darkPalette). useMode() subscribes to prefers-color-scheme. Hardcoded rgba neumorphic shadows in TodoScreen.tsx lines 393-394, TabBar.tsx line 132, and others do not read from token CSS variables.
mergedFindings.userImpact: iOS dark mode users (common for night use) get a bright cream screen. Health app used at night for sleep logging — bright screen defeats the purpose. The ADHD demographic frequently uses dark mode.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Step 1: audit and replace all hardcoded rgba shadow values in TodoScreen.tsx, TabBar.tsx, ChoresBox.tsx, GoalsBox.tsx with CSS custom property equivalents. Step 2: remove forceMode='light' from main.tsx. The token layer is ready; the component-level hardcodes are the blocker. (Per project memory, this is deferred to Faz 6b — flag as known deferred, not ignored.)
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium. Removing the forceMode pin without the shadow audit first will expose broken neumorphic shadows.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Visual regression: key screens in dark mode. Token test: buildTokens('dark') returns distinct cream/ink values.
mergedFindings.dissent: Rounds 1-3 all confirm. Round 1 did not list as a top finding. Round 3 noted it is actively deferred per UI plan (Faz 6b). Kept as P3 confirmed with note that forceMode pin is a blocker — not a bug to ignore.

mergedFindings.title: Clerk SignIn rendered with default Clerk styles — breaks olive-neumorphic visual language on first-impression screen
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/main.tsx line 86: `<SignIn routing='hash' signUpUrl='#/sign-up' />` — raw Clerk default component with no appearance prop. Renders Clerk's own blue-button, white-card styles. First screen every unauthenticated user sees.
mergedFindings.userImpact: First impression of Ollie is a generic blue-branded auth form that clashes with the cream/sage/neumorphic product identity established after login. Breaks product coherence at the most critical conversion moment.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add Clerk appearance prop: `appearance={{ variables: { colorPrimary: '#4A5E4C', colorBackground: '#FAFAF7' } }}`. Full custom UI via useSignIn() is cleaner but higher effort.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for appearance prop; medium for full custom UI.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Visual test: SignInGate uses Clerk appearance config with olive/cream tokens.

mergedFindings.title: No onboarding — 'Brain' module (TodayNoticings) has no navigable route — users cannot browse their AI noticings
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/Router.tsx: no /box/brain route. TodayNoticings is embedded in DumpScreen only. moduleManifest.ts has no brain entry. The brain module's output (noticings) is surfaced only on the home screen and is null-rendered when empty.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Users cannot navigate to a dedicated view of their AI noticings. For a product that promises an observant AI life assistant, the assistant's observations have no permanent home — they only flash on the home screen and disappear.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Either add a /box/brain placeholder screen that renders TodayNoticings with history, or explicitly document that noticings are home-screen-only and ephemeral (product decision). If intentional, add a brief copy note to the home screen so users know this is by design.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low if additive route. Product decision needed on whether persistent noticings history is v1 scope.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: If route added: navigation smoke test renders TodayNoticings at /box/brain.

implementationRuntimeMismatches: prefers-reduced-motion: Rounds 2 and 3 mark ack animation as 'correctly implemented' in doNotTouch; Round 1 correctly identifies that opacity:1 with animation-duration:0ms still produces a 2.5s solid-colour viewport block for reduced-motion users — the CSS intent (no animation) is achieved but the UX outcome (no jarring colour flood) is not.

Mood module reachability: Round 2 flags MoodBox as P2 unreachable. HealthRoom.tsx comment (line 353) says 'there's no mood screen' and the energy tile is explicitly READ-ONLY by design. Whether this is a product decision or an omission is unresolved — needs product verification before treating as a bug.

GoalCreateModal 5-field requirement: Rounds 1 and 2 flag as P2 ADHD blocker. Project memory (project_ollie_goals_rich_capture.md) records this as a deliberate design decision (required fields at creation for Ulysses-contract integrity). The bug vs feature status is a product call, but the UX impact on ADHD users is real regardless of intent.
quickWins: DumpScreen.tsx:264 — replace 'good evening' with 5-line getGreeting() helper — zero risk, instant credibility fix
HealthRoom.tsx:198 — change second 'last night' to 'tap to log' — one string, zero risk
BrainDumpInput.tsx:378 — hide 'cmd + enter' hint on touch via @media (hover: none) { display: none } — one CSS rule
Router.tsx + HouseholdRoom.tsx — add 'pets' to ROOMED_IDS and a Pets tile in HouseholdRoom — ~4 lines total, removes orphan section
main.tsx:86 — add Clerk appearance prop with cream/sage tokens to SignInGate — 5 lines, no logic change
topRisks: No onboarding: first-time alpha users hit a blank textarea with no mental model — highest churn risk at alpha launch
GoalCreateModal 5 required fields (including undefined jargon): ADHD users triggered by casual dump will abandon goal creation before saving — undermines the product's core retention mechanic
Migration failure silent infinite loading: if SQLite fails, entire module becomes permanently inaccessible with no signal or recovery — data trust destroyed silently
NeedsConfirmCard snake_case labels: every grey-zone routing surfaces developer jargon in the highest-trust confirmation moment

angle: Agent 11 — Design System & Frontend Code Quality
angleSummary: The olive-neumorphic design system has two structural blockers before Faz 6b (dark mode) can ship: (1) 40+ production files import the static `colors = lightPalette` alias instead of the reactive theme hook, and (2) all neumorphic shadow tokens hardcode white highlight values. Beyond dark mode, the Input primitive is silently unstyled due to ~14 undefined CSS variable names, DM Sans 300 weight is never loaded, and the type scale is bypassed by 139–158 raw fontSize integers across modules. Deduplication and copy-paste drift are pervasive: SMCP/kicker styles exist in 5–13 independent copies with diverging letterSpacing values, and the inset shadow string is duplicated 13–15 times with three different blur radii. Quick wins exist (paper-2 CSS var typo, App.css dead-code deletion, font weight import) that are single-line or near-zero risk.

mergedFindings.title: 40+ production files import static `colors = lightPalette` alias — dark mode is architecturally impossible without mass refactor
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/theme/tokens.ts:116 exports `export const colors = lightPalette` — a static object, not reactive. R2 confirmed 40 non-test TSX files import this alias (grep `import.*colors\b`). R3 confirmed the same count. apps/native/src/layout/Box.tsx:10 does the same import for the layout primitive. ThemeProvider.tsx is the ONLY file calling `useTheme()`/`useTokens()` — confirmed zero hits in src/ outside the definition. R2 additionally found apps/native/src/main.tsx:94 has `<ThemeProvider forceMode="light">` hardcoded, so dark mode is also gated at the entry point.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any OS or user-triggered dark mode switch leaves every module's inline background colors, ink colors, and shadow colors frozen to light olive-sage values. CSS-var-driven elements (Text.module.css, global.css, Button.module.css) do update — creating a split-render state where card backgrounds stay cream/sage while text turns dark-mode cream. Visually broken. Faz 6b cannot ship without this fix.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Step 1: Remove `forceMode="light"` from main.tsx (R2). Step 2: In each of the 40 files, replace `import { colors } from '../theme/tokens'` with `const { tokens: { palette: colors } } = useTheme()` inside the component function. Step 3: Fix Box.tsx to consume the active palette via context or CSS vars rather than a static import.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — mechanical replacement across 40+ files; safest done module-by-module with a feature flag. Missing one file leaves a partial-dark regression.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Render any module inside `<ThemeProvider forceMode='dark'>` and assert computed backgroundColor on a card element matches darkPalette value, not lightPalette.cream. Also assert `data-theme` attribute on html is 'dark'.
mergedFindings.dissent: R1 focused only on the static import pattern and did not surface the `forceMode='light'` lock in main.tsx. R2 and R3 both found the `forceMode` entry-point lock as an additional layer. No disagreement on severity.

mergedFindings.title: Input.module.css references ~14 CSS custom property names that do not exist in the token system — Input renders with zero design styling
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/ui/Input.module.css uses: --ollie-space-xs, --ollie-size-body, --ollie-weight-normal, --ollie-ink-dark, --ollie-ceramic-dim, --ollie-leading (bare), --ollie-space-sm, --ollie-duration-fast, --ollie-easing-standard, --ollie-ink-light, --ollie-sage (bare), --ollie-error-border, --ollie-error-text, --ollie-size-caption, --ollie-tracking-wide. None are emitted by `tokensToCssVars()` in tokens.ts:385–396. Correct names (R1 verified via writeGroup() calls): --ollie-space-1, --ollie-text-body, --ollie-weight-regular, --ollie-color-ink, --ollie-color-hairline, --ollie-leading-body, --ollie-duration-fade, --ollie-ease-calm-out, --ollie-color-ink-ghost, --ollie-color-sage, --ollie-color-rubric, --ollie-text-caption, --ollie-tracking-caps. Input is consumed by GoalCreateModal.tsx:32 and WorkBox.tsx:34.
mergedFindings.userImpact: All text inputs in Goals (create modal) and Work module render with fallback browser styles: no editorial typography, wrong colors, no neumorphic border, no error state visual feedback. Silent failure — no build or runtime error.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Rename every --ollie-* var in Input.module.css to the correct generated name using the camelToKebab transform as reference. Pure CSS rename, no token changes needed.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — pure CSS file, no runtime logic. Validate visually in DevTools after fix.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Mount Input, query computed style of the .input element, assert border-bottom is not 'none' and color is not default black.

mergedFindings.title: All neumorphic shadow tokens hardcode `rgba(255,255,255,0.70–0.85)` white highlight — will render as bright white glow on dark surfaces
mergedFindings.evidence: tokens.ts:245–252 — ALL shadow values (raised, raisedSm, inset, card) hardcode rgba(255,255,255,0.70) as the highlight side. tokens.ts comment at lines 233–235 acknowledges: 'if you need dark-aware shadow, switch to rgba(var(--ollie-color-shadow)...)'. darkPalette.shadow='0,0,0' (line 112) is exported but the shadows object has no dark counterpart and Box.tsx resolves from the single static shadows object. R1 independently noted 16 hardcoded white highlight values in modules (rgba(255,255,255,0.70|0.78|0.85)).
mergedFindings.userImpact: When Faz 6b dark mode ships, all neumorphic cards will show a bright white halo on dark backgrounds — the inverse of the intended depth effect. Neumorphic light source on dark requires a lighter-shade-of-surface highlight, not white.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a `darkShadows` object to tokens.ts using `rgba(55,65,55,0.90)` as the highlight side (adapting the existing `shadow: '0,0,0'` dark palette entry). Convert shadow CSS values to CSS custom properties so `[data-theme='dark']` can override them. Requires coordinating with the forceMode/static-colors fix (finding #1) since Box.tsx must consume the active token bundle.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — shadow token is consumed in 20+ places; must coordinate with the dark mode refactor.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Visual regression snapshot of a card component in dark mode asserting highlight side of box-shadow is not white.
mergedFindings.dissent: R1 flagged the white highlight values as part of the dark mode structural breakage but categorized it under the inline shadow duplication finding rather than as a separate token-level issue. R2 and R3 elevated it to an independent finding. Agreed on severity impact.

mergedFindings.title: fontWeight 300 (light) used at 8+ call sites but @fontsource/dm-sans 300 weight is never loaded — silently falls back to 400
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/main.tsx:11–13 imports @fontsource/dm-sans/400, 500, 700 only — no 300. fontWeights.light = 300 in tokens.ts:150. Used at: body/BodyBox.tsx:284+295, chores/ChoresBox.tsx:429, sleep/SleepBox.tsx:181+201, admin/AdminBox.tsx:330+375, grocery/GroceryBox.tsx:1309, ui/Input.module.css:36 (--ollie-weight-light). Browser silently substitutes 400.
mergedFindings.userImpact: All text intended to render lighter (sleep figure, chore metadata, admin labels, grocery items, input placeholder) renders at normal weight instead, losing the intended visual hierarchy.

mergedFindings.title: Button.module.css references `--ollie-color-paper-2` but token generator emits `--ollie-color-paper2` (no hyphen) — secondary and ghost button active states are transparently broken

mergedFindings.title: SMCP kicker style copy-pasted into 5 room files + 8 modules (13 total) with diverging letterSpacing values — no shared source of truth

R1 framed the neumorphic white shadow issue as part of the inline duplication finding (P2); R2 and R3 elevated it to a standalone structural problem (P1-adjacent) because it affects the shadow token definitions themselves, not just inline copies. Merged as separate P1 finding.

angleSummary: The test suite has solid unit coverage in isolated domains (crypto, sync LWW, crisis-lexicon, dump-classifier) but has three structural CI holes that let regressions ship silently: (1) deploy-workers.yml fires to production in parallel with ci.yml with no blocking dependency, (2) coverage thresholds in orchestrator/vitest.config.ts are never executed in CI, and (3) the client-side crisis safety wiring is untested end-to-end. Beyond CI structure, the partner module (consent/interpret/pairing routes) and brain/actions.ts action dispatch are almost entirely untested despite being privacy-sensitive and user-trust-critical flows.

mergedFindings.title: deploy-workers.yml deploys workers to production with no test gate — ci.yml and deploy run in parallel
mergedFindings.evidence: /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/.github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml — four deploy jobs (ai-proxy, cron, apns-push, sentry-tunnel), none have a `needs:` field referencing the ci.yml build job. Both workflows trigger on push to main simultaneously. Round 1 did not surface this directly but noted --passWithNoTests masking; Rounds 2 and 3 both confirmed by direct file inspection.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A breaking regression in ai-proxy (rate-limit, auth, crisis routing) or apns-push reaches all users in production even while CI tests are still running or have already failed. The existing test suite would catch the regression — it just never gets a chance to block the deploy.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Any logic regression in any worker ships to production silently.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `needs: [build]` (or a reusable `test` job) to each deploy job in deploy-workers.yml. Alternatively merge into a single workflow with sequential jobs. The fix is a CI-config-only change — zero product code touched.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: None — additive CI constraint. May surface that tests were already failing on recent pushes.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: No new tests required; wire existing worker tests as a prerequisite gate.

mergedFindings.title: Coverage thresholds in packages/orchestrator/vitest.config.ts are never enforced — `pnpm test` skips --coverage entirely
mergedFindings.evidence: /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/packages/orchestrator/vitest.config.ts lines 10-20 defines thresholds (statements:78, branches:55, functions:90, lines:78). Root package.json `test` script runs `pnpm -r test` → each package's `vitest run` (no --coverage). No `test:coverage` script exists in orchestrator/package.json or any other package.json. .github/workflows/ci.yml only calls `pnpm test`. The config comment reads '`pnpm test:coverage` runs the v8 provider in CI' — but that script does not exist. All three rounds confirmed independently by tracing the script chain.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Coverage can silently drop to 0% without breaking CI. The ratchet added as a post-audit safeguard (memory: ollie deep audit 2026-06-18) provides zero protection. Developers and Serra have false confidence that the floor is held.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `"test:coverage": "vitest run --coverage"` to /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/packages/orchestrator/package.json. Add one CI step in ci.yml: `pnpm --filter orchestrator test:coverage`. Verify @vitest/coverage-v8 is in devDependencies.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. CI may initially fail if current coverage is already below the 55% branch threshold — if so, adjust threshold to match reality before tightening.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None — wiring fix only. Run coverage locally first to verify current numbers.

implementationRuntimeMismatches: Partner consent filtering: interpret.ts is code-confirmed as the consent gate, but zero tests exist — there is no runtime verification that the flags default to 'no share' rather than 'share'. If the default is inverted (share-by-default), a runtime user would expose data without knowing it, but CI would never surface this.

Rate-limit key extraction: tests run with JWT enforcement disabled (T0_JWT_ENFORCED='0') while production runs with it enabled. The two code paths produce different rate-key sources (JWT sub vs x-user-id header). A bug in the JWT path is invisible to the test suite.

Coverage thresholds: vitest.config.ts documents thresholds as 'enforced in CI' but the script chain proves they never run. The comment and reality are inverted — teams reading the config believe coverage is gated when it is not.

deploy-workers.yml: the intent (test before deploy) is implied by having tests at all, but the implementation deploys concurrently with testing. Any developer who pushes a breaking change to main assumes tests would block the deploy — they do not.
quickWins: Remove --passWithNoTests from apps/api/package.json — one-word deletion, immediately forces CI to fail if the APNs test files are absent.
Add `needs: [build]` to each deploy job in deploy-workers.yml — 15-minute CI config change, blocks broken workers from reaching production.
Add `"test:coverage": "vitest run --coverage"` to packages/orchestrator/package.json and one CI step — enforces the thresholds that were already written but are currently dead.
Add apps/native/src/modules/partner/interpret.test.ts (~30 minutes, ~50 lines) — pure functions, no mocks needed, covers crisis + consent + go-dark paths that are privacy-critical.
topRisks: Workers deploy to production in parallel with (not after) the test run — a breaking ai-proxy or apns-push regression ships to all users before tests have a chance to catch it (confirmed in all 3 rounds).
Partner consent-flag logic in interpret.ts is completely untested — a wrong default could expose cycle/mood to a partner without consent; this is a privacy P0 at runtime that CI would never surface.
Client-side crisis safety wiring (server crisis response → onCrisis → CrisisBanner) is untested — a refactor could make a user in crisis receive a silent no-op with zero CI signal.
Coverage thresholds are documented as a CI gate but are dead config — the codebase may already be below the 55% branch floor with no one aware.

angleSummary: The Ollie monorepo has a two-tier CI blind spot: CF workers deploy to production without any quality gate, and the entire Rust/Tauri codebase is never compiled in CI. The banned-phrase scanner is hollow (scans ghost paths, misses 281+ active UI files). CSP is disabled in the production Tauri config. Three independent rounds converged on 5 of the 12 findings with confidence 3, and all major findings are corroborated by at least 2 rounds.
implementationRuntimeMismatches: tauri-plugin-localhost on iOS: Cargo.toml and lib.rs show unconditional initialization (Round 2 suspected, Round 3 did not flag it, Round 1 did not flag it). iOS build artifacts in Cargo.lock suggest it compiles, but runtime behavior of a TCP localhost server inside an iOS app process is unverified. Flagged as suspected by Round 2 only — needs device smoke-test.

ESLint no-banned-copy rule: Round 1 says it covers apps/native (mitigating the scanner gap); Round 2 confirms this; Round 3 confirms but notes JSON files are not covered by ESLint. All three agree ESLint is the real guard, but no round verified pnpm lint passes cleanly today — it has never been runtime-verified in CI output.

gen/apple committed to git: Round 2 flagged this as P3; Rounds 1 and 3 both note gen/apple in doNotTouch as intentionally committed for Xcode workflow. Dissent: Round 2 argues it should be gitignored (auto-generated), but Round 3 says it is committed intentionally. Needs product decision on whether gen/apple is hand-edited.

mergedFindings.title: CF workers deploy to production with zero quality gate (no needs: build, no typecheck, no test)
mergedFindings.evidence: /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/.github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml — all four deploy jobs (ai-proxy, cron, apns-push, sentry-tunnel) run only checkout + pnpm install + wrangler deploy. No `needs:` dependency on the build/test CI job. No typecheck or test step. Fires independently on any push to main touching workers/.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A TypeScript type error or runtime bug in ai-proxy (AI routing), apns-push (push notifications), or cron ships live to Cloudflare Workers immediately, breaking core features for all users with no automated detection.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Workers each have `typecheck` and `test` scripts in package.json that are never called by the deploy workflow. ci.yml and deploy-workers.yml are sibling workflows with no ordering or dependency relationship.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `needs: [build]` to each deploy job in deploy-workers.yml. Also add an explicit typecheck step per worker (or a shared job: `pnpm -r --filter './workers/**' typecheck && pnpm -r --filter './workers/**' test`) before wrangler deploy.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — purely additive CI config change.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Workers already have test scripts. Wire them into the deploy gate. Add a CI integration check: introduce a deliberate type error in a worker and confirm deploy is blocked.

mergedFindings.title: scan-banned-phrases.cjs SCAN_DIRS contain 3 phantom paths and omit all 281+ active UI files in apps/native/src
mergedFindings.evidence: tools/scan-banned-phrases.cjs lines 48-57: SCAN_DIRS includes apps/web/src, apps/desktop/src, packages/router/src — all deleted/non-existent. apps/native/src (281-291 active TS/TSX files) is entirely absent. Scanner silently skips missing dirs (existsSync guard). CI voice-library-guard job and the pretest hook both run this scanner and report a false green. Round 3 verified: `node tools/scan-banned-phrases.cjs` scans only 210 files from 5 package paths.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Banned shame/engagement copy (streaks, 'great job', 'we miss you', ADHD-shame patterns) in any of the 281 apps/native/src UI files — the entire rendered app surface — passes the scanner silently. ESLint no-banned-copy is the only real guard, but it is a separate CI step not in pretest.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: The standalone scanner and the pretest hook provide false confidence. Approximately 57% of the active codebase is unscanned. JSON string literals (crisis lexicon, future i18n) are also unchecked because the JSON-walking branch of the scanner points to ghost i18n dirs.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace stale paths in SCAN_DIRS with: ['apps/native/src', 'workers/ai-proxy/src', 'workers/apns-push/src', 'workers/cron/src', 'packages/logic/src', 'packages/orchestrator/src', 'packages/events/src', 'packages/store/src', 'packages/api/src']. Remove the three non-existent paths.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — may surface existing violations that then need fixing.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add an assertion in tools/banned-phrases.test.cjs that listFiles() returns at least one file from apps/native/src, to catch future path rot.

mergedFindings.title: Rust/Tauri source has zero CI coverage — cargo check/clippy never runs
mergedFindings.evidence: /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/.github/workflows/ci.yml — no cargo, rust, or Tauri step exists (grep confirmed by Round 3). CI runs only pnpm typecheck → pnpm lint → pnpm test. apps/native/src-tauri/src/ contains lib.rs, main.rs, local_notifications.rs, calendar.rs, group_container.rs — none compiled in CI.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A Rust compile error in any src-tauri file (notifications, calendar access, App Group writes) passes all CI checks and only fails when someone locally runs `tauri build` or attempts a TestFlight release — blocking release at the worst moment.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: cargo check is lightweight (type resolution only, no full compilation). macOS runners are available on GitHub Actions at ~$0.08/min; a cargo check job runs in ~2 minutes. Alternatively, `cargo check` without objc2 features can run on ubuntu-latest with cross-compilation flags.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a `rust-check` job to ci.yml using `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` that runs `cargo check --manifest-path apps/native/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`. Optionally add `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`. Use `actions/cache` for the Rust target cache.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — additive CI job. macOS runner cost is ~$0.16 per push to main.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: The cargo check job itself is the gate. Any new Rust IPC command should have a basic integration test via Tauri test harness.

mergedFindings.title: CSP is null in tauri.conf.json — Tauri capability allowlist is the only XSS barrier
mergedFindings.evidence: /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/apps/native/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json line 24: `"csp": null`. Capability file capabilities/default.json grants sql:allow-execute, sql:allow-load, sql:allow-select, store:allow-set, notification:allow-notify, deep-link:default to remote.urls: ["http://localhost:9527"]. With CSP null, any injected script at localhost:9527 has full SQL read/write on all user data.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If any XSS vector exists (malicious npm dependency, compromised server response), an attacker gets full SQLite access (all user data), can write to the app store, send arbitrary notifications, and trigger deep-link navigation. For a closed-alpha native app the immediate risk is low, but the gap is unacceptable before public launch.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Tauri's defence-in-depth model assumes CSP + capability allowlist together. With CSP null, the allowlist is the sole barrier. The null was likely set to unblock Clerk (which loads from clerk.accounts.dev); the fix requires allowlisting Clerk/Supabase domains surgically.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Set `"csp": "default-src 'self' http://localhost:9527; script-src 'self'; connect-src https://*.supabase.co https://clerk.com https://api.clerk.dev https://*.clerk.accounts.dev; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'"` in tauri.conf.json. Test Clerk OAuth, Supabase calls, and CF worker calls after applying.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — inline styles in React component libraries may need 'unsafe-inline' in style-src. Requires thorough smoke-test of auth and data flows.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: E2E smoke test: assert Content-Security-Policy header is present and non-null on the served app page after sign-in.

mergedFindings.title: ai-proxy and cron worker test files (38 total) excluded from typecheck via tsconfig include
mergedFindings.evidence: /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/workers/ai-proxy/tsconfig.json: `"include": ["src"]` — 34 test files under workers/ai-proxy/tests/ omitted. /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/workers/cron/tsconfig.json: same pattern, 4 test files omitted. apns-push and sentry-tunnel correctly include ["src", "tests"].
mergedFindings.userImpact: Type errors in ai-proxy test files (the most complex worker, 34 test files) are invisible to pnpm typecheck in CI. Wrong test assertions and broken test helpers compile silently.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: pnpm -r typecheck skips tests/ for ai-proxy and cron. Type drift between worker source and tests goes undetected until test runtime. Especially risky given ai-proxy handles all AI routing.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In workers/ai-proxy/tsconfig.json and workers/cron/tsconfig.json, change `"include": ["src"]` to `"include": ["src", "tests"]`. Match the apns-push pattern.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — may surface pre-existing type errors in test files that need fixing.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None needed — the fix itself makes typecheck cover the gap.

mergedFindings.title: apps/native tsconfig.json does not extend tsconfig.base.json — ES target and strictness diverged
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/tsconfig.json has no `extends` field (confirmed by all three rounds). tsconfig.base.json sets target: ES2022; apps/native sets target: ES2020. apps/native adds noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters which are absent from base. All 16 packages and 3 of 4 workers correctly extend base.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Silent target drift: native app compiles to ES2020 output while all shared packages compile to ES2022. ES2022-only syntax (Array.at(), Object.hasOwn) used in a package typecheck-passes but may fail at runtime on older WebViews. Future tsconfig.base.json tightening does not propagate to the app.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Stricter noUnusedLocals/Parameters apply only in apps/native, not in the 16 shared packages, allowing dead code to accumulate silently in package-layer code. ES version mismatch makes tsconfig-dependent tooling harder to share.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `"extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json"` to apps/native/tsconfig.json. Remove fields already defined in base. Keep app-specific overrides (noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, allowImportingTsExtensions, useDefineForClassFields). Set target to ES2022 to match base.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low-medium — may surface previously hidden type errors masked by the ES2020 target. Run `pnpm --filter native typecheck` after change to assess.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Run `pnpm --filter native typecheck` after the change and confirm no new errors beyond expected ES2022 surface.

mergedFindings.title: Tauri devtools feature enabled unconditionally in Cargo.toml — WebKit inspector accessible in production builds
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src-tauri/Cargo.toml line 21: `tauri = { version = "2", features = ["devtools"] }`. No cfg(debug_assertions) guard. lib.rs uses no devtools API directly — the feature declaration alone enables the right-click WebKit inspector in shipped .app/.ipa binaries.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any user who right-clicks inside the Ollie window on macOS gets a full WebKit inspector. The inspector can read DOM, localStorage, cookies, and network traffic including Clerk session tokens. Acceptable for a trusted closed alpha; unacceptable before public launch.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Cargo feature flags are compile-time. Removing the feature from the production dependency eliminates the inspector entirely from release binaries.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Remove `"devtools"` from the tauri features list in Cargo.toml. To retain it in dev builds, use a Cargo feature: add `[features] devtools = ["tauri/devtools"]` and enable only via `--features devtools` in dev scripts.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — removing devtools from production has no functional impact on shipping features.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Verify by building a release binary and confirming right-click inspector is absent.

mergedFindings.title: tauri-plugin-localhost initialized unconditionally on iOS — may break iOS launch or fail App Store review
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src-tauri/Cargo.toml: `tauri-plugin-localhost = "2"` in [dependencies] with no `[target.'cfg(not(mobile))'.dependencies]` guard. lib.rs line 27: `.plugin(tauri_plugin_localhost::Builder::new(LOCALHOST_PORT).build())` called unconditionally inside run(). Cargo.lock shows aarch64-apple-ios targets built, so it compiles — but runtime behavior of a TCP localhost server inside an iOS app process is unverified.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If the plugin's TCP server is non-functional or App Store review flags a localhost TCP listener, the iOS build path fails or is rejected. The localhost plugin is architecturally desktop-centric.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Round 3 did not flag this; Rounds 1 and 3 both note the localhost:9527 setup as intentional (required for Clerk http:// origin). The concern is mobile-specific runtime behavior, not the desktop use case.
mergedFindings.dissent: Round 2 flagged this as suspected P2. Rounds 1 and 3 explicitly list the localhost plugin in doNotTouch as intentional. The iOS Cargo.lock artifacts suggest it compiles on aarch64-apple-ios. Runtime risk on actual device is unverified — needs a device smoke-test to resolve.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Wrap the localhost plugin registration in `#[cfg(not(mobile))]` in lib.rs and verify the iOS app's window URL strategy for the mobile path (may need tauri://localhost or file:// scheme instead of TCP server).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — needs iOS smoke test after gating. The Clerk http:// origin requirement may need a separate iOS workaround.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Run an iOS device build with the cfg(not(mobile)) guard and confirm app launches and Clerk login works on iPhone.

mergedFindings.title: scan-banned-json.cjs is dead tooling — scans deleted apps/web/src/i18n, not wired to CI or pretest
mergedFindings.evidence: tools/scan-banned-json.cjs line 28: `const I18N_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'apps/web/src/i18n')` — apps/web is deleted. The script has zero references in package.json, ci.yml, or pretest hook (grep returns nothing outside the file itself).
mergedFindings.userImpact: No active JSON string scanning. apps/native has no i18n JSON files currently, so immediate risk is low. If locale strings are added to a new location they will not be scanned.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Dead tooling adds maintenance confusion. The JSON coverage gap it was meant to fill (banned copy in JSON data files, crisis lexicon) is currently unaddressed.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Delete the file — it does nothing. If JSON scanning is needed later, update I18N_DIR to apps/native/src/i18n and wire into pretest.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None.

mergedFindings.title: gen/apple (Tauri-generated iOS Xcode files) committed to git without clear intentionality signal
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 2: `git ls-files apps/native/src-tauri/gen/` returns 33+ tracked files under gen/apple/ including Assets.xcassets icon sets, Xcode project stubs, Info.plist. apps/native/src-tauri/.gitignore only ignores /gen/schemas, not /gen/apple.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Repo bloat and potential merge conflicts when `tauri ios init` regenerates different content. May mislead contributors into editing generated files directly.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Some teams intentionally commit gen/apple when they have manual Xcode customizations (entitlements, signing, capabilities). Round 3 explicitly lists gen/ in doNotTouch as committed intentionally for Xcode workflow.
mergedFindings.dissent: Round 2 says these should be gitignored (auto-generated). Round 3 says they are intentionally committed. This is a product/workflow decision — if gen/apple has no hand-edits, gitignore it; if it has customized entitlements or signing config, keep it tracked.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Diff gen/apple against a fresh `tauri ios init` output. If no manual edits exist, add /gen/apple to apps/native/src-tauri/.gitignore and `git rm -r --cached apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple`.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low if no manual edits. Medium if Xcode project settings have been hand-edited there.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None.

mergedFindings.title: packages/* tsconfigs missing noUnusedLocals / noUnusedParameters — dead code accumulates silently in shared logic
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/tsconfig.json has `"noUnusedLocals": true, "noUnusedParameters": true`. tsconfig.base.json (extended by all 16 packages) does NOT include these flags. packages/logic, packages/notifications, packages/orchestrator, packages/auth tsconfigs all extend base without override.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Dead code accumulates silently in the core AI/brain wiring (packages/orchestrator, packages/logic) without compile-time warning. The ESLint @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars rule is only 'warn' so it won't block CI.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Unused exports and dead parameter paths in shared packages are never flagged by typecheck. Especially risky in high-churn orchestrator and logic packages.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `"noUnusedLocals": true, "noUnusedParameters": true` to tsconfig.base.json. Expect some violations to surface and fix them. Alternatively, add per-package override to high-churn packages first (orchestrator, logic).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — will surface existing unused symbols across 16 packages that need cleanup.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None needed — pnpm typecheck becomes the gate after the change.

mergedFindings.title: TypeScript version split: apps/native on ~5.8.3, packages on ^5.6.0, typescript-eslint peer resolves 5.9.3
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/package.json: `"typescript": "~5.8.3"`. All packages/* and workers/* package.json: `"typescript": "^5.6.0"`. pnpm-lock.yaml shows two resolved versions: typescript@5.8.3 and typescript@5.9.3 (pulled in by typescript-eslint peer resolution). Three TS versions active in the same monorepo.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Unlikely to cause user-visible bugs today, but TS minor versions occasionally tighten type checking — a module that passes under 5.9.3 (ESLint) might fail under 5.8.3 (native app) or vice versa, causing silent divergence.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: pnpm workspace hoisting means packages can get different TS instances. `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` results can diverge in subtle ways.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Pin TypeScript to a single version across the monorepo. Choose the highest in use (5.9.3 or current stable) and update all package.json devDependencies. Add a pnpm catalog entry for it.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — TS minor upgrades are generally backward-compatible.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Run `pnpm typecheck` after version unification to catch any newly surfaced type errors.

mergedFindings.title: eslint.config.mjs ignores all *.config.{js,mjs,cjs,ts} files — blanket pattern excludes future feature files named *.config.ts
mergedFindings.evidence: eslint.config.mjs line 32: `'**/*.config.{js,mjs,cjs,ts}'` in global ignores. Excludes apps/native/vite.config.ts and any future *.config.ts files from all ESLint rules including no-banned-copy and react-hooks checks.
mergedFindings.userImpact: None currently — vite.config.ts (32 lines, no user-facing strings) is low risk. But any future feature code accidentally named *.config.ts would be silently unguarded.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Overly broad ignore pattern. Intent was to exclude tooling configs (wrangler, eslint itself). A narrower pattern preserves the intent.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace `'**/*.config.{js,mjs,cjs,ts}'` with explicit named patterns: `'**/vite.config.*', '**/eslint.config.*', '**/wrangler.config.*', '**/vitest.config.*'`.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low.

mergedFindings.title: No Prettier config — code formatting entirely unenforced across 16 packages and 4 workers
mergedFindings.evidence: No .prettierrc*, prettier.config.*, or prettier entry in root package.json scripts found. ESLint config has no prettier integration. Confirmed by checking /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/ root.
mergedFindings.userImpact: No user-facing impact. Developer experience degrades as team grows — inconsistent indentation, quote styles, trailing commas across packages; PR diffs become noisy.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Style divergence across 16 packages and 4 workers. Becomes a friction point when adding contributors.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a root .prettierrc.json with `{"singleQuote": true, "semi": true, "trailingComma": "all", "printWidth": 100}` and add `"format": "prettier --write '**/*.{ts,tsx,js,json}'"` to root package.json scripts. Add `prettier --check` to CI. Add eslint-config-prettier to suppress conflicting ESLint style rules.

mergedFindings.title: Default Tauri greet() IPC command left in production invoke_handler — undocumented IPC endpoint
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src-tauri/src/lib.rs lines 14-16 and 49: verbatim Tauri scaffold `fn greet(name: &str)` registered in `generate_handler![greet, ...]`. No TypeScript code calls `invoke('greet')`.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Negligible functional impact. Increases attack surface by one unauthenticated IPC string-echo endpoint. Misleads contributors about what IPC commands are real.

mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Delete the `greet` function and remove it from the `generate_handler!` list in lib.rs (4-line deletion).

Entire Rust/Tauri codebase (lib.rs, local_notifications.rs, calendar.rs, group_container.rs) has zero CI coverage — compile errors only surface during local tauri build or at TestFlight release time

Replace stale SCAN_DIRS in tools/scan-banned-phrases.cjs: remove apps/web/src, apps/desktop/src, packages/router/src; add apps/native/src (5-line edit, zero risk)

Remove `"devtools"` from Cargo.toml tauri features list (3-word deletion) — eliminates WebKit inspector in production builds
Delete tools/scan-banned-json.cjs (dead file, does nothing, zero risk)
