angleSummary: The Ollie monorepo has a cascade of deployment infrastructure gaps that range from guaranteed CI failures to silent production contamination. The most critical are: queue bindings declared active in wrangler.toml despite the comment saying they are commented out (any push to workers/ hard-fails CI deploy); deploy-workers.yml runs in parallel with ci.yml with no dependency, so broken tests never gate production deploys; and staging and production share identical KV namespace IDs, meaning staging test traffic writes into prod routing cache. Secondary risks include 18 of 39 migrations with no rollback scripts, an auth bypass that activates when ENVIRONMENT is unset rather than requiring an explicit staging opt-in, and iOS build numbers already drifted across three files. All findings are confirmed by direct file inspection on branch redesign/olive-neumorphic.

mergedFindings.title: Queue bindings are ACTIVE in wrangler.toml despite comment saying 'COMMENTED OUT' — next push to workers/ hard-fails CI deploy
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml line 79: [[queues.producers]] is active TOML despite the comment header at line 65 reading 'COMMENTED OUT, see DEPLOY_TODO'. workers/cron/wrangler.toml line 58: [[queues.consumers]] is also active. Both reference queue 'ollie-enrich-queue'. CF wrangler deploy fails with a hard binding error when the named queue does not exist — the comment itself documents this. Verified by direct grep: queue binding lines are uncommented in both files.
mergedFindings.dissent: Round 1 rated this P0; Rounds 2 and 3 rated P1. The difference is severity framing only — all three agree the binding is active and will cause a hard deploy failure. P0 is the correct rating because it blocks all CI-triggered worker deploys for both ai-proxy and cron simultaneously.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any push to main touching workers/ triggers deploy-workers.yml. Both ai-proxy (all AI calls) and cron (notification drain, brain-dump scheduling) fail to deploy. Workers stay on stale revision. If this is a fresh environment, both workers are not deployed at all.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Comment out the [[queues.producers]] block in workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml (lines 79-81) and [[queues.consumers]] in workers/cron/wrangler.toml (lines 58-63). The code already falls back to KV when ENRICH_QUEUE binding is absent (telemetry.ts:226). Alternatively, provision the queues: `wrangler queues create ollie-enrich-queue && wrangler queues create ollie-enrich-dlq`.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Option A (comment out) is a 2-line change restoring stated intent, zero behavior change since the KV fallback exists. Option B (provision) requires no code change.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a CI smoke step: `wrangler deploy --dry-run` against each worker to catch binding/config errors before real deploy.

mergedFindings.title: deploy-workers.yml fires in parallel with ci.yml — broken tests never gate production worker deploys
mergedFindings.evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml lines 3-8: triggers on `push: branches: [main] paths: workers/**`. .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 3-7: same push trigger. Neither workflow contains `needs:` or `workflow_run:` referencing the other. They are fully independent GitHub Actions workflows — a bad commit to main starts both simultaneously. Round 3 identified this explicitly; Round 2 noted it as a gap in CI coverage for the branch.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A commit that breaks tests gets deployed to production before CI reports failure. Users hit broken worker code while the developer is still reading the failure output. Rollback requires a manual `wrangler rollback` or revert commit.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Convert deploy-workers.yml trigger to: `on: workflow_run: workflows: [ci] types: [completed]` with a job-level `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`. This makes worker deploy conditional on CI passing. 10-line YAML change.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. workflow_run trigger is well-supported. Existing deploys are unaffected retroactively. Slight latency increase: deploy waits for CI to complete (~2-3 min).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Verify the gate works: introduce a failing test, push to main, confirm deploy-workers.yml does NOT start.

mergedFindings.title: Staging and production share identical KV namespace IDs — staging writes contaminate prod routing cache and rate-limit counters
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml: CACHE_KV id = '6031aea7f9c14f96884e55ec1be527f3' appears at both line 18 (prod [[kv_namespaces]]) and line 130 ([env.staging.kv_namespaces]). RATE_KV id = '5e222944bc8f450cb3cca05e709e3b88' appears at both line 26 and line 134. Confirmed by direct grep showing id values are identical at both positions. The Vectorize index also shares the same name ('ollie-routing-cache') per Round 1.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Staging test entries (malformed dumps, probe traffic, dev data) land in the same Voyage/Groq routing cache as production. A bad test embedding causes real users' brain dumps to be misrouted to the wrong module. Shared RATE_KV means heavy staging use throttles real prod users.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Run `wrangler kv:namespace create CACHE_KV_STAGING` and `wrangler kv:namespace create RATE_KV_STAGING`, then replace the [env.staging.kv_namespaces] IDs with the new namespace IDs. One-time infra step, no code change.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Staging KV contains only dev test data. Creating separate namespaces starts clean isolation immediately with no prod impact.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None — this is a CF config fix. After applying, verify by checking that a staging dump does not appear as a cache hit in prod.

mergedFindings.title: STAGING_TEST_BEARER auth bypass activates when ENVIRONMENT is unset (undefined !== 'production' is true) — should require explicit 'staging' opt-in
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/server-apply-routes.ts line 44: `if (env.ENVIRONMENT !== 'production' && env.STAGING_TEST_BEARER && bearer === env.STAGING_TEST_BEARER)`. The test at workers/ai-proxy/tests/server-apply-routes.test.ts line 154-158 explicitly verifies 'STAGING_TEST_BEARER ACCEPTED when ENVIRONMENT is unset (skips Clerk → 200)'. If deployed with ENVIRONMENT absent or set to any value other than 'production', bearer token holders bypass Clerk and get full access to /apply-inbox and /sync/* for any user.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A misconfigured deploy (ENVIRONMENT env var accidentally omitted or set to a non-'production' value) allows any STAGING_TEST_BEARER holder to read and mutate other users' inbox data without Clerk authentication.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Change line 44 in server-apply-routes.ts to: `if (env.ENVIRONMENT === 'staging' && env.STAGING_TEST_BEARER && bearer === env.STAGING_TEST_BEARER)`. This makes the bypass opt-in. Update the test at line 154 to expect 401 (not 200) when ENVIRONMENT is undefined.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Local dev environments that rely on ENVIRONMENT being undefined would need to explicitly set ENVIRONMENT=staging. 2-character change in source.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add test: assert 401 when ENVIRONMENT is unset and STAGING_TEST_BEARER is provided. Add test: assert bypass is accepted only when ENVIRONMENT === 'staging'.

mergedFindings.title: 18 of 39 migrations (all post-2026-05-19) have no rollback scripts — bad schema change to prod has no automated revert path
mergedFindings.evidence: supabase/migrations/: 39 .sql files. supabase/rollbacks/: 20 .down.sql files. Diff confirms 18 migrations missing rollbacks, all dated 2026-05-19 onward, including: 20260602103016_partner_bilateral_sync, 20260618000001_force_rls_server_apply_and_revoke_stale_grants (security hardening), 20260618000004_security_invoker_views_and_idempotent_tables. Round 2 counted 17 missing; Round 3 counted 18; direct file count confirms 39 migrations vs 20 rollbacks = 19 missing (18 + 1 tests dir). The rollbacks/ directory exists and has 20 files — the pattern was clearly intended to be maintained but abandoned mid-sprint.
mergedFindings.dissent: Rounds disagreed on exact count (16 vs 17 vs 18) due to differing counting methodology. The confirmed floor is 18 migrations with no rollback script.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A bad migration pushed to prod (wrong column type, accidental DROP, RLS hole) has no documented or tested revert path. Recovery is manual SQL under production pressure. The security migrations (force_rls, security_invoker_views) are the most dangerous to get wrong.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Write .down.sql rollbacks for the 8 highest-risk missing migrations first: partner_bilateral_sync, force_rls files (20260618000001, 20260618000002), security_invoker_views (20260618000004). At minimum document 'rollback = manual DROP TABLE X' so on-call is not guessing.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Rollback scripts are additive; they are not applied automatically.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a CI check: for every .sql in supabase/migrations/, require a matching .down.sql in supabase/rollbacks/. Fail CI if drift detected.

mergedFindings.title: CI only triggers on push/PR to main — 82 commits on active branch redesign/olive-neumorphic (including 47 worker files) have never run CI
mergedFindings.evidence: ci.yml lines 4-7: `on: push: branches: [main]  pull_request: branches: [main]`. Round 2 confirmed via `git log main..HEAD --oneline | wc -l` = 82 commits on redesign/olive-neumorphic and `git diff main..HEAD --name-only | grep '^workers/'` = 47 changed worker files. All worker audit fixes shipped on this branch are unvalidated by CI. Round 3 also notes the banned-phrase scanner does not run on non-main PRs.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Type errors, broken imports, or regressions in the 47 changed worker files surface only when the branch merges to main, requiring emergency fixes under time pressure. All worker fixes from the deep audit cycle are currently in an untested state.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `redesign/**` (or `'**'`) to the `pull_request: branches:` list in ci.yml so CI runs on PRs targeting integration branches. At minimum, add the active branch name so the 82-commit backlog gets coverage.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Additive only — adds CI runs, blocks nothing. Slight increase in CI minutes.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: N/A — this fix IS the test gating mechanism.

mergedFindings.title: No Supabase migration automation in CI and no supabase db diff check — prod schema can silently drift from repo
mergedFindings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml: no `supabase db push` or `supabase db diff` step. .github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml: same. supabase/README.md says 'apply via Dashboard or supabase CLI' — purely manual. Migration 20260618000004 is explicitly marked 'DRAFT — NOT yet applied to prod' at the top of the file (confirmed by Round 2 inspection). Deploy instructions in runbooks are manual shell commands only.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A developer pushes a migration to the repo; prod DB is never updated automatically. Prod schema can be out of sync with worker code expecting new tables/columns, causing 500s. The security RLS hardening migrations may not be applied to prod.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a `supabase db diff --linked --fail-if-exists` step to CI as a lint step (validates but does not apply). Add a deploy runbook step requiring `supabase migration list` against prod before any worker deploy that touches a new column or table.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium for automated push to prod (risk of bad migration). Low for `db diff` check (read-only).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: CI step: `supabase db diff --linked --fail-if-exists` on every PR to detect schema drift.

mergedFindings.title: deploy-workers.yml deploys all 4 workers in parallel with no job ordering — cron depends on apns-push and ai-proxy service bindings
mergedFindings.evidence: deploy-workers.yml: grep for 'needs' returns 0 matches — all 4 jobs (deploy-ai-proxy, deploy-cron, deploy-apns-push, deploy-sentry-tunnel) run in parallel. workers/cron/wrangler.toml lines 34-43: cron has service bindings to both 'ollie-apns-push' and 'ollie-ai-proxy'. CF service bindings resolve at deploy time against the live worker registry.
mergedFindings.userImpact: On a fresh account or after a worker deletion, cron deploys with broken service bindings before its dependencies exist. Low risk on normal redeploys (workers already exist), high risk on disaster recovery or environment setup.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `needs: [deploy-ai-proxy, deploy-apns-push]` to the deploy-cron job in deploy-workers.yml. This serializes correctly: apns-push and ai-proxy deploy in parallel first, cron only after both succeed.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low. `needs:` is additive; existing deployments are unaffected. Adds ~2 min of sequential wait on deploys.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: No automated CF binding test possible, but the ordering fix removes the failure mode.

mergedFindings.title: apps/api (ollie-notifications) has a placeholder KV namespace ID and is excluded from CI deploy — account-delete path non-functional if ever deployed
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/api/wrangler.toml line 60: `id = 'REPLACE_AFTER_wrangler_kv_create_DEVICE_TOKENS'` — literal placeholder string confirmed in all three rounds. deploy-workers.yml path filter `workers/**` excludes apps/api entirely (grep for 'apps/api' in deploy-workers.yml = no matches). The worker handles /account/delete (App Store GDPR erasure requirement) and device token registration.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If deployed, the worker hard-fails on startup (invalid KV namespace ID). The /account/delete route returns 503. Apple requires functional account deletion for App Store apps — a failing delete endpoint is grounds for App Store rejection.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Decision first: is this worker superseded by workers/apns-push? If yes, delete apps/api/ and document that /account/delete is handled elsewhere. If no, provision the KV namespace (`wrangler kv:namespace create DEVICE_TOKENS`), replace the placeholder ID, and add apps/api to deploy-workers.yml.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for deletion if superseded. Medium for activation (requires provisioning + secret injection).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a wrangler.toml lint step in CI that rejects any config file containing the string 'REPLACE_AFTER'.

mergedFindings.title: Sentry tunnel has no CF native [[ratelimits]] binding — per-isolate in-memory fallback does not bound burst across edge nodes
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/sentry-tunnel/wrangler.toml: no [[ratelimits]] block (confirmed, file is ~9 lines). workers/sentry-tunnel/src/index.ts: code checks `env.TUNNEL_RATE_LIMITER?.limit(...)` and falls back to in-memory per-isolate counter when binding absent. Code comment at line 22-27: 'per-IP fixed-window rate limit (429)' — but this is per-isolate only. In contrast, ai-proxy and apns-push both have [[ratelimits]] native bindings configured.
mergedFindings.userImpact: The tunnel is a public unauthenticated relay (by design). Per-isolate rate limiting means an attacker can relay volume through multiple CF edge nodes simultaneously, with each node seeing a fresh counter. Effective global rate limit approaches (RATE_MAX × CF node count). Sentry quota exhaustion would silence all error reporting.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a `[[ratelimits]]` block to workers/sentry-tunnel/wrangler.toml matching the pattern in ai-proxy/wrangler.toml. The binding name must match `TUNNEL_RATE_LIMITER` in the Env interface. The wrangler ratelimits binding auto-provisions on deploy — 5-line config addition.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Additive config. Worker code already handles the binding when present.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a test: when TUNNEL_RATE_LIMITER binding is present, assert the worker returns 429 after RATE_MAX requests from the same IP in the window.

mergedFindings.title: iOS build number (CFBundleVersion) drifted across three files: project.yml=1.1.0 vs Info.plist=1.1.1 vs tauri.conf.json=1.1.1
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json line 4: version = '1.1.1'. apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple/native_iOS/Info.plist: CFBundleVersion = '1.1.1'. apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple/project.yml line 89: CFBundleVersion = '1.1.0'. Confirmed by direct file reads — project.yml is one version behind. Apple requires CFBundleVersion to be an incrementing integer for each TestFlight upload (Apple TN2420). manageAppVersionAndBuildNumber=true in ExportOptions.plist may mitigate, but the mismatch is unexplained.
mergedFindings.dissent: Round 2 notes that `manageAppVersionAndBuildNumber=true` in ExportOptions.plist may work around the mismatch at archive time. This reduces the immediate rejection risk but does not explain the drift, and manual-only release remains a repeatability problem.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Depending on which file drives the Xcode archive, next TestFlight upload may be built with version 1.1.0 (Apple will reject if a 1.1.0 build already exists) or silently ship the stale version. RELEASE.md already documents build-number bump as a known manual step that is error-prone.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Update apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple/project.yml CFBundleVersion from '1.1.0' to '1.1.1'. Write a `scripts/bump-version.sh <NEW_VERSION>` script that updates all three files atomically. Reference from RELEASE.md.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Cosmetic config fix to project.yml; script is additive.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Pre-release CI check: assert CFBundleVersion in Info.plist, project.yml, and tauri.conf.json all match before any archive step.

mergedFindings.title: deploy-workers.yml has no typecheck gate before wrangler deploy — a manual workflow_dispatch can push type-broken worker code
mergedFindings.evidence: ci.yml line 35: `pnpm typecheck` recurses into workers/ai-proxy (tsc --noEmit). But deploy-workers.yml has zero typecheck steps — only install + cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3. A worker that fails typecheck in CI can still be manually deployed via workflow_dispatch, which bypasses CI entirely.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A manual deploy triggered by workflow_dispatch on a type-broken worker goes to prod with no guardrail. Low probability but zero protection when it happens.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `run: pnpm typecheck` before each `uses: cloudflare/wrangler-action` step in deploy-workers.yml. 4-line change.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low. Additive CI step only.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None — the fix is the gate itself.

mergedFindings.title: Single CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN covers all 4 workers with no least-privilege scoping; wrangler-action pinned to major version only
mergedFindings.evidence: deploy-workers.yml: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN used in all 4 deploy jobs (lines 28, 49, 70, 91). CF API tokens support fine-grained Worker-specific scopes. Token scope cannot be confirmed from code — requires CF dashboard check. cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3 is pinned to major version only, not to a SHA, creating supply-chain risk if the action repo is compromised.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If the GitHub Actions secret is leaked, an attacker has write access to all 4 live workers and can read KV namespaces containing user data. Unpinned action means a compromised wrangler-action@v3 tag could execute arbitrary code in CI.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Scope the CF API token to only the 4 specific workers and their required KV/Queue resources (CF dashboard change only, no code change). Pin wrangler-action to a specific commit SHA and add Dependabot to update it.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Token scoping and SHA pinning are additive security improvements.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a CI lint step (actionlint or zizmor) that rejects unpinned action versions.

mergedFindings.title: Tauri iOS release process is entirely manual — no CI automation, no version bump script, repeated TestFlight rejections documented
mergedFindings.evidence: docs/RELEASE.md: entire TestFlight release is 3 manual shell commands with no CI job. The version-drift finding above (CFBundleVersion mismatch across 3 files) is a direct consequence of the manual process. RELEASE.md line 65 explicitly warns the build number must increment every upload, but provides no script. The TestFlight install failure documented in the MEMORY.md (installCount 0 ever) was a separate Apple server-side issue, but manual release process means no audit trail and no reproducible builds.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Forgotten build bump = TestFlight upload rejected. No CI audit trail means a tsc error could silently ship old dist/ if the build step is skipped during a rushed release.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Write `scripts/bump-version.sh <NEW_VERSION>` (updates tauri.conf.json + project.yml + Info.plist atomically). Add a GitHub Actions job that accepts version as input and runs `tauri ios build` + `xcrun altool` upload (requires Apple credentials in secrets).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for the bump script. Medium for full CI automation (requires Apple ID secrets in GitHub).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Assert all three version sources equal after bump script runs.

implementationRuntimeMismatches: workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml comment says [[queues.producers]] is 'COMMENTED OUT' but the binding is live TOML — comment and code disagree (all 3 rounds confirmed).
workers/cron/wrangler.toml same mismatch: comment says 'COMMENTED OUT' but [[queues.consumers]] is active.

Supabase migration 20260618000004 is marked 'DRAFT — NOT yet applied to prod' in the file header, meaning security_invoker_views RLS fix documented as done in audit reports may not actually be live in the production database.

quickWins: Comment out [[queues.producers]] in workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml (lines 79-81) and [[queues.consumers]] in workers/cron/wrangler.toml (lines 58-63) — 2-line change, prevents next deploy failure immediately.
Change server-apply-routes.ts line 44 from `env.ENVIRONMENT !== 'production'` to `env.ENVIRONMENT === 'staging'` — 2-character change, closes silent auth bypass on misconfigured deploys.
Add `needs: [deploy-ai-proxy, deploy-apns-push]` to deploy-cron job in deploy-workers.yml — 1-line change, enforces service binding deployment order.
Add [[ratelimits]] binding to workers/sentry-tunnel/wrangler.toml — 5-line config addition, enables atomic edge rate limiting (binding name = TUNNEL_RATE_LIMITER, already wired in code).
Update apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple/project.yml CFBundleVersion from '1.1.0' to '1.1.1' — 1-line fix, unblocks next TestFlight upload.
Add `on: workflow_run:` dependency to deploy-workers.yml so deploys only fire after CI passes — 10-line YAML change, closes the broken-test-goes-to-prod gap.

angleSummary: The dump-and-routing pipeline has three compounding failures that make it effectively non-functional as a fast path: (1) cacheHitBump destroys Vectorize entries on first hit by omitting createdAt, making the entire cache a one-shot; (2) PostgREST hit_count increment is silently a no-op in both route.ts and feed-me.ts; (3) pass-2 segmentation and the cron drain both run serial Groq/Anthropic calls that can push total latency past 15–50 seconds. Layered on top: no fetch timeouts on any upstream API call, a 6-second unconditional SQLite polling loop on 37+ screens, no code splitting for the 14-module bundle, and the Groq free-tier TPM ceiling that collapses under 2 concurrent users. The Vectorize eviction sweep (CAP_PER_USER=10,000) is also dead code — never invoked from any cron job.

mergedFindings.title: cacheHitBump omits createdAt — Vectorize cache entry self-destructs after first hit
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/vectorize.ts line 171-185: cacheHitBump() upserts metadata WITHOUT the createdAt field. cacheLookup() at line 101 reads `const createdAt = typeof meta.createdAt === 'number' ? meta.createdAt : 0` — missing field defaults to 0. TTL check at line 102: `Date.now() - 0 ≈ 56 years > TTL_MS (30 days)` → returns null. Code-verified: cacheUpsert() at line 156 does write createdAt correctly; cacheHitBump() at lines 175-183 writes userId/module/payload/confidence/language/hitCount/lastHitAt but omits createdAt. Every entry that gets one cache hit is permanently dead on next lookup.
mergedFindings.userImpact: The Vectorize routing cache is a one-shot — it returns a hit exactly once, then self-destructs. Every subsequent dump for the same phrase pays full Voyage embed + Groq classify cost. The repeated-phrase fast path (<1s) never kicks in; every dump stays at 2–4s. All 5M free Vectorize dimensions/month are consumed by unnecessary cache misses.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Groq free-tier 14.4k req/day is consumed faster. Dump latency never falls to the <1s cache-hit target. The dogfood B5 latency sprint's fast path is entirely negated.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In cacheHitBump() add `createdAt: row.createdAt ?? Date.now()` to the metadata object. Also add `createdAt: number` to the CacheRow interface and populate it from metadata in cacheLookup() (currently cacheLookup returns a CacheRow without carrying createdAt forward). Two-file change: vectorize.ts only.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Fire-and-forget write path. No response path changes.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: workers/ai-proxy/tests/vectorize.test.ts: mock index.upsert, call cacheLookup → cacheHitBump → cacheLookup again, assert second lookup returns the row (not null).

mergedFindings.title: PostgREST hit_count increment is silently broken — routing_cache popularity metric permanently zero
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/route.ts:448 and workers/ai-proxy/src/router/feed-me.ts:818 both send `hit_count: { increment: 1 }` in a raw fetch() PATCH to PostgREST. PostgREST maps JSON body values directly to column types; `{ increment: 1 }` is a JSON object, not an integer. The hit_count column is `int not null default 0` (supabase/migrations/20260521000001_routing_cache.sql:47). PostgREST will 400/422; the .catch() in both call sites swallows the error silently (route.ts:299, feed-me.ts:255). The `{ increment }` operator is a supabase-js SDK abstraction, not raw PostgREST syntax. All three rounds independently confirmed this from the same evidence.
mergedFindings.userImpact: hit_count is permanently 0 on every routing_cache row. Cache popularity-weighted eviction is permanently broken. Any future eviction strategy that relies on hit_count would treat all entries as equally cold and evict randomly.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Create a SQL function `increment_routing_cache_hit(p_id uuid)` that runs `UPDATE routing_cache SET hit_count = hit_count + 1, last_hit_at = now() WHERE id = p_id` and call it via PostgREST RPC in both route.ts and feed-me.ts. Alternatively use PostgREST URL expression syntax `?hit_count=hit_count%2B1`. Both files need the same fix.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Fire-and-forget background write; no user-visible side effect at fix time.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test asserting cacheHitUpdate produces a valid PostgREST request (plain integer or RPC call for hit_count, not a JSON object).

mergedFindings.title: Pass-2 segmentation runs serial Groq calls per flagged fragment — worst-case 15–20s before classification
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts lines 263-283: `for (const frag of pass1.fragments) { if (frag.needsPass2) { ... await pass2Split(...) } }` — each pass2Split is an individual Groq call awaited sequentially. segmentation.ts lines 70-72: any fragment with >7 words OR >4 words + no conjunction + no terminal punctuation is flagged. A typical 3-sentence dump can produce 2-3 flagged fragments; a comment in the code says pass-2 triggers on ~30% of dumps. Each Groq call is ~2-3s at P50 under free tier.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A 3-fragment dump with all needsPass2 adds 3 serial Groq round-trips (~2-3s each) BEFORE classification begins. Total dump latency can reach 15-20s in worst case. Also consumes Groq TPM budget N times per dump instead of once.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace the serial for-loop with `Promise.all` over only the needsPass2 fragments: `const pass2Results = await Promise.all(flaggedFrags.map(f => pass2Split(f.text, providers).catch(() => null)))`, then merge results back by index. Single-fragment dumps are unaffected.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low-medium. Calls are independent. Risk: parallel calls may hit free-tier TPM faster — mitigated by the existing cascade fallback.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: dump.test.ts: input with 3 needsPass2 fragments, mock pass2Split with a latency recorder, assert all 3 are initiated before any resolves.

mergedFindings.title: No fetch timeout on Voyage/Groq/Gemini calls — stalled upstream hangs worker for full 30s
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/groq.ts line 102: bare `await fetch(GROQ_URL, {...})` with no AbortController. workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts lines 543-576: voyageEmbedBatch() uses bare `await fetch(...)`. workers/ai-proxy/src/gemini.ts: same. The ONLY timeout in the codebase is in invites.ts (line 417-425: fetchWithTimeout with SUPABASE_REST_TIMEOUT_MS). Cloudflare Worker wall-clock limit is 30s. Three rounds independently found the same absence.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A stalled Voyage or Groq response hangs the entire worker for up to 30 seconds before CF kills it with a 524. The dump draft IS saved to disk (BrainDumpInput.tsx:217) so data is not lost, but the user sees a frozen spinner then a hard error.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Wrap each upstream fetch in `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` (native in CF Workers since compatibility_date 2022-10-31): Voyage 8s, Groq 20s, Gemini 20s. On AbortError, throw a structured 408 error the caller can map to 'took too long — your words are saved' (already wired in BrainDumpInput:260).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. AbortSignal.timeout is in the compatibility baseline. 20s is generous vs normal P99 Groq latency.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Mock fetch to hang indefinitely; assert groqChat and voyageEmbedBatch throw within the timeout window.

mergedFindings.title: Cron drain: 50 serial Anthropic calls with no time-budget guard — worker killed mid-batch under backlog
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/cron/src/drain.ts lines 127-171: `for (const entry of list.keys)` with `await processOne(env, parsed)` inside. BATCH_CAP=50. processOne calls Anthropic (~1-3s) + two Supabase REST writes. At 2s/item × 50 = 100s serial wall time, far past CF's 30s CPU limit. No elapsed-time check, no partial-batch-commit. Round 1 also found that KV values are fetched serially inside the same loop (line 134 `await env.CACHE_KV.get(entry.name)` before processOne), adding 100-250ms of pure KV latency before any Anthropic call. Native CF Queues path is commented out in wrangler.toml.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Under backlog (outage, busy day), cron drain is killed mid-batch. Items at positions 31+ silently stay in the KV queue and retry next tick, causing enrichment lag. With continued backlog, items expire at their 3-day KV TTL without ever reaching Supabase.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a start-time guard: `const deadline = Date.now() + 25_000` before the loop; break and log when exceeded. Also parallelize the KV.get fetches: `await Promise.all(list.keys.map(k => env.CACHE_KV.get(k.name)))`. Reduce BATCH_CAP to 20 until native CF Queues are provisioned. Fan processOne out in batches of 5 with Promise.allSettled.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Breaking early is safe; items remain in KV and retry next 5-min tick. Parallel processOne needs per-entry error isolation (currently each failure is caught independently — preserve that).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Mock processOne to take 600ms; with deadline=5000ms assert drain processes ≤8 items and logs a deadline-exceeded warning. Assert KV values are fetched in parallel (count concurrent gets).

mergedFindings.title: Groq free-tier 8k TPM ceiling — 2 concurrent dumps already exhaust the bucket, every additional user degrades to Gemini/CF cascade
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump-classify.ts:291 documents '8k tokens/min' free-tier ceiling. SYSTEM_PROMPT measured at 14,735 chars ≈ 3,684 tokens (Round 2) / 8,987 chars ≈ 2,247 tokens (Round 1 — discrepancy likely from different measurement methods). Even at the lower estimate, one classify call = ~2,247 + 300 input + 256 output ≈ ~2,800 tokens. At 4 concurrent 3-fragment dumps the bucket is exhausted. Cascade falls to Gemini (250 req/day) then CF Workers AI then OpenRouter. None of these caps are tracked or alertable.
mergedFindings.userImpact: At >2-4 simultaneous active users, every dump classify falls through to 3-8s Gemini latency. Beyond 250 Gemini requests/day, all dump classifies fail until the next UTC day. This is alpha-blocking.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Upgrade to Groq Dev Tier ($50/mo, 500k TPM) before alpha invite expansion. As a stopgap, add a per-minute token-budget counter in KV to proactively route to Gemini before Groq 429, and add a SYSTEM_PROMPT length CI assertion (`assert len < 12000 chars`) to catch prompt bloat.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for paid tier (infrastructure). Medium for KV token tracker (new code path).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Load test with 5 concurrent 3-fragment dumps; assert p99 < 3s (will fail on free tier, pass on Dev Tier). CI assertion: SYSTEM_PROMPT.length < 12000.

mergedFindings.title: Voyage embed: no retry on 429, no timeout — single transient failure kills entire dump pipeline with 502
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts voyageEmbedBatch() (line 543-577): single bare fetch(), no AbortController signal, no retry. Non-ok response immediately throws `voyage ${res.status}: ...`. Caller returns 502 upstreamError. Same in route.ts voyageEmbed() (line 358-386). By contrast, gemini.ts:64-71 already implements a single 900ms retry on 429/503. Round 1 noted this as part of the broader 'no retry on dump submission' finding; Rounds 2 and 3 isolated it as a distinct Voyage-specific gap.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A single Voyage API transient 429 (common under free-tier burst) kills the entire dump routing pipeline. User sees a hard 502 failure with no guidance. Dump text is not lost (client holds it) but UX is broken for an ADHD user mid-thought.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a single 1s backoff retry to voyageEmbed() and voyageEmbedBatch() on status 429 or 503, mirroring the pattern already in gemini.ts:64-71.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low. Mirrors existing Gemini retry pattern in the same codebase.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: voyageEmbedBatch retries once on 429 and returns embeddings on second call. Throws after both calls fail.

mergedFindings.title: No client-side retry with backoff on dump submission — user must manually re-tap after any transient failure
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/dump/BrainDumpInput.tsx:245-265: on any non-ok response the code sets error state and returns. Draft preserved via PENDING_DUMP_KEY (line 217). No automatic exponential backoff retry anywhere in the client submit path. dumpId idempotency is already in place (dump.ts:217), making automatic retries architecturally safe.
mergedFindings.userImpact: On a momentary Groq 429 or 500ms cellular drop, the ADHD user sees an error banner mid-thought and must manually re-tap. This friction causes dumps to be abandoned.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add 2-attempt retry with 1s backoff + jitter for `rate_limited` and `network` errors inside the submit handler, reusing the same dumpIdRef.current (idempotency key stays valid).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. dumpId idempotency is already in place.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test: a rate_limited error triggers one retry, and both attempts use the same dumpId.

mergedFindings.title: GroceryBox N+1 SQLite: O(N) cadence queries per 6-second poll tick
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/modules/grocery/GroceryBox.tsx:142-145 fans out `cadenceRepo.getCadenceFor(it.name)` for every pantry item inside Promise.all. Each getCadenceFor runs a separate `SELECT id, name, logged_at FROM grocery_purchase_log WHERE name = ?` (apps/native/src/modules/grocery/repo.ts:691-700). With N pantry items this is N SQLite queries per 6-second poll. SQLite in WKWebView serializes concurrent queries.
mergedFindings.userImpact: On a pantry with 40+ items (realistic for active users), 40+ SQLite reads fire every 6 seconds. The actual wall-clock cost compounds under WKWebView serialization. App can feel janky on older iPhones during grocery screen use.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `listCadenceForNames(names: string[])` to cadenceRepo that runs `SELECT name, logged_at FROM grocery_purchase_log WHERE name IN (...)` in one query, then groups in JS.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Pure repo layer change, no business logic impact.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test listCadenceForNames returns correct cadence estimates matching individual getCadenceFor calls.

mergedFindings.title: 37+ module screens unconditionally poll SQLite every 6 seconds with no visibility guard
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/lib/useModuleData.ts:107 — `setInterval(() => { void refresh(); }, pollMs)` with POLL_MS=6000. 37 call sites confirmed by grep. HealthRoom.tsx:138 calls 9 parallel SQLite queries every 6s. TodoScreen.tsx:200 has its own independent 6s setInterval on top. No document.visibilityState check inside the interval callback. main.tsx:44 already uses the visibilityState pattern for pushScanner.
mergedFindings.userImpact: On a loaded home screen with rooms visible, 5+ simultaneous 6-second timers each firing 9 SQLite reads = ~45 SQLite reads/6s even when nothing has changed. Heats CPU and shortens battery on low-end iPhones.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `if (document.visibilityState !== 'visible') return` guard inside the interval callback in useModuleData — 2-line change mirroring the existing pushScanner pattern.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. The visibility guard pattern is already proven in the same codebase.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that refresh is NOT called when document.visibilityState is 'hidden'.

mergedFindings.title: Vectorize eviction sweep (CAP_PER_USER=10,000) is dead code — never wired to any cron job
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/vectorize.ts lines 189-198: evictionScore() is exported with comment 'Called from the eviction sweep job (separate cron worker).' workers/cron/src/index.ts: no vectorize eviction job exists. cacheUpsert() performs no cap enforcement before writing. CAP_PER_USER=10,000 is declared but never enforced. Three rounds independently confirmed by grep across all worker TS files. Round 1 also notes the routing_cache hit_count eviction scoring is broken (hit_count=0 always), compounding this gap.
mergedFindings.userImpact: At dogfood scale: no immediate impact. At production scale with daily use over months, prolific users push unbounded Vectorize entries. Free-tier 5M dimensions/month total across all users gets consumed faster. Old misclassified entries from early use persist forever, degrading lookup precision.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Wire a daily cron job in workers/cron/src/index.ts that performs a metadata-filter scan for each user and calls deleteByIds on entries above CAP_PER_USER, scored by evictionScore(). Note: Vectorize's 'list all vectors for a user' requires a metadata filter scan — verify API support before committing to this approach.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium. Vectorize filter-scan API needs verification. Keep deferred until user volume warrants it.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Integration test: seed 10,001 vectors for one userId, run eviction, assert ≤10,000 remain with highest-score entries kept.

mergedFindings.title: GROQ_MODEL constant uses unverified identifier 'openai/gpt-oss-120b' — may cascade 100% of classify calls to Gemini
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/groq.ts:13: `export const GROQ_MODEL = 'openai/gpt-oss-120b'`. Groq's documented public model IDs follow patterns like `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`. The file comment says `gpt-oss-120b pricing [VERIFY]`. admin.config.ts:65 uses `llama-3.1-8b-instant` (a real Groq model) for fast tier but `openai/gpt-oss-120b` for accurate tier. All tests mock Groq responses so a wrong model name would not surface in CI. Both Round 1 and Round 2 independently flagged this as suspected; neither could confirm without a live API call.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If the model name is invalid on Groq, every /route/:module call (accurate tier) and every Layer 1 dump classify fails with Groq 400, forcing all classify traffic through the Gemini cascade (3-5s latency, 250 req/day cap).
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Run `curl -s https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models -H 'Authorization: Bearer $GROQ_API_KEY'` and confirm the model exists. If not, replace with `meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` or `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`. Add a smoke integration test that verifies GROQ_MODEL exists in the models list.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low if the model name is correct (no change). Low if wrong (one-constant swap).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Smoke integration test (with live GROQ_API_KEY): assert GROQ_MODEL exists in GET /openai/v1/models response.

mergedFindings.title: 14 Box components and 5 Room components are eagerly imported at startup — no code splitting
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/navigation/moduleRegistry.ts:11-24: 14 Box imports at module level. apps/native/src/navigation/Router.tsx:42-46: 5 Room imports. All static. apps/native/vite.config.ts: no manualChunks, no rollupOptions. All 14 modules (each with their own SQLite repos, migrations, AI config) load into the initial JS bundle.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Cold start on iPhone requires parsing and JIT-compiling the entire application JS before the home screen renders. On lower-end iPhones this adds 100-500ms to time-to-interactive. Users never navigate to most modules in a session.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Convert moduleRegistry.ts imports to `React.lazy(() => import('../modules/<name>'))` wrapped in Suspense boundaries at route level. Start with the 5 Room screens. Vite handles chunk splitting automatically.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low-medium. Requires Suspense wrappers at route boundaries. Risk: flash of loading state on first navigate; module SQLite migrations (run inside components) must still fire before render.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Build-time: assert chunk count > 1 after the change. Smoke test: confirm home screen renders before any Room-specific module code is loaded.

mergedFindings.title: Concurrent dump idempotency race — two simultaneous retries with same dumpId both classify (double AI cost)
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts:217-229: idempotency check is KV.get → (if hit replay) → else classify → KV.put. This is not atomic. Two overlapping requests with the same dumpId both miss the KV check simultaneously, each run the full Voyage + Groq + Vectorize pipeline, and both write the result. The idempotency comment at line 213 notes this is 'best-effort' but cost implication is undocumented.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Double Voyage/Groq/Vectorize cost on the overlap window. Negligible at dogfood scale. Under flaky connections at beta scale, can multiply AI costs and push toward rate limits faster.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Write a lightweight 'in-flight' sentinel to KV before classifying (30s TTL) and check it first. Or explicitly document as known race, accepting the cost at current scale.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — sentinel write adds latency to the happy path.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test documenting the known race behavior so future changes don't regress the best-effort protection.

mergedFindings.title: Cache write failures (cacheHitBump, cacheHitUpdate) have no observability — failures are 100% silent
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts line 394-398: `keepAlive(cacheHitBump(...).catch(e => console.error(...)))`. workers/ai-proxy/src/router/route.ts line 299: `void cacheHitUpdate(...).catch(e => console.error(...))`. Both errors go only to console.error with no telemetry counter, no metric emission, no alert. Combined with the cacheHitBump createdAt bug (P1 finding), failure rate would be 100% but invisible without wrangler tail.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any regression in Vectorize upsert or Supabase PATCH goes undetected until users report latency degradation. No alarm fires.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `metric: 'cache_write_failed'` structured log line in each catch block alongside the existing console.error. Emits structured JSON visible in wrangler tail and queryable in CF analytics.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero. Additive logging change.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Extend existing vectorize.test.ts to assert the metric field is present in the console.error call on Vectorize failure.

mergedFindings.title: Cron drain serial KV.get inside the loop adds 100-250ms of pure dead latency before Anthropic calls begin
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/cron/src/drain.ts:134 `const raw = await env.CACHE_KV.get(entry.name)` is called inside the serial for...of loop. KV.list() at line 125 returns key metadata but not values; each value is fetched one at a time. For 50 entries at ~2-5ms each KV read = 100-250ms of pure KV latency before the first Anthropic call starts. This is a subset of the broader serial drain issue (merged above) but is independently fixable with a one-line Promise.all.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Compounded with the serial processOne issue: worst-case batch time is 50 × (5ms KV + 1000ms Anthropic + 10ms Supabase × 2) ≈ 51s — well past the 30s worker limit.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace serial KV.get loop with `await Promise.all(list.keys.map(k => env.CACHE_KV.get(k.name)))` to parallelise value fetches before the processOne loop.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Read-only; doesn't change retry or DLQ logic.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Assert that drainEnrichQueue fetches all KV values in parallel (mock KV, count concurrent get calls).

implementationRuntimeMismatches: GROQ_MODEL='openai/gpt-oss-120b': all three rounds flag this as suspected-invalid but cannot confirm without a live Groq API call. admin.config.ts uses valid Groq model IDs (llama-3.1-8b-instant) for the fast tier but the accurate-tier constant uses an OpenRouter-style path. Needs `curl /openai/v1/models` verification before triaging as bug vs. intentional alias.

Vectorize eviction: Round 1 noted eviction score logic is architecturally sound. Round 3 confirmed it is dead code. No dissent on the dead-code finding, but there is disagreement on whether it matters now (Round 1: 'not yet a problem at free tier cap', Round 3: 'old misclassified entries poison cache precision'). The P1 cacheHitBump bug makes this moot in the short term — entries self-destruct anyway.

routing_cache hit_count: All three rounds agree it is silently broken. Round 3 additionally notes there is no stored procedure for atomic increment in any migration file, confirming the fix requires a new SQL function or RPC — not just a client-side change.
topRisks: cacheHitBump omits createdAt: the entire Vectorize routing cache self-destructs after first hit — every dump pays full Voyage+Groq cost, the fast path is a no-op (P1, confidence 1 but mathematically proven by code)
Groq free-tier 8k TPM + large SYSTEM_PROMPT: 2 concurrent active users already exhaust the bucket and cascade to Gemini (250 req/day) — alpha-blocking without Groq Dev Tier upgrade
Cron drain: 50 serial Anthropic calls with no time-budget guard, compounded by serial KV.get fetches, can hit CF 30s wall-clock under backlog, leaving enrichment entries to expire in KV unprocessed
quickWins: Add `createdAt: row.createdAt ?? Date.now()` to cacheHitBump() metadata — 3-line fix, immediately restores cache persistence and fast-path latency
Fix PostgREST hit_count increment in route.ts:448 and feed-me.ts:818 — replace JSON object body with RPC call; ~10 min, 2 files
Add AbortSignal.timeout(8000) to voyageEmbedBatch() and AbortSignal.timeout(20000) to groqChat() — mirrors existing invites.ts fetchWithTimeout pattern; 2 files, ~5 min
Add `if (document.visibilityState !== 'visible') return` guard to useModuleData setInterval callback — 2-line change, stops 37+ wasted SQLite bursts when app is backgrounded
Add `metric: 'cache_write_failed'` structured log in both cacheHitBump and cacheHitUpdate catch blocks — zero-risk, zero-latency observability improvement

Run `curl https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models -H 'Authorization: Bearer $GROQ_API_KEY'` to verify GROQ_MODEL='openai/gpt-oss-120b' is a valid model — 2-minute check that either closes or elevates this finding to P0

angleSummary: The ai-proxy Cloudflare Worker is the integration hub for Clerk JWT auth, Supabase, Voyage embeddings, Groq/Gemini/CF-AI/OpenRouter cascade, APNs push, Sentry tunnel, and CF Queues. Round 1 produced no findings. Rounds 2 and 3 are in strong agreement on all major issues. Three P1s stand out: /brain-copy has no rate limit (flagged in the 2026-06-18 audit and still unfixed), CF Queues TOML blocks are live despite comments saying they should be commented out (deploy bomb), and Voyage is a single embedding-layer SPOF with no fallback. Additional P2s cover unsalted telemetry user hashes, stale Supabase JWT fallback never removed after Clerk migration, APNs JWT cache not keyed on keyId, missing GEMINI_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_API_KEY in secrets docs, and unauthenticated requests bypassing rate limiting before getting 401. P3s cover Sentry being dead infrastructure and Groq model pricing having unverified constants.

mergedFindings.title: /brain-copy endpoint has no rate limit — any valid Clerk JWT can drain Groq quota unboundedly
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/index.ts lines 383-389: /brain-copy dispatches directly to handleBrainCopy() with zero checkRate() call. Every other AI-cost endpoint (/route/dump line 402, /route/:module line 424, /brain-dump line 447) is wrapped in checkRate(env.AI_RATE_LIMITER, …). brain-copy.ts calls groqChat with COPY_MODEL='openai/gpt-oss-120b' and maxTokens=600. The 2026-06-18 audit flagged this as critical (#2 in FINAL_AUDIT.md); still unfixed on this branch.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A single leaked or malicious Clerk session JWT can loop /brain-copy to exhaust the Groq free-tier quota (8k tokens/min), degrading or blocking all dump classification for all users. On a paid Groq tier, direct cost amplification with no server-side brake.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: The existing AI_RATE_LIMITER and RATE_KV bindings are already wired on adjacent routes; the guard is structurally missing here. Client accepts fully client-controlled system and user strings (up to 4000 chars), making this effectively a free general-purpose LLM proxy on Ollie's Groq account.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In workers/ai-proxy/src/index.ts, before dispatching to handleBrainCopy, resolve resolveUserIdForRateLimit and call checkRate(env.AI_RATE_LIMITER, env.RATE_KV, 'rl:ai:braincopy:'+userId) — same 4-line pattern as /route/dump at lines 400-410.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low. Static fallback is already in the client. Rate-limiting this endpoint does not change any happy-path behavior.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a test in workers/ai-proxy/tests/route-rate-limit.test.ts that stubs AI_RATE_LIMITER to return {success: false} and asserts /brain-copy returns 429.

mergedFindings.title: CF Queues producer and consumer TOML blocks are both ACTIVE despite comments saying they should be commented out — next wrangler deploy may hard-fail
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml lines 79-81: [[queues.producers]] binding='ENRICH_QUEUE' queue='ollie-enrich-queue' is uncommented live TOML, but the prose comment says 'COMMENTED OUT, see DEPLOY_TODO'. workers/cron/wrangler.toml lines 58-63: same mismatch for [[queues.consumers]]. If the queue does not exist in Cloudflare, wrangler deploy will hard-fail with a binding resolution error. If the queue DOES exist, the KV-scan fallback in drain.ts is now redundant and may double-process dump entries.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If the queue is not provisioned: the next wrangler deploy of ai-proxy or cron is blocked, preventing ALL future deploys including hotfixes. If double-processing: duplicate enriched_signals rows in Supabase per brain dump.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Cannot be caught by unit tests — only visible at deploy time. The inconsistency between prose comments and live TOML creates a latent deploy bomb.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Run `wrangler queues list` to confirm whether ollie-enrich-queue and ollie-enrich-dlq exist. If YES: update prose comments to match live TOML. If NO: comment the blocks out (prefix with #) and restore KV fallback path. Check DEPLOY_TODO.md §'Item #4' for intended state.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low if re-commenting (KV fallback has worked reliably). Medium if confirming queue exists (must verify both queues and the DLQ).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a CI step that runs `wrangler deploy --dry-run` and asserts it exits 0 before any production deploy.

mergedFindings.title: Voyage embeddings are a single point of failure for all classification — a Voyage 429 or outage returns 502 with no fallback
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts line 352: voyageEmbedBatch failure returns upstreamError('voyage_embed_failed', 502). workers/ai-proxy/src/router/route.ts line 282: same pattern for /route/:module. The four-provider json-cascade (Groq→CF→Gemini→OpenRouter) only covers the LLM classify step; the embedding step has no fallback provider or retry. Voyage free tier caps at 10M tokens/month with per-minute rate limits.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any Voyage outage or rate-limit spike causes ALL brain dumps and ALL module routing to return 502. Every user sees 'something went wrong' on every dump attempt for the duration of the outage.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Most exposed SPOF in the AI pipeline. No per-minute counter or alerting on Voyage call volume. The cascade fallback for LLM is robust but the embedding layer has no equivalent.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a retry-once with 500ms backoff for Voyage 429 inside voyageEmbedBatch(), mirroring the existing Gemini retry in gemini.ts lines 57-67. Longer-term: fall back to CF Workers AI @cf/baai/bge-m3 embeddings on Voyage failure (note: dimension mismatch 1024 vs 768 requires a separate Vectorize index).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for retry path. Medium for CF AI embedding fallback due to Vectorize index dimension mismatch.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a test in dump.test.ts where the Voyage fetch mock returns 429 and assert the response is 429 after retry, not 502.

mergedFindings.title: Supabase JWT legacy fallback in verifyJwt() never removed after Clerk migration — stale Supabase tokens still accepted on all write endpoints
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/invites.ts lines 390-411: verifyJwt() tries Clerk first, then falls through to a Supabase /auth/v1/user round-trip if Clerk returns null. Comment says 'Removed once the Supabase session window has fully aged out' but no TTL, deadline, or removal ticket exists. Used for /enrich-dump, /ingest-event, /label, /generate-invite, /validate-invite, /claim-invite.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A long-lived Supabase JWT (e.g. from a compromised device or log) can still authenticate to write telemetry, generate invites, or claim invites under a different identity than the user's Clerk account. The Clerk migration is structurally incomplete at the auth layer.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Dual-identity window is open indefinitely. No deadline exists in code or config to close it. An attacker who obtained a Supabase JWT can operate as a different identity than their Clerk account on sensitive endpoints.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a SUPABASE_JWT_CUTOFF env var (ISO date). In the Supabase fallback branch, reject JWTs with iat before that date. Set a calendar reminder to null out SUPABASE_ANON_KEY once all sessions have aged out (Supabase default session TTL is 1 hour).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium. May log out users still on Supabase sessions. Coordinate with Clerk migration timeline.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a test in telemetry-auth.test.ts verifying that a valid Supabase JWT is accepted when CLERK_ISSUER is set and Clerk returns null (confirming fallback works), and that a tampered JWT is rejected.

mergedFindings.title: GEMINI_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_API_KEY not documented in wrangler.toml secrets section — silent missing-key risk on redeploy
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml secrets section documents ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, SUPABASE_*, CLERK_ISSUER, VOYAGE_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, and T0_JWT_ENFORCED — but not GEMINI_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY. FeedMeEnv.GEMINI_API_KEY: string (router/feed-me.ts:55) is a required non-optional field; DumpRouteEnv.GEMINI_API_KEY: string (router/dump.ts:85) is also required. TypeScript types pass at build but produce undefined at runtime if the secret is absent.
mergedFindings.userImpact: On a new worker deploy, secrets rotation, or new developer setup, if GEMINI_API_KEY is not manually set, the Gemini fallback tier is silently eliminated from the classify cascade. Feed Me recipe generation breaks entirely. OPENROUTER_API_KEY absence degrades the cascade further to CF Workers AI only.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: No build-time check catches missing CF Worker secrets. Silent failure removes the ~250k TPM fallback buffer without any warning log.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add GEMINI_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_API_KEY to the secrets documentation block in workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml. Add a startup guard in the fetch handler that logs a warning when these keys are absent (similar to dump.ts:237 which returns 503 on missing GEMINI_API_KEY for vision paths).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero — documentation only plus optional warning log.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a test that simulates missing GEMINI_API_KEY and verifies the cascade proceeds to CF Workers AI rather than throwing uncaught.

mergedFindings.title: USER_HASH_SALT secret not documented in wrangler.toml — telemetry user hashes are unsalted and reversible in production
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/telemetry.ts line 47: 'if (!salt) console.warn("[telemetry] USER_HASH_SALT unset — hashing userId unsalted")'. USER_HASH_SALT does not appear in workers/ai-proxy/wrangler.toml or workers/cron/wrangler.toml (grepped, no match). It does appear in test env objects (tests/ingest-event.test.ts line 17 sets it to 'test-salt'). Status is 'suspected' because the secret could be set via `wrangler secret put` without appearing in wrangler.toml.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If USER_HASH_SALT is unset in production, every user_hash in raw_dumps, enriched_signals, retention_events, session_events, and module_events is SHA-256(userId) — a deterministic, reversible mapping given Clerk user IDs follow a known format (user_<26-char-base62>). Privacy regression for all opted-in telemetry users.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Any future salt addition breaks all existing join keys across telemetry tables. The warn-only log means this degrades silently.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: 1. Add USER_HASH_SALT to the wrangler.toml secrets documentation block of both ai-proxy and cron. 2. Set the secret via `wrangler secret put USER_HASH_SALT` (choose once and keep; changing it breaks historical join keys). 3. Elevate the console.warn to a startup error if the salt is absent.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low if done before beta. High if done after production data accumulates (breaks historical join keys).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a test asserting that deriveUserHash('user_abc', undefined) emits a console.warn AND that deriveUserHash('user_abc', 'salt') produces a different hash than the unsalted version.

mergedFindings.title: APNs JWT signer cache not keyed on keyId/teamId — stale token served up to 45 minutes after Apple key rotation
mergedFindings.evidence: packages/apns-jwt/src/index.ts lines 93-101: the in-process cache (let cache: CachedJwt | null) stores one token per signer instance; the cache check at line 97 only tests cache.exp - now > refreshMarginSec. workers/apns-push/src/index.ts line 65: the signer is module-scoped — one instance per isolate, surviving multiple requests. If APPLE_KEY_ID or APPLE_TEAM_ID changes, the cached token from the old key is returned for up to 45 minutes, causing every APNs push to fail with 401.
mergedFindings.userImpact: After rotating the Apple push key, all notifications — including watcher offers and real-time reminders — silently fail to deliver for up to 45 minutes. No error reaches the user.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Silent auth failure window of up to 45 minutes on key rotation. No alerting on APNs 401 response.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Include a fingerprint of (keyId, teamId) in the CachedJwt entry. Before the exp check at line 97, add: if (cache.keyId !== config.keyId || cache.teamId !== config.teamId) cache = null. Two-line guard.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low. Only affects the cache invalidation path, not the signing path.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a unit test in packages/apns-jwt/ where the signer is called with keyId='A' then keyId='B'; assert the second call re-signs rather than returning the key-A token.

mergedFindings.title: Unauthenticated requests to /route/dump and /route/:module bypass rate limiting before returning 401
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/index.ts lines 400-434: resolveUserIdForRateLimit is called before the route handler. When T0_JWT_ENFORCED !== '0', a request with no JWT causes resolveUserIdForRateLimit to return null, so the 'if (routeUserId)' guard at line 423 skips checkRate entirely. The handler correctly returns 401, but not before the Clerk JWKS fetch (remote round-trip). An unauthenticated attacker can spam these endpoints at full CF Workers free-tier rate (1000 req/min) with no per-IP rate gate.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Not a direct cost leak (Voyage/Groq calls not reached). Latent DoS vector: high-frequency unauthenticated spam burns CPU on JWT verify round-trips and may stress the Clerk JWKS endpoint (faithful-stag-15.clerk.accounts.dev). Relevant for beta launch.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Missing rate limit on unauthenticated requests means the only guard is the CF default Workers rate limit. Same gap exists on /route/dump (index.ts:400-411).
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: When resolveUserIdForRateLimit returns null, apply a separate anonymous rate limit keyed on req.headers.get('cf-connecting-ip') ?? 'anon' before handing to the route handler.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — additive guard only.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that /route/grocery with no auth header and a stubbed IP-based rate limiter that rejects the key returns 429 before 401.

mergedFindings.title: Sentry SDK not installed in apps/native — sentryTunnel() and the deployed CF worker are dead infrastructure
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/package.json has no @sentry/* entry (grepped, no match). No file in apps/native/src/ imports from @sentry. apps/native/src/api/workers.ts exports sentryTunnel() at line 579 but it is never called because there is no Sentry.init(). pnpm-workspace.yaml: '@sentry/capacitor' appears only in allowBuilds (Capacitor-era, not a dependency). The sentry-tunnel CF worker (workers/sentry-tunnel/) is deployed and consuming free-tier requests for zero benefit.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Production crashes, uncaught promise rejections, and dump failures in the Tauri/React app are invisible. Bugs found only when Serra hits them manually.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Error observability gap affects beta quality. The deployed sentry-tunnel worker consumes CF free-tier request quota for zero benefit.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Either: (a) install @sentry/react + call Sentry.init() in apps/native/src/main.tsx with tunnel pointing to VITE_SENTRY_TUNNEL_URL and add beforeSend to strip encrypted fields (mentioned in workers.ts comment at line 572); OR (b) remove sentryTunnel() from workers.ts and decommission the sentry-tunnel worker if error reporting is intentionally deferred.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for either option.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: For option (a): add a smoke test verifying the tunnel worker rejects DSNs not in ALLOWED_PROJECT_IDS.

mergedFindings.title: Groq model 'openai/gpt-oss-120b' has a [VERIFY] TODO on pricing constants and the docstring still says 'Llama 3.3 70B'
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/groq.ts line 13: GROQ_MODEL = 'openai/gpt-oss-120b'; docstring on line 6 still says 'Llama 3.3 70B'. lines 68-72: PRICE_PER_MTOK = {input: 0.15, output: 0.6} marked '[VERIFY] confirm against https://groq.com/pricing before trusting'. Same model string appears in all 10 module *.config.ts constants and brain-copy.ts:27. Model was not in Groq's catalogue as of August 2025 knowledge boundary — may have been added in 2026.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If the model ID is invalid on Groq, all dump classification and brain-copy calls fail and cascade to Gemini (burning the 250 req/day free-tier cap faster). If pricing constants are wrong, cost_usd fields in all ai_call metrics are systematically miscalibrated, making cost projections for alpha/beta unreliable.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: No runtime test verifies the model name against Groq's live model list. Cost monitoring via wrangler tail is silently wrong if pricing is stale.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: 1. Run `curl https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models -H 'Authorization: Bearer $GROQ_API_KEY'` and confirm 'openai/gpt-oss-120b' is listed. 2. Update the groq.ts docstring to match the actual model. 3. Verify and correct PRICE_PER_MTOK values. 4. Remove the [VERIFY] comment once confirmed.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero — documentation and constant update only.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a regression test that asserts GROQ_MODEL is not 'llama-3.3-70b' (guards against silent future swaps back to the old string).

mergedFindings.title: Gemini fallback comments conflate RPD (250/day) with TPM (250k) — cascade capacity is overestimated, exhaustion is invisible
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/gemini.ts line 7: '250 requests/day cap'. workers/ai-proxy/src/router/json-cascade.ts line 9: 'Gemini 2.5 Flash (~250k TPM)'. workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump-classify.ts line 298: '~31× the TPM (250k/min)'. These apply to different free-tier limits (RPM is 10; RPD is 250; TPM is 1M on paid). At beta scale, a user dumping 50 times/day plus Groq TPM hits could burn the 250 Gemini RPD in hours. No per-day counter or alerting on Gemini call volume exists. geminiJson has no equivalent metric log to groqChat's ai_call.
mergedFindings.userImpact: At beta scale, Gemini exhaustion is invisible until users see classification failures. After 250 Gemini calls/day the cascade falls to CF Workers AI (~10k neurons/day) then OpenRouter — if OPENROUTER_API_KEY is unset, classification fails entirely.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Cost tracking only covers Groq calls. Gemini exhaustion has no alerting path. Comments mislead operators about available headroom.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: 1. Add a console.log metric line in geminiJson() matching the groqChat ai_call pattern. 2. Correct the conflicting comments to accurately state: free-tier Gemini 2.5 Flash = 10 RPM + 250 RPD. 3. Set up a Gemini quota alert in GCP console.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero — logging only plus comment correction.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add a test verifying the Gemini fallback is invoked when Groq returns 429 and that the result is correctly parsed.

implementationRuntimeMismatches: CF Queues TOML blocks: prose comments say 'COMMENTED OUT' but the TOML is live — actual queue provisioning state in Cloudflare cannot be determined from source alone; requires `wrangler queues list` to resolve
USER_HASH_SALT: not in wrangler.toml docs but could be set via `wrangler secret put` — status 'suspected' not 'confirmed'; requires CF dashboard inspection to confirm

Groq model 'openai/gpt-oss-120b': appeared after August 2025 knowledge cutoff; cannot confirm it is a valid Groq model ID from source alone; requires `curl https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models` to resolve
topRisks: /brain-copy has no rate limit — flagged in 2026-06-18 audit (#2) and still unfixed; any valid Clerk JWT can drain Groq quota in seconds
CF Queues TOML blocks are active despite 'COMMENTED OUT' prose — next wrangler deploy hard-fails if queue is not provisioned, blocking ALL future deploys including hotfixes
Voyage is a single SPOF for all classification: a Voyage 429 or outage returns 502 on every brain dump with no embedding-layer fallback or retry
quickWins: Add checkRate(env.AI_RATE_LIMITER, env.RATE_KV, 'rl:ai:braincopy:'+userId) before handleBrainCopy() in index.ts — 4 lines, mirrors /route/dump pattern exactly
Run `wrangler queues list` NOW to determine queue provisioning state and either update the prose comment or re-comment the TOML blocks before the next deploy
Add GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and USER_HASH_SALT to the wrangler.toml secrets documentation block — zero-risk, prevents silent missing-key on future deploys
Add keyId+teamId to the APNs JWT cache entry in packages/apns-jwt/src/index.ts — 2-line fix prevents stale tokens after Apple key rotation
Add console.log metric line in geminiJson() matching the groqChat ai_call pattern — zero risk, gives Gemini cost and exhaustion visibility

angleSummary: Covers the dump routing pipeline (Layer 1/2), crisis detection, confidence policy, Vectorize cache lifecycle, module classification validation, replenishment/cadence logic, noticing selection scoring, and the learning loop across the Ollie monorepo (branch redesign/olive-neumorphic). All three rounds inspected the same core files; findings converge on three structural problems: (1) crisis tier-1 false-positives causing silent dump loss, (2) unreviewed safety-critical lexicons with no CI gate, and (3) multiple cache/validation gaps that silently corrupt routing data.

mergedFindings.title: Crisis tier-1 (ambiguous distress) triggers full dump short-circuit — silently discards data on ADHD burnout phrases
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts:292-302: `const crisis = detectCrisis(combinedDump) ?? undefined; if (crisis) { return json({...}) }`. The comment at line 15 says 'tier ≥ 2' but the guard is `if (crisis)` which fires on any non-null CrisisSignal including tier-1. packages/crisis-lexicon/data/lexicon.en.json tier-1 patterns include `can't take it anymore`, `tired of everything`, `nothing matters anymore`, `what's the point`. Same tier-1 suppression exists in apps/native/src/dump/BrainDumpInput.tsx:192-196 (local pre-screen). When the short-circuit fires: no Voyage embed, no Vectorize write, no server-apply, no dumpArchive.record() — absolute data loss.
mergedFindings.userImpact: An ADHD user venting 'I can't take it anymore, bought milk and eggs' hits a tier-1 pattern → full crisis banner → dump permanently discarded with no retry path. Items in the dump are silently lost. At scale, false-positive rate trains users to avoid honest venting.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Code-vs-comment mismatch makes the bug invisible to reviewers. All items in the dump are gone: no writeInbox row, no idempotency key. The client archive write (DumpScreen line 164 checks `!output.crisis`) also skips. Total data loss per false-positive event.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In dump.ts change `if (crisis)` to `if (crisis?.tier >= 2)`. Mirror same guard in BrainDumpInput.tsx where localCrisis is computed. For tier-1 hits, attach the crisis signal to the response but still route fragments normally.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — narrowing the short-circuit from any-tier to tier>=2 only reduces false positives. Real tier-2/3/4 signals are unchanged.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test: POST tier-1 phrase ('can't take it anymore') → response.fragments.length > 0, response.crisis absent or non-short-circuiting. Integration test: 'I can't take it anymore, bought milk' → grocery.pantry_add still appears. Tier-2 phrase → full short-circuit still fires.

mergedFindings.title: All three crisis lexicons are PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL — safety-critical content shipping to device with zero CI enforcement gate
mergedFindings.evidence: packages/crisis-lexicon/data/lexicon.en.json:3, lexicon.tr.json:3, lexicon.es.json:3 all have `"last_reviewed_by": "PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL"`. packages/crisis-lexicon/src/index.ts:16 states 'last_reviewed_by must be @serra before any merge that ships to alpha'. No CI gate exists: grep for PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL in .github/ returns nothing. App is already installed on device. EN 'end it' / 'end things' tier-2 patterns have no exclusions for 'end it early' or 'let's just end the meeting'.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Crisis detection (the only safety net for self-harm signals) ships with unreviewed lexicons. False negatives miss real signals; false positives (confirmed P1 above) cause data loss + banner fatigue. For ADHD users in distress this is a direct safety risk.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Self-declared alpha blocker in source comments that has never been actioned. Lexicon frozen at v0.1.0 dated 2026-05-25. The app is already on device, meaning unreviewed patterns are live.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a CI test that reads all three lexicon JSON files and fails build if `last_reviewed_by === 'PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL'`. This is a review task, not a code change — Serra reviews and updates the field. Also add exclusions for 'end it early' / 'end the meeting' in EN tier-2.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero — the CI gate is purely additive.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add to crisis-lexicon/tests/detect.test.ts: `it('all lexicons are Serra-approved', () => { for (const lang of ALL_LANGUAGES) { expect(getLexicon(lang).last_reviewed_by).toBe('@serra'); } })`. Fail until reviewed.

mergedFindings.title: AI-returned module value never validated against allowed MODULES list — hallucinated module names flow to Vectorize cache, server-apply, and client dispatch
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump-classify.ts:239-253: `parsed.module` is a TypeScript type annotation (Module) only — no runtime check. MODULES array at line 20 is used only in the prompt, never for validation. parseBatchResults (line 282) and classifyFragment (line 251) both return r.module directly. If Groq/Gemini/CF returns 'wellness', 'brain', 'household', etc., it propagates into Fragment, server-apply (dump_inbox row with routed_module=hallucinated_string), Vectorize cache (dump.ts:454), and client dispatch.ts which finds no handler and silently drops the fragment.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A misclassified fragment is silently lost from all module views. The action (grocery pantry update, finance log, etc.) never applies. User sees 'okay!' ack but nothing happens. The Vectorize cache also stores the invalid module, poisoning future cache hits for semantically similar phrases.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Cache poisoning: future hits for the same phrase also return the invalid module. Server-apply inserts a bogus routed_module into dump_inbox. Client dispatch no-ops silently with reportNoHandlerDrift.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In dump-classify.ts after JSON.parse: `if (!MODULES.includes(parsed.module)) { return { module: 'dump_only', payload: { action: 'archive_only', reason: 'invalid_module' }, confidence: 0 }; }`. Apply same guard in parseBatchResults.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — demotion to dump_only is the same result as the current handler-miss path, but prevents cache poisoning.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test: mock classifyBatch to return module='unknown_module' → fragment.module === 'dump_only'. Test that cacheUpsert is not called with invalid module. Test in route.test.ts that invalid modules are demoted server-side.

mergedFindings.title: AI-routed module='crisis' fragment bypasses zero-storage policy — flows to Vectorize cache and dump_inbox
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts: detectCrisis() fires first (line 292); if crisis, returns early with zero storage. But classifyBatch() result handling (lines 427-463) never checks whether a fragment comes back with module='crisis'. A phrase that bypasses the lexicon (transliteration, novel phrasing) but that Groq classifies as module='crisis' is written to Vectorize (line 454) and dump_inbox via writeInbox (line 517). apps/native/src/modules/stubs.ts:70-75 crisisHandler returns ok('crisis surface engaged') without enforcing zero-storage.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A user whose crisis text bypasses the lexicon but triggers the LLM router has that text stored in Vectorize and Supabase dump_inbox — violating the explicit zero-storage invariant documented in #77.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Zero-storage guarantee is circumventable via the AI-classification path. The crisis screen is driven by RouterOutput.crisis field only, not by fragment.module, so the handler does not trigger the crisis UI either.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In dump.ts Pass B result loop (~line 441), add: `if (tiered.module === 'crisis') { /* skip cacheUpsert and writeInbox, optionally set soft crisis flag */ continue; }`. Also update crisis UI to respond to fragment.module === 'crisis'.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — additive guard before existing fire-and-forget writes. No schema change.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: classifyBatch returns module='crisis' but detectCrisis returns null → assert no Vectorize upsert, no writeInbox call, and client receives a soft crisis signal.

mergedFindings.title: cacheHitBump omits createdAt field — Vectorize cache entries expire on first hit, breaking the repeat-phrase optimization
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/vectorize.ts:165-186: `cacheHitBump` upserts metadata WITHOUT `createdAt`. CF Vectorize upsert fully replaces metadata on id collision. cacheLookup:101-102: `const createdAt = typeof meta.createdAt === 'number' ? meta.createdAt : 0; if (Date.now() - createdAt > TTL_MS) return null` — missing createdAt defaults to 0, age ≈ 1.75 billion ms >> 30-day TTL → null. cacheUpsert (line 142) correctly sets `createdAt: now`; cacheHitBump does not. Test file always includes createdAt in mock data so bug is invisible to existing tests.
mergedFindings.userImpact: The routing cache degrades for every repeat user — the ADHD core use case. 'Bought milk' said weekly: first time → AI + cache write. Second time → cache hit → bump (drops createdAt) → third time → expired → AI call again. Cache hit rate approaches zero for popular phrases. Cost and latency benefits disappear.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Popularity-weighted eviction (evictionScore = hitCount * decay) is fed incorrect data since entries expire instead of being evicted. Groq TPM usage and Voyage embedding costs are higher than intended.
