mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: (1) Add `createdAt` to CacheRow interface. (2) Pass it through cacheHitBump from the row. (3) Include it in the bump upsert metadata: `createdAt: row.createdAt ?? Date.now()`.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — additive field only. Ensures entries live their full 30-day TTL.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: cacheHitBump upserts WITH createdAt preserved. Test: subsequent cacheLookup on bumped entry does not return null due to TTL.

mergedFindings.title: Low-confidence Vectorize cache hits replayed with default confidence 0.8 — uncertain cache entries silently routed without confirm card
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/vectorize.ts:117: `confidence: typeof meta.confidence === 'number' ? meta.confidence : 0.8`. Legacy or corrupt rows with no confidence field are served at 0.8. dump-schema.ts:73-75: `if (confidence >= 0.8) return { needsConfirm: false }` — silent apply. A fragment originally classified at 0.62 (needsConfirm: true) that loses its confidence in metadata is silently applied on re-hit. UNCERTAIN_CONFIDENCE in dump-classify.ts:199 is 0.6, making 0.8 an inconsistent and risky default.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A misclassified fragment that originally required user confirmation is silently applied to the wrong module on subsequent encounters if its cache metadata lost the confidence field. Data written to wrong module without user awareness.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Inconsistency between UNCERTAIN_CONFIDENCE (0.6) and the cache fallback (0.8). Makes the confidence policy non-deterministic across cached vs fresh classifications.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Change vectorize.ts:117 default from 0.8 to 0.6 (same as UNCERTAIN_CONFIDENCE). Unknown-confidence entries trigger a confirm card instead of silent apply.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — makes fallback more conservative. A few extra confirm cards on legacy entries is acceptable vs silent misclassification.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: cacheLookup on row with no confidence field → returned confidence <= 0.79 (triggers needsConfirm: true).

mergedFindings.title: hit_count PATCH uses PostgREST-unsupported {increment:1} object — routing cache popularity signal is permanently dead
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/route.ts:448: cacheHitUpdate PATCHes `{ hit_count: { increment: 1 } }`. PostgREST has no atomic increment operator for plain int columns — treats the object literal as the column value, producing a 400 (type mismatch) which fire-and-forget `.catch(console.error)` swallows silently. Same bug in workers/ai-proxy/src/router/feed-me.ts:818. Previously documented in docs/audit/2026-06-18/round-2.md line 95 and round-3.md line 73 — still not fixed. hit_count is forever 0.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Cache eviction is blind to popularity. Hot phrases ('bought milk') are evicted at the same rate as one-off phrases. The 10,000-entry-per-user cap will eventually evict the most useful entries first. Long-term: cache hit rate degrades for power users.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Popularity-weighted eviction (evictionScore = hitCount * decay in vectorize.ts) is permanently inert. The algorithm exists but is fed all-zeros. Previously documented in two prior audit rounds and not addressed.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace PATCH body with an RPC: create `SECURITY DEFINER` SQL function `routing_cache_bump(id uuid)` that does `UPDATE routing_cache SET hit_count = hit_count+1, last_hit_at = now() WHERE id = $1`. Call via /rest/v1/rpc/routing_cache_bump.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Requires one migration + one RPC wrapper.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: In route.test.ts: assert PATCH body is an integer (not an object) OR assert RPC is called with correct id.

mergedFindings.title: Medication orchestrator never writes 'medication.patterns' — missed/overdue doses invisible on brain home surface
mergedFindings.evidence: packages/orchestrator/src/medication.ts recompute() writes to 'medication.dueSlots', 'medication.adherence', 'medication.lastRecomputeAt' (lines 94-96) but never 'medication.patterns'. apps/native/src/modules/brain/noticings.ts:42 includes 'medication' in PATTERN_NAMESPACES — gatherer reads store.get('medication', 'patterns', []) → always empty array. Medication overdue signals only fire push notifications; they never appear as NoticingCandidates. Desktop (no APNs) = fully silenced.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Missed medication doses — explicitly called out as ADHD-critical in orchestrator comments (line 16) — are invisible on the home surface. On desktop (no APNs), medication reminders are fully silenced. Only push notifications surface them, requiring notification permission + app backgrounded.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Gap between orchestrator output schema and the patterns contract expected by noticings.ts. Follows the same pattern used by admin/sleep/grocery orchestrators but the medication one was never completed.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In medication.ts recompute(), after computing dueSlots, build a patterns array from overdue slots and call `store.set('medication', 'patterns', patterns)`. Follow the RawPattern shape used by peer orchestrators.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Additive store write. No schema change.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: with an overdue slot, medication orchestrator's store contains non-empty 'medication.patterns' array with pattern='medication-overdue'.

mergedFindings.title: No fragment count cap — highly-conjunctive dump can generate unbounded fragments, exhausting Groq TPM and Voyage batch limits
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/segmentation.ts: pass1Segment() splits on sentence boundaries AND trilingual conjunctions with no cap. MAX_TEXT_CHARS = 10,000. workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump-classify.ts:327: `maxTokens = 256 * items.length + 256` — no ceiling, so a 100-fragment dump requests 25,856 output tokens from Groq in one call (beyond model context + 8k TPM free-tier). voyageEmbedBatch sends all fragment texts in one call; Voyage batch API limit is typically 128 inputs.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A very long conjunction-heavy dump (common ADHD brain-dump style) causes a 429 from Groq or embedding API error. The whole dump is lost with a soft 'rate_limited' or 502 error. User's words not archived.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: classifyBatch maxTokens calculation is unbounded. Voyage batch has undocumented cap in the codebase. A single pathological dump can exhaust the entire Groq TPM budget for the minute.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add `MAX_FRAGMENTS = 20` cap in dump.ts after fragmentsText is built: `if (fragmentsText.length > MAX_FRAGMENTS) fragmentsText.splice(MAX_FRAGMENTS)`. Cap classifyBatch maxTokens: `Math.min(maxTokens, 4096)`.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Cap only affects pathological inputs. Legitimate dumps rarely exceed 10 fragments.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: 50-fragment dump is capped at MAX_FRAGMENTS. Test: classifyBatch maxTokens never exceeds 4096.

mergedFindings.title: Vectorize routing cache has no prompt version — stale classifications served silently after system prompt updates
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/vectorize.ts: cache metadata schema (lines 19-27) has no promptVersion or schemaVersion field. dump.ts:456 upserts with only { userId, text, embedding, module, payload, confidence, language }. When SYSTEM_PROMPT in dump-classify.ts changes (new module, new routing rules), previously-cached embeddings return old classifications indefinitely — up to 30-day TTL.
mergedFindings.userImpact: After any routing rule change (frequent this sprint), cached users get wrong module routing for semantically similar phrases for up to 30 days. A 'cleaned the kitchen' fragment cached under old prompt stays as dump_only for a month.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Every prompt update silently invalidates the correctness of the entire cache without any mechanism to purge stale entries. The 30-day TTL means bugs introduced by prompt changes persist for a month.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a PROMPT_VERSION constant in dump-classify.ts (short hash or date-stamp). Include in Vectorize upsert metadata. On cache lookup, filter entries where promptVersion !== CURRENT_PROMPT_VERSION. Alternatively: bump a CACHE_NAMESPACE env var on deploy and use as key prefix.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium. Adding a Vectorize filter requires the field to be indexed. CACHE_NAMESPACE prefix approach is simpler.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: after PROMPT_VERSION bump, cacheLookup returns null for a semantically identical phrase.

mergedFindings.title: Pass-2 segmentation calls are serial — O(N×RTT) latency for multi-fragment dumps
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts:263-283: `for (const frag of pass1.fragments) { if (frag.needsPass2) { const split = await pass2Split(...) } }`. Every fragment with wordCount > 7 OR (wordCount > 4 AND no terminal punct) triggers a serial await. A typical 4-sentence ADHD dump with 8+ word sentences → 4 sequential Groq/Gemini round-trips before batch classification even starts. Each RTT ~500-1500ms → 2-6 seconds for pass-2 alone.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Noticeably slow dump processing for typical users. ADHD users often write long, comma-free brain dumps — the exact input that maximizes pass-2 serial depth.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Pass-2 is the dominant latency contributor for multi-fragment dumps. Serial calls also consume Groq TPM faster than necessary.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Fan out pass-2 calls: `const splitResults = await Promise.all(fragmentsNeedingPass2.map(frag => pass2Split(frag.text, ...)))`. Reduces pass-2 latency from O(N×RTT) to O(RTT).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — pass-2 calls are independent. Provider cascade inside each call already handles fallbacks.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that pass2Split is invoked concurrently when multiple fragments need pass-2 (mock and count concurrent calls).

mergedFindings.title: Confirmed-low-confidence cache entries never get confidence upgraded — perpetual confirm cards for repeated phrases
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/dump/DumpScreen.tsx:200-213: onKeep calls applyFragment(e.fragment) but never invalidates or updates the Vectorize cache entry. workers/ai-proxy/src/router/vectorize.ts:128-160: confidence is written once at AI-classification time, never updated. A 0.62-confidence fragment confirmed correct by the user still caches at 0.62. applyConfidencePolicy re-flags needsConfirm=true on every future cache hit for the same phrase.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Every repeated phrase that was originally uncertain keeps showing a confirm card forever, even after the user has confirmed it multiple times. Especially noticeable for ADHD users who repeat phrases regularly.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: The learn-from-confirmation signal is absent. The Vectorize cache cannot improve confidence from user feedback. This is the same learning gap that makes the learning loop's deferral model cold-start-only.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: On user confirmation (onKeep), fire-and-forget POST to update Vectorize cache entry's confidence to 0.9 for that text+module pair.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — requires a new write path from native to the AI worker on confirm.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that confirming a fragment triggers a cache update with elevated confidence.

mergedFindings.title: Rate-limit check skipped when userId resolves to null (no IP + no JWT sub) — authenticated user can bypass rate limit
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/index.ts:400-411: `const dumpUserId = await resolveUserIdForRateLimit(req, env); if (dumpUserId) { checkRate(...) }`. resolveUserIdForRateLimit (line 520-536) returns null when JWT verification fails AND no `x-user-id` AND no `cf-connecting-ip`. The JWT auth inside handleDumpRoute still blocks unauthenticated callers, but a valid-JWT + null-IP caller skips the rate-limit entirely. The comment says '10/min per user' which implies always-enforced.
mergedFindings.userImpact: An authenticated user with spoofed or absent CF IP header can spam the most expensive endpoint (Voyage embed + Groq classify) without rate limiting. In practice CF always injects cf-connecting-ip at the edge, so this mainly affects test/staging environments.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: AI budget burn in non-production environments. The CF Native Rate Limiter binding (AI_RATE_LIMITER) would catch this if deployed — but the KV fallback path has the null bypass.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Change: `const dumpUserId = resolveUserIdForRateLimit(...) ?? 'anonymous'; checkRate(env.AI_RATE_LIMITER, env.RATE_KV, dumpUserId)`. Remove the null gate entirely.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — tightens rate-limit layer only. JWT check in handleDumpRoute still blocks unauthenticated callers.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: valid JWT + no IP → still rate-limited (uses sub as key). Test: null sub + null IP → 401 from rate-limit layer.

mergedFindings.title: originalDump sent to client and archived locally is pre-scrub text — PII stripped from AI path echoed back in plaintext SQLite
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump.ts:255-256: `const { scrubbed: cleanDump } = scrubPII(combinedDump)` — cleanDump used for segmentation and AI. But line 497: `originalDump: combinedDump` — sends pre-scrub raw text. DumpScreen.tsx:165-168 calls `dumpArchive.record({ text: output.originalDump })` writing unscrubbed text to SQLite dump_archive.text. archive.ts:16 says 'stays local (SQLite) — no cloud write here'.
mergedFindings.userImpact: If a future feature adds server-side dump_archive mirroring, the unscrubbed text would transit the wire. For now impact is local storage only. Users who expect PII removal everywhere may be surprised. The tension is unresolved by any code comment.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Architectural ambiguity: scrubPII protects the AI/Vectorize path but not the local archive. No comment explains whether this is intentional. If scrub-everywhere is the intent, dumpArchive writes the wrong data.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Product decision required. If always-scrub: change `originalDump: combinedDump` to `originalDump: cleanDump`. If intentional (user owns their own data locally): add explicit comment at dump.ts:497 explaining why unscrubbed text is returned.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low if clarification only. Medium if switching to cleanDump — changes what users see in past-dump resurfacing.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: If always-scrub decision: test that dumpArchive.record is called with scrubbed text, not raw.

mergedFindings.title: hasConjunction check in pass1Segment is dead code — always false after conjunction split, making pass-2 trigger broader than intended
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/segmentation.ts:61-67: sentence.split(CONJ_RE) removes conjunctions from resulting parts by definition. Subsequent `CONJ_RE.test(part)` on line 65 tests whether any conjunction remains inside the already-split part — impossible. hasConjunction is therefore always false. Effective pass-2 trigger becomes: `wordCount > 7 || (wordCount > 4 && !hasTerminalPunct)` — the hasConjunction guard intended to prevent pass-2 on still-compound fragments is inoperative.
mergedFindings.userImpact: More 4-7 word fragments trigger unnecessary Groq/Gemini pass-2 calls than intended, increasing latency and token spend. Estimated ~30% pass-2 rate per dump.ts comments, likely higher than designed.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Dead code makes the condition harder to reason about. Actual behavior diverges from documented intent.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Remove hasConjunction variable and CONJ_RE.lastIndex reset. Simplify to: `needsPass2 = wordCount > 7 || (wordCount > 4 && !hasTerminalPunct)`. Document the intentional simplification.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low — current behavior is already shipping, fix makes the condition explicit.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Segmentation test: 5-word conjunction-joined input after split → verify needsPass2 matches the simplified formula.

mergedFindings.title: selectNoticings thresholdFor('high') returns identical value to 'medium' — high-capacity days get no additional noticing surface
mergedFindings.evidence: packages/logic/src/brain/select.ts:287-288: `thresholdFor(capacity)` returns `capacity === 'low' ? BASE_THRESHOLD + LOW_CAPACITY_BUMP : BASE_THRESHOLD` — both 'medium' and 'high' return BASE_THRESHOLD. brain-select.test.ts:140 confirms: `expect(thresholdFor('medium')).toBe(thresholdFor('high'))`. The 'high' capacity path is a dead branch.
mergedFindings.userImpact: On a high-energy day the assistant surfaces the same 2-3 noticings as a medium day. The intention (high capacity = can handle more) is not implemented. Minor UX gap since MAX_NOTICINGS=3 caps regardless.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Dead branch in capacity logic. Whether 'high' should lower the threshold or simply equal 'medium' is undocumented.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a comment at thresholdFor: 'high is intentionally identical to medium — MAX_NOTICINGS=3 is the binding constraint'. OR lower threshold for high: `capacity === 'high' ? BASE_THRESHOLD - 0.5 : BASE_THRESHOLD`.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Clarification or minor threshold change only.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Product decision — if high should behave differently, add test asserting `thresholdFor('high') < thresholdFor('medium')`.
mergedFindings.dissent: Round 1 noted this scoring algorithm as intentional product design in doNotTouch. Round 3 flags it as a confirmed dead branch. The resolution: the algorithm is intentional but the 'high' branch is a dead code gap within it — rounds agree on the code fact, they differ only on framing.

mergedFindings.title: remindIn sanity gate only blocks unit='day' > 30 — 'remind me in 100 hours' or '9999 seconds' passes through
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/remindIn.ts:49-71: `const MAX_DAYS = 30; if (u === 'day' && amount > MAX_DAYS) return null` — only 'day' unit is guarded. 'hr', 'min', 'sec' have no upper bounds. `{ amount: 99999, unit: 'hr' }` (11+ years) passes. `amount: 0.5, unit: 'day'` (12 hours) also passes.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A confusable LLM output like `{ amount: 1000, unit: 'hr' }` schedules a local notification 41 days out. In practice an edge case but wastes notification quota and could confuse users.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Not a security issue. Local notification quota waste. The 1-hour idempotency window is unrelated.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add per-unit caps: sec <= 3600, min <= 1440, hr <= 168, day <= 30. One extra guard object next to MAX_DAYS.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test: `computeScheduledAt(99999, 'hr', now)` returns null.

mergedFindings.title: Tier escalation relies on self-reported model confidence with no calibration guard — confidently-wrong fast model never escalates
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/route.ts:519-568: tier ladder escalates from fast to accurate model when `confidence < threshold` (e.g. 0.7). Confidence is read directly from model's tool_call output (line 562: args.confidence). No calibration, cross-validation, or spot-check against a ground-truth set. A fast model systematically overconfident on code-switched TR/EN or ambiguous purchase intents will always return confidence >= threshold and never escalate.
mergedFindings.userImpact: For modules with a tier ladder (admin, body, cycle, finance, goals, habits, medication, pets, sleep, work), a user whose dumps fall into the fast model's blind spots gets silently wrong routing without escalation. The needsConfirm path catches low-confidence errors but a high-confidence-wrong result bypasses it entirely.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: No empirical calibration data exists. The tier ladder is designed correctly but without a golden test set its reliability for edge cases is unknown.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a sampling audit: for 1-5% of requests (env var controlled), call BOTH models and log disagreements. Maintain a golden test set in workers/ai-proxy/tests/ for edge cases.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Sampling audit is additive and opt-in.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Golden test cases per module covering TR/EN code-switch, past/future tense, ambiguous purchase intent. Assert expected module + action on both model tiers.

mergedFindings.title: replenishment STATIC_FALLBACK_DAYS=14 applied for all items not in SHELF_LIFE_MAP — specialty items generate constant false 'replenish soon' nudges
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/replenishment.ts:192: single-purchase rows fall to low-data path → SHELF_LIFE_MAP drives daysLeft → if canonical missing from SHELF_LIFE_MAP, STATIC_FALLBACK_DAYS=14 applies. Cooking oil (monthly replacement) would show replenish nudge every 2 weeks.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Low-frequency items not in SHELF_LIFE_MAP always show 14-day replenishment estimate. For items spanning multiple months this triggers constant false nudges, creating notification fatigue.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Magic constant with no per-item awareness. Known cold-start limitation but undocumented.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Increase STATIC_FALLBACK_DAYS from 14 to 21 (less aggressive). Log unmapped canonicals for future SHELF_LIFE_MAP additions.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: canonical NOT in SHELF_LIFE_MAP with 1 purchase returns daysLeft based on 14-day fallback, not negative.

implementationRuntimeMismatches: dump.ts comment line 15 says 'tier ≥ 2' for crisis short-circuit but code at line 302 checks `if (crisis)` (any tier) — all three rounds confirm this mismatch

Module comment in packages/crisis-lexicon/src/index.ts:16 declares PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL as an alpha blocker, but the app is already installed on device with no CI gate — self-declared gate is inoperative

cacheHitBump is documented as a 'bump' (preserve entry, update hit count) but CF Vectorize upsert semantics replace metadata entirely — the bump deletes createdAt, turning a popularity signal into an expiry trigger

hit_count PATCH uses {increment:1} object syntax which PostgREST does not support for int columns — documented in two prior audit rounds (docs/audit/2026-06-18/round-2.md, round-3.md) but still not fixed; the feature exists in code but is permanently non-functional at runtime
hasConjunction in segmentation.ts is computed from already-split parts — always false at runtime, making the documented 'prevent pass-2 on still-compound fragments' guard a no-op

selectNoticings thresholdFor('high') is documented as a capacity-aware scoring adjustment but returns the same value as 'medium' — Round 1 flagged it as intentional product design; Round 3 confirmed it as a dead branch; the code fact is agreed upon, the intent is ambiguous
topRisks: Crisis tier-1 false-positives silently delete daily ADHD burnout dumps (P1, confidence 3) — 'tired of everything', 'can't take it anymore', 'nothing matters anymore' cause full dump loss
Three unreviewed crisis lexicons with no CI enforcement gate are live on device — missed/false signals in the only safety-critical feature (P1, confidence 3)
AI-returned module names never validated at runtime — hallucinated modules poison Vectorize cache and silently drop fragments (P2, confidence 3)
cacheHitBump drops createdAt — routing cache is effectively broken for all repeat users, the ADHD core use case (P2, confidence 2)
Medication overdue signals never reach brain home surface — desktop users and users with notifications off have no safety net for missed doses (P2, confidence 1)
quickWins: dump.ts:302 — change `if (crisis)` to `if (crisis?.tier >= 2)` (one line, prevents false-positive dump loss for tier-1 burnout phrases)
BrainDumpInput.tsx:192-196 — mirror the same tier >= 2 guard for the local pre-screen crisis check
vectorize.ts:117 — change default confidence from 0.8 to 0.6 (one number, makes cache-miss defaults conservative, matches UNCERTAIN_CONFIDENCE in dump-classify.ts:199)
vectorize.ts:171-185 — add `createdAt: row.createdAt ?? Date.now()` to cacheHitBump metadata (one field, fixes cache expiry for bumped entries)
dump-classify.ts parseBatchResults + classifyFragment — add `if (!MODULES.includes(parsed.module)) parsed.module = 'dump_only'` (prevents hallucinated modules reaching Vectorize)
Add CI test asserting `last_reviewed_by !== 'PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL'` for all three crisis lexicon JSON files — zero risk, blocks unsafe shipping
segmentation.ts:65-67 — remove dead hasConjunction check (two-line delete, makes pass-2 trigger explicit and correct)
remindIn.ts — add per-unit upper bound map (sec <= 3600, min <= 1440, hr <= 168) next to existing MAX_DAYS guard

angle: Agent 18 — Dead Code, Duplication & Reinvented Wheels
angleSummary: The Ollie monorepo carries a large belt of dead and duplicated code accumulated across multiple architecture pivots. The most severe issue is a P0 GDPR/App Store compliance gap: the only account-deletion endpoint lives in an undeployed legacy worker (apps/api), meaning user erasure requests silently fail. Below that, three P2 issues carry real data-leakage or wasted-compute risk: Turkish/Spanish names reach Anthropic unredacted because 5 of 6 ai-proxy routes import the weaker local pii.ts instead of the canonical @ollie/pii-scrub; the void:braindump:submitted event is never emitted from the native app, so 9 orchestrator per-dump optimization handlers are permanently dark; and the burhan (olive-tree game) orchestrator runs on every boot writing store keys that no UI ever reads. Beyond those, roughly 3,400 lines of dead logic (predict, consumption, corrections, astrology, ritual, prompts, research-stream, braindump-dispatch, routeViaHaiku) compile and test on every CI run for zero production utility. Duplication is systematic: two PII scrubbers, two brand lists, three queue implementations, three retry policies, three newId() copies, and a local json() helper in apns-push that @ollie/worker-http already exports. Quick wins (one-file import swaps) can close several of these in under an hour.

mergedFindings.title: Account deletion endpoint lives only in undeployed apps/api worker — GDPR and App Store erasure broken
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/api/src/worker.ts line 67 `.post('/account/delete', ...)` and apps/api/src/account-delete.ts (385 lines). .github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml deploys only ai-proxy, cron, apns-push, sentry-tunnel — apps/api is absent. grep of workers/ and apps/native/src/ for 'account/delete' returns zero hits. Confirmed absent from all live surfaces by direct filesystem check.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any user requesting account deletion (GDPR right-to-erasure, App Store guideline 5.1.1) hits a non-existent endpoint. This is an App Store submission blocker and a legal compliance failure.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: apps/api/src/account-delete.ts (385 lines) handles Clerk user deletion + Supabase data wipe + storage cleanup. None of it is reachable in production. The functionality does not exist in any deployed worker.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Port handleAccountDelete from apps/api/src/account-delete.ts into workers/ai-proxy as POST /account/delete with Clerk JWT verification matching the existing pattern. Add ai-proxy to deploy-workers.yml deploy matrix. Only delete apps/api after the migrated route is confirmed deployed and smoke-tested.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — must verify Clerk JWT + Supabase admin key are both available in ai-proxy worker env before porting.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Integration test: call POST /account/delete with a valid Clerk JWT, assert Supabase user row is deleted and Clerk user is deactivated. Add to deploy-workers.yml job output verification.

mergedFindings.title: void:braindump:submitted event never emitted from native app — 9 orchestrator per-dump handlers permanently dark
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 2: grep of apps/native/src/ returns zero calls to events.emit('void:braindump:submitted'). apps/native/src/dump/BrainDumpInput.tsx routes via routeDump → POST /route/dump → ai-proxy, then calls dispatchRouterOutput() in apps/native/src/modules/dispatch.ts. Round 3 confirms dispatch.ts does not emit the event. packages/orchestrator/src/{work.ts:446, sleep.ts:710, goals.ts:351, body.ts:332, habits.ts:246, admin.ts:865, dump.ts:181, matter-routing.ts:325, finance.ts:1254} — 9 handlers wait for it. Direct verification: grep of apps/native/src/ for the event string returns no output.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Silent functional gap: every dump triggers a full recompute across all 9 orchestrators instead of the module-filtered shortcut the braindump handler provides. On a low-capacity device this means more CPU work per dump than designed. Any logic written exclusively inside the braindump handler path (module-filter optimizations, scheduling shortcuts) is never executed.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: ~9 dead code branches across 9 orchestrator files. New orchestrators built to this event pattern will appear to work in unit tests but be silently misrouted in production.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In apps/native/src/modules/dispatch.ts, after dispatchRouterOutput() returns, emit: events.emit('void:braindump:submitted', { v: 2, items: dispatched.entries.map(...), raw: output.originalDump, ts: Date.now(), idempotency_key: dumpId, route_path: 'native' }). No orchestrator changes needed.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — additive change. The orchestrators already do independent store.subscribeKey recomputes as a fallback; this adds the optimized path on top.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Integration test: emit the event with a work-only item set and assert that the work orchestrator's braindump handler fires but sleep orchestrator's does not (v:2 module filter path).

mergedFindings.title: Dual PII scrubbers in ai-proxy: 5 of 6 routes use weaker EN-only local pii.ts — Turkish/Spanish names reach Anthropic unredacted
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: workers/ai-proxy/src/pii.ts (134 lines) acknowledged duplicate of @ollie/pii-scrub (459 lines). Round 2 confirms ai-proxy already imports @ollie/pii-scrub in router/feed-me.ts (line 28), proving the build pipeline supports workspace imports. Round 3 (most specific): pii.ts is imported by label.ts:27, telemetry.ts:30, index.ts:46, router/dump.ts:38, router/route.ts:28. Only feed-me.ts uses the locale-aware canonical package. pii.ts has no locale parameter; @ollie/pii-scrub handles Turkish names ('İrem', 'İsmail') and Spanish names. File header (lines 4-9) explicitly says 'keep these two implementations in sync' — an acknowledged divergence trap.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Turkish and Spanish first names in brain dumps are forwarded unredacted to Anthropic on the /route/dump, /label, /telemetry, /route/route, and root /index paths. This is a PII compliance failure on the five highest-traffic routes.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Any PII scrub fix or new locale pattern added to @ollie/pii-scrub must be manually mirrored to pii.ts or one path will continue to leak. The divergence is designed in by the 'keep in sync' comment.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In router/dump.ts, router/route.ts, label.ts, telemetry.ts, and index.ts: replace `import { scrubPII } from '../pii'` with `import { scrubPII } from '@ollie/pii-scrub'`. Add locale parameter from dump body language field. Add @ollie/pii-scrub to workers/ai-proxy/package.json if not already listed. The build pipeline already works (feed-me.ts proves it).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — feed-me.ts already does this import successfully. The canonical package is a superset of the local one.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Golden test in workers/ai-proxy: assert that 'İrem süt aldı' → redacted form on /route/dump. Add the same check for a Spanish name ('María compró').

mergedFindings.title: Burhan (olive-tree) orchestrator runs on every boot, writes store keys, has zero native UI consumers
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: packages/orchestrator/src/index.ts lines 27, 236, 282, 302, 345 wire createBurhanOrchestrator. Store key burhan.events is written on lifecycle events. grep of apps/native/src/ for 'burhan', 'BurhanBox', 'BurhanRoom' returns only prose comments in work module handoff notes (modules/work/WorkBox.tsx:749, bridge.ts:44, types.ts:89). Round 2 confirms no moduleRegistry entry. Round 3 confirms no moduleManifest.ts reference and no room file referencing burhan. All three rounds agree: orchestrator is wired and running; UI is entirely absent.
mergedFindings.userImpact: The olive-tree growth feature runs CPU overhead (event subscriptions, store writes) on every app boot but the user never sees output. It is a ghost feature burning cycles with no visible product value.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: packages/orchestrator/src/burhan.ts subscribes to lifecycle events and writes ('burhan','state') and ('burhan','lastAddedAt') store keys on every boot. No test coverage exists for burhan in packages/orchestrator/tests/.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Remove the createBurhanOrchestrator instantiation from packages/orchestrator/src/index.ts (lines 236, 282, 302, 345) until the UI lands. The store keys will stop being written; the source file can stay for when BurhanBox.tsx is built.

mergedFindings.title: 6 dead modules in @ollie/logic totaling ~2,122 lines (predict, consumption, corrections, astrology, ritual, prompts)
mergedFindings.dissent: Round 1 lists 7 orphans (also includes 'stats' and 'products') with slightly different counts. Round 2 confirms predict (981 lines) and products (148 lines) dead. Round 3 counts 6 modules (predict, consumption, corrections, astrology, ritual, prompts — 2,122 lines) but does not list 'stats' or 'products' separately. All rounds agree the modules are re-exported from packages/logic/src/index.ts with zero external import sites. The exact list is: predict, consumption, corrections, astrology, ritual, prompts (all 3 rounds), plus products and stats (rounds 1-2 only). Combined dead line count is ~2,270+ lines.

Round 3: ritual is referenced by prompts internally — both are dead. Round 2: predict/products confirmed 981+148 lines with no callers. Round 1: corrections/consumption/stats/ritual/prompts confirmed dead by exhaustive caller search.

Delete if product decision confirms cancellation; keep source if features are planned. astrology and predict were flagged as 'follow-up phases' in logic/src/index.ts:10 — confirm with Serra before deleting.

mergedFindings.title: consumption/brands.ts and pii-scrub/brand-allowlist.ts maintain overlapping brand lists independently — silently destroys AI signal
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: packages/logic/src/consumption/brands.ts exports BRAND_SEED — 150+ entry structured catalog with category_l1/l2, aliases, keys. packages/pii-scrub/src/brand-allowlist.ts exports a separate flat BRAND_ENTRIES string array with many of the same brands, maintained independently for 'never scrub brands' use-case. No shared source between them.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A brand added to BRAND_SEED for routing/detection will still be scrubbed if not also added to BRAND_ENTRIES. This silently destroys brand signal in the AI routing pipeline. The two lists will diverge as brands are added to one but not the other.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Two independent brand catalogs with overlapping coverage and no sync mechanism. The scrubber's allow-list is a manual subset of the detection catalog.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Make brand-allowlist.ts derive its entries from BRAND_SEED: import BRAND_SEED from @ollie/logic/consumption and build BRAND_ENTRIES as BRAND_SEED.flatMap(b => b.aliases). Single source of truth. (Note: consumption module is currently dead per finding above — wire consumption or extract BRAND_SEED to a standalone file first.)
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — pii-scrub already operates in the same workspace ecosystem.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test that every key in BRAND_SEED has at least one alias present in BRAND_ENTRIES.

mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: After migrating /account/delete to workers/ai-proxy (P0 fix), delete the apps/api directory. Do not delete until the migration is deployed and verified.

mergedFindings.title: DAY_MS / HOUR_MS inline-redefined in 12+ production source files instead of using @ollie/logic/util
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: grep confirms const DAY_MS = 86_400_000 defined in at least 12 production .ts files: packages/logic/src/brain/harm.ts:23, packages/orchestrator/src/body-correlations.ts:45, body-weekly.ts:61, body-signals.ts:36-37, sleep.ts:85, admin.ts:66, body.ts:50, cycle.ts:56, apps/native/src/notify/datelessLadder.ts:51, modules/brain/noticings.ts:28, modules/brain/copy.ts:47, plus others. Canonical constants exported from packages/logic/src/util/index.ts. Some files that already import from @ollie/logic/util still redeclare DAY_MS locally.

mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In each file that already imports from @ollie/logic/util, add DAY_MS/HOUR_MS to the destructure and remove the local const. For remaining files, add the import. One PR, zero behavior change.

mergedFindings.title: Three independent in-memory queue implementations across sync, research-stream, and notifications
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: (1) packages/sync/src/index.ts lines 159-170: QueueEntry[] persisted to store, readQueue()/writeQueue(), QUEUE_CAP=10000. (2) packages/research-stream/src/index.ts lines 124-310: ResearchEvent[] persisted to store, QUEUE_CAP=5000, same flush+batch pattern. (3) packages/notifications/src/aggregator.ts lines 24-97: in-memory NotificationSpec[] with enqueue/flush/size. All three implement: enqueue-with-cap, read-from-store, write-to-store, drain on flush.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any fix to queue-cap logic, store serialization, or flush error handling must be applied independently to all three. Bugs found in one won't be caught in the others.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Three divergent queue policies. research-stream queue is already dead (see above), so this is primarily sync vs notifications duplication in live code.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Extract a generic createStoredQueue<T>(store, key, cap) into @ollie/sync or a new @ollie/queue package. Wire sync and (when activated) research-stream to use it. Notifications queue is in-memory only and can remain separate or get a simpler generic.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — touches sync which is persistence-critical. Needs thorough testing with fake stores.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Shared test suite for the extracted queue covering: enqueue, cap overflow, flush-batch, empty-flush.

mergedFindings.title: Three independent retry implementations (api/client.ts, sync/retry.ts, ai-proxy/invites.ts bare loop) — invites.ts has no delay between retries
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 2: (1) packages/api/src/client.ts:134 doFetch() with retry.max/baseDelayMs, jitter-less exponential. (2) packages/sync/src/retry.ts:101 createBackoffScheduler() maxAttempts=8, exponential, jitter-less. (3) workers/ai-proxy/src/invites.ts:112 bare `for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 3; attempt++)` with no delay, no jitter, no dead-letter. The invites.ts loop is the most fragile: no cooldown between invite-code uniqueness-conflict retries.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Under concurrent invite creation, all 3 retries hit the same collision window with zero delay and can all fail. Rare at current scale but a latent bug.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Three divergent retry policies across the system. Workers cannot use @ollie/api directly (CF runtime vs Node), but a shared workers/lib/retry.ts could be vendored across workers.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In workers/ai-proxy/src/invites.ts:112, add `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 50 * 2**attempt))` between retries. Long-term: add workers/lib/retry.ts with a CF-compatible backoff helper.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low for invites.ts one-liner. Medium for full consolidation.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test for invites.ts retry: mock Supabase POST to fail twice then succeed; assert third attempt returns invite URL.

mergedFindings.title: newId() (crypto.randomUUID fallback) has 3 private copies alongside the canonical export in apps/native/src/storage/id.ts
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 3: apps/native/src/storage/id.ts:10 canonical export. All 13 module repos import correctly from storage/id.ts — only dump/ and braindump-dispatch stray.

mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In apps/native/src/dump/archive.ts and BrainDumpInput.tsx, replace private function with `import { newId } from '../storage/id'`. For braindump-dispatch.ts, inline `crypto.randomUUID()` directly (orchestrator always runs in a modern runtime) or fix as part of the braindump-dispatch legacy cleanup.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Near-zero — behavioral equivalence guaranteed.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None — existing id.ts tests cover the canonical implementation.

mergedFindings.title: levenshtein1 in journal/search.ts is a one-liner alias of util/index.ts levenshtein — unnecessary duplicate export
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 1: packages/logic/src/journal/search.ts:28 defines `export function levenshtein1(a, b) { return levenshtein(a, b, 1); }`. The canonical levenshtein with cap parameter lives in packages/logic/src/util/index.ts:172. levenshtein1 is only called inside journal/search.ts itself.

mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Two named exports for the same operation in the same package.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Delete levenshtein1 from journal/search.ts. Replace internal calls with levenshtein(a, b, 1) from util.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Near-zero — levenshtein1 is only called inside the same file.

mergedFindings.title: workers/apns-push has a private json() helper instead of importing the identical export from @ollie/worker-http
mergedFindings.evidence: Round 3: workers/apns-push/src/index.ts:195 defines `function json(obj: unknown, status = 200): Response { return new Response(JSON.stringify(obj), { status, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }); }`. @ollie/worker-http exports an identical helper. workers/apns-push/package.json does not list @ollie/worker-http as a dependency (while workers/ai-proxy, workers/cron, workers/sentry-tunnel all do).

angleSummary: The documentation layer of the Ollie monorepo is severely stale across every major doc. README.md, CODEBASE_MAP.md, DATA_SCHEMA.md, DEPLOY_TODO.md, and IOS_SETUP.md all describe architectures, commands, bundle IDs, or product names that are factually wrong. The app moved from Electron+Capacitor+apps/web to Tauri+apps/native months ago, but no doc was updated. Three runbook errors (wrong product name, wrong bundle ID, wrong command) will cause an operator to either test the wrong app, sign for the wrong bundle ID, or get a white screen during iOS installation. All fixes are documentation-only and zero-risk.

mergedFindings.title: README.md describes a completely defunct architecture (apps/web + Electron + Capacitor) with dev commands that fail
mergedFindings.evidence: README.md lines 8-31 show apps/web, apps/desktop (Electron), apps/ios (Capacitor); lines 30-31 give `pnpm electron:dev` and `pnpm ios:open`. `ls /Users/serrayildirim/ollie/apps/` returns only `api` and `native`. The correct dev command (`pnpm --filter native tauri dev`) is absent from README. Git log shows 289 commits since the README's baseline of 31.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Any new contributor following README will run commands that fail (electron:dev, ios:open, pnpm dev) and never get the app running. The entire setup section is a dead end.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Rewrite README dev section: replace apps/web/desktop/ios block with apps/native (Tauri v2) + apps/api (CF Worker); replace `pnpm dev` with `pnpm --filter native tauri dev`; remove all Electron/Capacitor/apps/web references.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: None — purely documentation.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Optional CI lint step that fails if README contains 'electron:dev' or 'ios:open'.

mergedFindings.title: CODEBASE_MAP.md is a 43-day stale snapshot (2026-05-11): explicitly states crypto/sync/apps/api do not exist (they do), lists 4 packages (16 exist), misses 5 native modules and entire rooms/ IA layer

All three now exist. Current HEAD is 25e3828 (2026-06-24) — 289 commits, not 31.

A developer onboarding from this doc will have a completely wrong mental model of the codebase.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add stale banner at top of CODEBASE_MAP.md: '⚠️ STALE — snapshot 2026-05-11, pre-Tauri, pre-backend. Do not use for architecture reference. See docs/MASTER_ROADMAP_2026-06-15.md + docs/CHECKLIST.md.' Full rewrite deferred — stale marking is sufficient immediate fix.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: None to mark as stale. Full rewrite risk: medium (could introduce inaccuracies).
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None.

mergedFindings.title: IOS_SETUP.md states bundle ID 'com.ollie.app' throughout but iOS builds use 'app.ollie.ollie' — silently breaks App Group / snapshot writes on iOS
mergedFindings.evidence: IOS_SETUP.md lines 23, 105, 109, 192, 215 all say 'com.ollie.app'. tauri.ios.conf.json line 2 sets 'identifier: app.ollie.ollie'. gen/apple/ExportOptions.plist also uses app.ollie.ollie. RELEASE.md and CHECKLIST.md correctly state 'iOS bundle id app.ollie.ollie (com.ollie.app başkasında — değişmez karar)'. June-18 audit (docs/audit/2026-06-18/) flagged that GROUP_ID uses com.ollie.app prefix causing containerURLForSecurityApplicationGroupIdentifier to return None on iOS, silently failing all snapshot writes.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Developer following IOS_SETUP.md signing section will configure provisioning for the wrong bundle ID. App Group / widget snapshot-write feature (A7) is silently broken on iOS with no error surfaced to user.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Update IOS_SETUP.md: replace all iOS-context 'com.ollie.app' with 'app.ollie.ollie'; add a note that tauri.conf.json = macOS (com.ollie.app), tauri.ios.conf.json overrides to app.ollie.ollie for iOS. Separately fix GROUP_ID platform-conditional split in group_container.rs (low-risk Rust change).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Doc fix: zero. group_container.rs fix: low risk.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Unit test that group_container.rs returns a valid container path on the iOS target identifier (app.ollie.ollie).

mergedFindings.title: Plaid integration removed from product but plaid_items/plaid_inbox migrations remain active and account-delete.ts still sweeps them — no documentation explains the orphan state
mergedFindings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260514000009_plaid_items.sql and 20260514000010_plaid_inbox.sql exist and create real tables. apps/api/src/account-delete.ts lines 114-115 still reference both tables. mergedFindings.title: DEPLOY_TODO.md §4 instructs setting VITE_USER_HASH_SALT as a client-side env var — actual salt is a server-side worker secret (USER_HASH_SALT in workers/ai-proxy)
mergedFindings.evidence: DEPLOY_TODO.md §4 describes VITE_USER_HASH_SALT as a client-side .env.local var. workers/ai-proxy/src/telemetry.ts lines 47 and 56 derive user hashes server-side using the worker secret USER_HASH_SALT. The VITE_* version does not appear anywhere in live code. If the worker secret is unset, telemetry.ts logs a warning but proceeds — hashes are derived unsalted.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Operator following DEPLOY_TODO will set a client-side env var with no effect. If the worker secret USER_HASH_SALT was never set (because the doc pointed the wrong direction), all user hashes in telemetry are unsalted — a privacy issue.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace DEPLOY_TODO §4 VITE_USER_HASH_SALT instruction with: 'cd workers/ai-proxy && wrangler secret put USER_HASH_SALT'.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: None.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: None.

angleSummary: Cross-cutting launch-readiness audit of the Ollie monorepo (branch redesign/olive-neumorphic, closed-alpha target). Covers distribution blockers, silent data-loss, auth/security gaps, App Store compliance, and privacy/consent wiring. 3 rounds × 8 findings each; merged to 15 unique findings ranked by severity then confidence.

mergedFindings.title: Identity migration 20260618000002 (uuid→text) not confirmed applied to prod — silent data loss for all real users
mergedFindings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260618000002_identity_clerk_text.sql: six tables (encrypted_state, finance_records, scheduled_jobs, push_tokens, plaid_inbox, plaid_items) still have user_id uuid FK to auth.users. docs/audit/2026-06-18/REMEDIATION_ROADMAP_2026-06-24.md Lane C '#22 identity (CRITICAL): apply 20260618000002 to prod. Without it, real users reminders + finance sync + push silently fail.' Round 1 and 2 treated the migration as applied (inferred from dogfood memory); Round 3 found explicit NOT-YET-APPLIED marker in the migration header.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Every new user's INSERTs into encrypted_state, finance_records, scheduled_jobs fail silently — Clerk user_id 'user_2abc...' is not a valid uuid. Sync appears to work locally (localStorage-backed) but all server-side durable data is lost per user with no error shown.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: auth.uid() returns NULL under Clerk JWT so all RLS on the six tables evaluates to empty. Supabase REST returns 422/400 on insert. The entire Layer-2 server reminder pipeline produces zero rows.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Run `supabase db push` (or apply migration via dashboard SQL editor) to prod, then apply 20260618000003 and 20260618000004 in order. Verify: SELECT pg_typeof(user_id) FROM encrypted_state LIMIT 1 → should return 'text'.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. The migration uses USING user_id::text (safe widening cast); all existing rows preserved. Migration file is already written and reviewed.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: After applying: insert one row into encrypted_state with a Clerk-format user_id from a live test session; confirm no 422/400 from Supabase REST.
mergedFindings.dissent: Rounds 1 and 2 inferred the migration was applied because dogfood data persists (memory: 'motor pretty much çalışıyor'). Round 3 found explicit 'DRAFT / NOT yet applied' markers in the migration headers and the 2026-06-24 remediation roadmap. Cannot confirm prod DB state without live Supabase access. Flagged P0 because if Round 3 is correct the entire server-side data model is broken.

mergedFindings.title: iOS push notifications non-functional end-to-end: empty aps-environment entitlement, no token registration code, push_tokens empty in prod
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple/native_iOS/native_iOS.entitlements: <dict/> (empty body). docs/SERVER_PUSH_ROADMAP_2026-06-24.md:16 states 'push_tokens is EMPTY in prod' and 'iOS most likely has no push capability'. No tauri-plugin-mobile-push or APNs token registration code exists anywhere in apps/native/src/. Round 3 corroborated via absence of any push registration path in bridge/index.ts and notify/serverReminderBridge.ts.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Every durable server-initiated reminder (watcher offers, dateless-ladder, scheduled jobs) silently vanishes. The entire Layer-2 proactive-assistant vision is inert. Only on-device local notifications (app open/backgrounded on macOS) work.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: cron worker scans scheduled_jobs but push_tokens is always empty → zero APNs calls ever happen. apns-push worker is deployed with valid credentials but has zero consumers.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: (1) Enable Push Notifications on App ID app.ollie.ollie in Apple Developer portal and add aps-environment to iOS entitlements in Xcode. (2) Integrate tauri-plugin-mobile-push in an isolated worktree. (3) On token-received, POST to /register-token with Clerk bearer. Documented in docs/SERVER_PUSH_ROADMAP_2026-06-24.md.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium. P1 is Apple portal changes (no code risk). P2 requires ObjC runtime injection via plugin — vet plugin maintenance before merging.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Integration test: verify a row appears in push_tokens after device launch. E2E: reminder created → app closed → APNs push delivered.

mergedFindings.title: TestFlight install confirmed broken (installCount=0 ever) — no working OTA distribution channel for closed alpha
mergedFindings.evidence: docs/CHECKLIST.md Faz 0.5: 'Serra'nın iPhone'u: KABLODAN KURULDU (2026-06-11) — TestFlight not available hatası verdiği için bypass.' Memory project_ollie_testflight_fix.md: 'install fails… installCount 0 ever; Apple bug report SENT 2026-06-22, awaiting reply.' External tester acikbetul@icloud.com ACCEPTED but never installed. Round 2 confirmed project.yml CFBundleVersion=1.1.0 vs tauri.conf.json version=1.1.1 — mismatched build numbers block re-upload. Round 3 flagged APNS_BUNDLE_ID secret may be wrong (com.ollie.app vs app.ollie.ollie).
mergedFindings.userImpact: No external testers can receive the app. Closed alpha cannot start. Cable-install requires developer mode and physical access — not viable for external testers.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Distribution pipeline works at Xcode/altool level but Apple-side delivery is broken. Build number mismatch (project.yml 1.1.0 vs tauri.conf.json 1.1.1) will cause upload rejection independently of the Apple bug.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: (1) Fix project.yml CFBundleVersion to 1.1.1 (one-line change). (2) Verify APNS_BUNDLE_ID secret = 'app.ollie.ollie' not 'com.ollie.app'. (3) Submit fresh build 1.1.1 to TestFlight — may bypass stuck 0.1.0 state. (4) Track Apple bug report; if no reply in 1 week, try external TestFlight link or AdHoc/Diawi as contingency.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low code risk. Apple-side only for the distribution issue; project.yml is a one-line fix.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Smoke: confirm tester can install from TestFlight link within 24h of build processing. Install on second device via TestFlight (not cable) and complete one dump.

mergedFindings.title: Account deletion: backend handler deletes by Supabase uuid but tables will hold Clerk text user_id after migration — GDPR + App Store violation
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/api/src/account-delete.ts line 274-295: verifyJwtAndExtractUserId calls Supabase /auth/v1/user and returns a uuid-shaped Supabase user id. After migration 20260618000002 all tables use Clerk text ids ('user_2abc…'). DELETE WHERE user_id = <supabase-uuid> will find zero rows. Round 2 confirmed the UI surface is missing entirely from Router.tsx (zero results for deleteAccount, account-delete, AccountDelete in apps/native/src/). Round 3 adds the Clerk/uuid mismatch angle. Both rounds confirmed the worker endpoint itself is implemented (apps/api/src/account-delete.ts).
mergedFindings.userImpact: User requests account deletion, gets success response, but all data rows remain. App Store Review Guideline 5.1.1 (effective June 2023) requires in-app account deletion — blocks any beta expansion or App Store submission. GDPR right-to-erasure promise in privacy policy is broken.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Silent no-op delete after migration 0002 is applied. No error returned to client. Also: UI surface does not exist at all in the native app, so no user can trigger the endpoint regardless.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: (1) Add a 'Delete Account' button to Router.tsx SettingsScreen with a confirm dialog. (2) Fix account-delete.ts to verify JWT via Clerk JWKS (same verifyClerkJwt pattern as ai-proxy) and derive user_id from JWT sub claim. Sequence: fix code before or simultaneously with applying migration 0002.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — requires careful sequencing with migration 0002. If migration is applied before the handler is fixed, there is a window where deletes use the wrong id type.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Integration test: create row with Clerk-format text user_id, call runAccountDelete with Clerk JWT, assert row count = 0. E2E: tap delete → confirm → assert Supabase rows cleared and Clerk session invalidated.

mergedFindings.title: /brain-dump and /v1/messages Anthropic proxy endpoints require no authentication — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exposed to any internet caller
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/index.ts:436-500: after all named-route handlers, the fallthrough block for /brain-dump or /v1/messages applies only a rate-limit keyed on caller-controlled x-user-id header or IP. No JWT verification, no secret check. No auth enforced before forwarding to ANTHROPIC_URL with env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The legitimate app path /route/dump requires Clerk JWT; the legacy proxy does not.
mergedFindings.userImpact: External abuse can exhaust the Anthropic budget, causing 429s for all legitimate users. Financial damage proportional to abuse volume.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Per-IP rate limit (10/min) is the only guard. CF IP spoofing + multiple IPs trivially bypass it. brainDump() is exported in workers.ts but has zero call sites outside of api/ definitions.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Return 404 for /brain-dump and /v1/messages in ai-proxy/src/index.ts — the endpoints are dead code (brainDump() has zero confirmed call sites in apps/native/src/). This is a 2-line change. Alternatively add verifyClerkJwt before the fallthrough block.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low. brainDump() has zero call sites in apps/native. Removing or 404-ing the endpoint has no user-facing impact.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: POST /brain-dump without Authorization → 401/404. POST /v1/messages without Authorization → 401/404.

mergedFindings.title: Crisis lexicon all three languages marked PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL — ships unreviewed to alpha
mergedFindings.evidence: packages/crisis-lexicon/data/lexicon.en.json line 4: '"last_reviewed_by": "PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL"'. Same in lexicon.tr.json and lexicon.es.json. packages/crisis-lexicon/src/index.ts line 15: 'Lexicons are PENDING_SERRA_APPROVAL — last_reviewed_by must be @serra before any merge that ships to alpha.' MASTER_ROADMAP states crisis-word-list approval is 'the only pending security gate from Serra before alpha'.
mergedFindings.userImpact: False positives: user gets distressing crisis banner for benign input. False negatives: user in crisis gets no signal. Both outcomes are serious in a mental-health-adjacent app.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: The crisis detection code path is live and wired; the lexicon data driving it is the only unreviewed component.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Serra reviews all three JSON lexicons and changes last_reviewed_by to '@serra' + sets review_date. Zero code change needed — purely a human review and sign-off step.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero code risk. Metadata-only change after review.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: No new tests needed — the lexicon test suite already covers detection; sign-off is a human review step.

mergedFindings.title: invite_funnel views run as security_definer (bypass RLS) — migration 20260618000004 is DRAFT and not applied to prod
mergedFindings.evidence: supabase/migrations/20260618000004_security_invoker_views_and_idempotent_tables.sql line 5: '-- DRAFT — NOT yet applied to prod.' Original 20260519000003_invite_funnel_views.sql creates invite_funnel and invite_funnel_by_channel with no security_invoker option (security_definer by default). Any caller with SELECT on these views can enumerate all invited users' activation steps + session/retention/dump counts across all users, bypassing RLS.
mergedFindings.userImpact: A caller with SELECT on invite_funnel (e.g. a compromised worker key) can enumerate all users' activation steps and session data. Active privacy risk for alpha friend testers.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: RLS on underlying tables is bypassed entirely for anyone who can reach these views. The migration fix is idempotent and already written.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Apply migration 20260618000004 to prod (CREATE OR REPLACE is idempotent). 2-minute operation. The grant block in the same migration also re-asserts service_role-only access.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Zero risk. SQL is already written, tested, reviewed. Only changes security context of two read-only views.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: After applying: confirm `SET ROLE authenticated; SELECT * FROM invite_funnel;` returns 0 rows (RLS blocks non-service-role).

mergedFindings.title: Consent gate not wired in native app — users boot and use the app without ever seeing a consent screen
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src/main.tsx and apps/native/src/navigation/Router.tsx: zero imports or references to @ollie/consent, ConsentScreen, ConsentGate, hasNecessaryConsent(), or any consent gate. packages/consent/src/index.ts doc at line 108 says 'written by ConsentScreen, read by App.tsx's boot gate' — but the real main.tsx/Router.tsx never call it. Auth gate is Clerk SignIn → Router directly with no consent step. Round 1 confirmed via grep; Round 2 confirmed via direct file inspection; Round 3 confirmed via packages/research-stream/src/index.ts showing consent check uses only hasNecessaryConsent() which is structurally true for any booted user.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Privacy policy states necessary consent is required for app to run. App violates its own stated consent contract. GDPR/CCPA: sending Sentry error data without asking is legal exposure. App Store: trust-breaker if reviewers check privacy policy against behavior.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: research_optin = null for all users (no consent record ever written). @ollie/consent package's CONSENT_PIVOT_TS logic is dead letter. B2B research pipeline would send data without user agreement if ever wired.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add a ConsentGate component in Router.tsx that checks hasNecessaryConsent() on mount; if false, renders a one-screen necessary-consent prompt before showing the Router. packages/consent has the read/write API already built and tested.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. packages/consent is already built and tested; just needs a render gate wired into the auth-passed branch of main.tsx.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: fresh store (no consent key) keeps user on consent screen. Test: accepting consent lets router render. Test: skipping → app does not boot.

mergedFindings.title: Voyage + Gemini + CF API keys were chat-exposed and rotation is an unchecked alpha gate
mergedFindings.evidence: docs/CHECKLIST.md Faz 3: 'Token rotasyonu: Voyage + Gemini + CF API token (hepsi chat'e sızdı, beta gate olarak işaretliydi) — UNCHECKED (⬜)'. docs/audit-2026-06-09/FINAL_AUDIT.md:479 confirms VOYAGE_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY are in local .env and .dev.vars (gitignored) and flags them as chat-exposed. Voyage is in the critical path for every brain dump.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Attacker with keys can (a) drain Voyage embedding credits causing all AI routing to fail; (b) drain Gemini quota; (c) with CF API token, modify or delete Cloudflare resources including workers themselves.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Voyage is in critical path for every brain dump (embedding before Groq classify). CF API token compromise most severe — could delete KV namespaces or workers.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Rotate all three before any external tester receives the app: (1) revoke old Voyage key → issue new → wrangler secret put VOYAGE_API_KEY; (2) revoke old Gemini key → wrangler secret put GEMINI_API_KEY; (3) revoke old CF API token → update GitHub Actions secret CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN. This is the Faz 3 gate per CHECKLIST.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Standard key rotation. Deploy workers after rotation. Test: one brain dump routes correctly end-to-end after new keys.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Post-rotation smoke: one real brain dump → verify Voyage + Groq path still live.

mergedFindings.title: APNs push token registration uses shared static secret instead of per-user Clerk JWT — any caller with the secret can register tokens for arbitrary user_ids
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/api/src/worker.ts line 308: `if (!auth.startsWith('Bearer ') || auth.slice(7) !== env.REGISTER_SHARED_SECRET)`. Body accepts arbitrary `user_id` field (line 303). No per-user identity verification — any client that knows the shared secret can register a token for any user_id, causing push notifications destined for user A to deliver to user B's device.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Push notification misdirection. An attacker with the shared secret could redirect sensitive health/cycle/medication reminders to a device they control. Concrete cross-user privacy risk for friend testers.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Shared secret stored as wrangler env var (not per-user). Token stored in KV keyed as user:${body.user_id} with no JWT ownership check.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Replace shared-secret auth on /register-token with verifyClerkJwt and derive user_id from verified JWT sub claim, ignoring client-supplied body.user_id. REGISTER_SHARED_SECRET can remain for /send (server-to-server only).
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium — requires native app to pass Clerk JWT instead of shared secret when registering tokens.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: POST /register-token with valid Clerk JWT but body.user_id differing from JWT sub → assert stored user_id equals JWT sub, not body field.

mergedFindings.title: iOS build number mismatch: project.yml CFBundleVersion=1.1.0 vs tauri.conf.json version=1.1.1 — Apple will reject re-upload
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple/project.yml line 89: CFBundleVersion: '1.1.0'. apps/native/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json line 4: version: '1.1.1'. apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple/native_iOS/Info.plist already shows 1.1.1 (regenerated) but project.yml is stale. Any upload at the same build number as a prior submission is rejected by App Store Connect.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Build rejected by App Store Connect on upload. TestFlight distribution blocked until resolved — compounding the existing TestFlight failure.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Stale generated config file causes CFBundleVersion mismatch. Xcode and App Store Connect treat CFBundleVersion (build number) as the unique identifier per submission.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple/project.yml, update CFBundleVersion to '1.1.1'. Add a CI check asserting project.yml CFBundleVersion == tauri.conf.json version.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low — one-line change in a generated config file.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: CI check: assert project.yml CFBundleVersion == tauri.conf.json version on every PR.

mergedFindings.title: CSP is null in tauri.conf.json + NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent=true — no content-security controls on the app WebView
mergedFindings.evidence: apps/native/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json line 24: `"csp": null`. apps/native/src-tauri/gen/apple/native_iOS/Info.plist lines 25-29: NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent: true. With CSP null, any injected script via a third-party JS dependency or malformed AI response rendered as HTML runs with full app permissions (localStorage, Tauri event bus, local notifications, Rust commands).
mergedFindings.userImpact: Supply-chain XSS in any npm dependency (Clerk, React, etc.) or an AI response rendered unsanitized could read stored module data or schedule malicious notifications. Tolerable for closed alpha, must be hardened before public beta.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Tauri allowlist is the primary defense but a null CSP removes defense-in-depth. WKWebView origin is localhost:9527 which partially limits external fetch, but inline script execution is unrestricted.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Set a minimal CSP in tauri.conf.json: `default-src 'self' http://localhost:9527; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co https://*.workers.dev https://*.clerk.accounts.dev`. Test that Clerk and Sentry still initialize.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Medium. CSP can break Clerk's embedded iframe, Sentry replay, and Fontsource CDN imports. Must test all auth flows and error reporting after adding.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Browser dev-tools: confirm CSP header present on app load. Negative test: confirm inline script injection is blocked.

mergedFindings.title: Privacy policy still lists Plaid as an active integration — Plaid was product-removed, creating material misrepresentation
mergedFindings.evidence: marketing/privacy.md line 34 describes bank transactions fetched via Plaid. Line 82 lists Plaid in the third-party table. Line 114 lists plaid_inbox + plaid_items in the account deletion cascade. Per memory: Plaid/TrueLayer integration REMOVED entirely (commit 47a6fa6 — product decision). apps/api/src/account-delete.ts lines 114-115 still DELETEs from plaid_inbox and plaid_items as dead-code.
mergedFindings.userImpact: App Store review reads the privacy policy URL. Listing Plaid as a data controller for bank credentials when it is not integrated is a material misrepresentation. Could trigger rejection or regulatory complaint.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Dead-code delete from empty tables is harmless but misleading. Privacy policy text is actively incorrect.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Remove Plaid references from marketing/privacy.md and marketing/terms.md. Remove the plaid rows from the deletion cascade in apps/api/src/account-delete.ts.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Very low — documentation and dead-code cleanup only.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Automated lint: grep for 'plaid' in marketing/ and CI-fail if found.

mergedFindings.title: chores and mood modules classified by Layer-1 router but have no Layer-2 config — any re-route for these modules returns 404, fragments silently dropped
mergedFindings.evidence: workers/ai-proxy/src/router/dump-classify.ts line 20-36: MODULES array includes 'mood' and 'chores'. workers/ai-proxy/src/router/route.ts line 118-130: MODULE_CONFIGS only includes admin, grocery, body, cycle, finance, goals, habits, medication, pets, sleep, work. Line 240: returns `{ error: 'unknown_module', module }` 404. No chores.config.ts or mood.config.ts in workers/ai-proxy/src/modules/.
mergedFindings.userImpact: Chores and mood dumps that the AI is uncertain about (grey-zone 0.60-0.79 confidence) are silently dropped to dump_only archive. 'I vacuumed' or 'feeling anxious' at borderline confidence get no confirmation card and no module routing. User sees no error.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: Two module names are routable by classification but unhandled by the module config layer. Any needsConfirm re-route for these returns 404 to the client.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: Add chores.config.ts and mood.config.ts to workers/ai-proxy/src/modules/ following the pattern of habits.config.ts, then register them in MODULE_CONFIGS in route.ts.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Additive change. Existing dump_only fallback unchanged; fix only adds a working path.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Add route tests for POST /route/chores and POST /route/mood similar to tests/habits-route.test.ts.

mergedFindings.title: Research-stream telemetry gates on `necessary` consent (structurally always true) instead of `research_optin` — behavioral data ships without explicit opt-in
mergedFindings.evidence: packages/research-stream/src/index.ts line 157-165: hasConsent() calls hasNecessaryConsent(deps.store). packages/consent/src/index.ts: necessary is structurally true for any user who can boot the app. Round 3 docs/audit/2026-06-18/round-1.md line 471-474 confirms: 'structured session/module/retention rows POST for every user by default; research_optin only gates the free-text corpus path.' Round 2 confirmed research orchestrator is also never mounted in native app (zero call sites for createResearchOrchestrator in apps/native/src/).
mergedFindings.userImpact: Behavioral telemetry (module visits, dump count per session, d1 retention) sent to Supabase for every user regardless of research opt-in. Consent copy presented to users describes necessary as crash analytics + Sentry replay — behavioral module-visit data is not disclosed there. Trust risk before public beta.
mergedFindings.technicalImpact: hasNecessaryConsent() = true for all booted users → behavioral rows post unconditionally. research_optin toggle affects only the free-text corpus path, not structured telemetry.
mergedFindings.smallestSafeFix: In research-stream/src/index.ts, change hasConsent() to also check research_optin === true, OR update consent screen copy to explicitly disclose structured behavioral telemetry under the necessary toggle.
mergedFindings.riskOfFixing: Low. Change is local to research-stream. If gating on research_optin, retention/funnel analytics will be blank for users who decline — acceptable for alpha.
mergedFindings.testsToAdd: Test: research stream with research_optin=false, calls track() → assert no fetch fired. research_optin=true → assert fetch fired.
